title: Preflight Checks

content:
Accelerator Requests Pod admission webhooks validate accelerator requests and compute quota units at creation for every Pod carrying kueue.x-k8s.io/queue-name. Unlabeled Pods bypass these checks and credit folds. See Pool troubleshooting to inspect pool capacity and Pending workloads.
Contents Accelerator resource families Request rules RDMA resource requests Legacy request migration Limitations Pool troubleshooting Accelerator resource families GPUStack separates software slicing and hardware partitioning into disjoint resource families:
Family Mechanism Isolation Example Logical slicing (.sliced*) Software sharing of an unpartitioned card Vendor runtime or preload shim caps VRAM and compute (Isolation mode selection ) 50% of an NVIDIA A10G Physical partitioning (.partitioned*) Hardware instance on a MIG-enabled card Hardware partition materialized by Device Manager NVIDIA mig-3g.40gb, T-Head mig-4g.48gb, Hygon mig-2g.15gb A partitioned card advertises only .partitioned* keys; an unpartitioned card advertises only <base>, .shared, and .sliced* keys. Those populations map to the four InstanceType views (EX, SH, SL, and PT).
Resource keys <base> is the vendor extended resource (nvidia.com/gpu, huawei.com/npu, amd.com/gpu, and others in Accelerator Support ):
Key Provider Eligible cards Request value Node capacity <base> Device plugin (Exclusive) Unpartitioned Whole card count Healthy tokens <base>.shared Device plugin (Shared) Unpartitioned Distinct cards on one Node (1 of 10 shares per card) Healthy tokens <base>.sliced Device plugin (Sliced) Logically sliceable Always 1 Healthy tokens <base>.sliced.units Node capacity Logically sliceable Webhook-derived (never set manually) Cards × 1,600,000 <base>.sliced.cores-percentage Node capacity Logically sliceable (0, 100] (defaults to 100) Sum of card budgets <base>.sliced.memory-percentage Node capacity Logically sliceable (0, 100] Sum of card budgets <base>.sliced.memory-mib Node capacity Logically sliceable Positive MiB <= card VRAM Sum of card budgets <base>.partitioned Device plugin (Partitioned) Partitioned Always 1 Healthy tokens <base>.partitioned.units Node capacity Partitioned Webhook-derived (never set manually) Cards × 1,600,000 <base>.partitioned.<kind>-<profile> Node capacity Partitioned Always 1 allocated + remaining device.gpustack.ai/<manufacturer>.visibility Device plugin (Visibility) Any card Workload container’s card count Healthy tokens Webhook-owned .units keys: The Pod webhook overwrites .units from slice memory or partition VRAM to charge Kueue credits.gpustack.ai/<manufacturer>. Token binding: <base>, .shared, and .sliced tokens bind specific cards in kubelet, while .partitioned and .visibility tokens are fungible counts resolved by Device Manager at Allocate. Pod request examples Submit Pods on a pool’s namespace LocalQueue (ENTRANCE on kubectl get instancetypes).
Exclusive (two whole cards):
yamlCopy apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: name: exclusive-pod labels: kueue.x-k8s.io/queue-name: <local-queue> spec: containers: - name: main image: ubuntu:24.04 command: - sleep - "3600" resources: limits: nvidia.com/gpu: "2" Shared (one unisolated 1/10 share on each of two distinct cards on one Node; for >= 2 cards, the webhook injects acceleratable.feature.gpustack.ai/<group>.count Gt N-1):
yamlCopy apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: name: shared-pod labels: kueue.x-k8s.io/queue-name: <local-queue> spec: containers: - name: main image: ubuntu:24.04 command: - sleep - "3600" resources: limits: nvidia.com/gpu.shared: "2" Logical slice (50% VRAM and 40% compute on one card):
yamlCopy apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: name: sliced-pod labels: kueue.x-k8s.io/queue-name: <local-queue> spec: containers: - name: main image: ubuntu:24.04 command: - sleep - "3600" resources: limits: nvidia.com/gpu.sliced: "1" # always "1" nvidia.com/gpu.sliced.memory-percentage: "50" # or .sliced.memory-mib, never both nvidia.com/gpu.sliced.cores-percentage: "40" # optional, default: "100" Physical partition (one 3g.40gb MIG instance):
yamlCopy apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: name: partitioned-pod labels: kueue.x-k8s.io/queue-name: <local-queue> spec: containers: - name: main image: ubuntu:24.04 command: - sleep - "3600" resources: limits: nvidia.com/gpu.partitioned: "1" # always "1" nvidia.com/gpu.partitioned.mig-3g.40gb: "1" # always "1" SSH visibility sidecar (sits outside the four families to share main’s device grant):
yamlCopy apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: name: ssh-sidecar spec: containers: - name: sshd image: gpustack/ssh-server:v1.4.0 resources: limits: device.gpustack.ai/nvidia.visibility: "1" Instance API requests An Instance declares whole cards, one logical slice, or one hardware partition in spec.resources (GPU Instance Configuration ):
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: Instance metadata: name: partitioned-instance namespace: team-a spec: type: gpustack--nvidia-h100-80gb-hbm3-linux-amd64 image: ubuntu:24.04 command: - sleep - infinity resources: accelerator: "1" # integer whole cards, or "1" for sliced/partitioned requests # acceleratorSlicedMemoryPercentage: 50 # acceleratorSlicedCoresPercentage: 50 acceleratorPartitionedProfile: 3g.40gb # mutually exclusive with slice percentages volume: ephemeral: capacity: 10Gi Admission rejects unknown partition profiles (listing offered profiles), partitioning on unsupported vendors or unpartitioned pools, slice percentages on pools without logical slicing, non-1 card counts on slice/partition requests, and whole-card counts exceeding status.accelerator.capacity. Host CPU and RAM scale by card count or slice/partition VRAM share.
Preferred accelerator placement Steer kubelet’s intra-node device selection to specific cards by setting a Pod annotation for whole, shared, or logical-slice requests:
yamlCopy apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: name: preferred-card-pod labels: kueue.x-k8s.io/queue-name: <local-queue-name> # required; selects the pool LocalQueue and Pod webhook annotations: device.gpustack.ai/accelerator.preferred-index: "3,1" # comma-separated Devices index order # device.gpustack.ai/accelerator.preferred-id: "GPU-...,GPU-..." # takes precedence over preferred-index spec: nodeSelector: # optional; annotations select cards inside one node, so constrain the node separately kubernetes.io/hostname: gpu-node-0 containers: - name: main image: ubuntu:24.04 resources: limits: nvidia.com/gpu: "2" Annotation precedence: Presence of device.gpustack.ai/accelerator.preferred-id (even when empty) overrides device.gpustack.ai/accelerator.preferred-index. Value matching: Match comma-separated IDs or indices against the node’s Devices.spec.groups[].accelerators[] (id or index); whitespace and duplicates are ignored. Advisory intra-node hint: Applies only inside the scheduled Node via GetPreferredAllocation; unavailable, cross-node, or insufficient cards fall back to other node cards. For logical slices, if every card lacks the requested units, a fallback hint can still be returned and Allocate rejects overcommitment. Selection order: Over-specified lists take the highest-priority available cards up to the request size, returned in ascending hardware order. Unsupported modes: Hardware partitioning (Partitioned / MIG) and SSH visibility sidecars ignore preferred-card annotations. Pod scope: Both annotations apply at Pod scope across all containers requesting accelerators. Request rules Admission groups containers by lifetime: standard spec.initContainers (without restartPolicy: Always), spec.containers, and native sidecars (spec.initContainers with restartPolicy: Always). Include full container image and queue-name labels when applying.
Rule 1: Family and container group All accelerator requests in a Pod must use one family and sit in one container group (either init containers or app containers, never both, because kubelet holds init devices for the Pod’s life while the scheduler charges max(init, app)):
yamlCopy apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: name: mixed-family-pod spec: containers: - name: a image: ubuntu:24.04 resources: limits: nvidia.com/gpu: "1" - name: b image: ubuntu:24.04 resources: limits: nvidia.com/gpu.sliced: "1" nvidia.com/gpu.sliced.memory-percentage: "50" spec: Forbidden: a Pod may request only one accelerator family, found [exclusive sliced]
Rule 2: Logical slice count A logical slice request must set <base>.sliced to "1" and specify exactly one of .sliced.memory-percentage ((0, 100]) or .sliced.memory-mib ((0, card VRAM]). Use multiple Pods or whole cards for multi-GPU workloads:
yamlCopy apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: name: invalid-slice-count spec: containers: - name: main image: ubuntu:24.04 resources: limits: nvidia.com/gpu.sliced: "2" nvidia.com/gpu.sliced.memory-percentage: "50" spec.containers[0].resources.limits[nvidia.com/gpu.sliced]: Invalid value: "2": a logical slice request is always a single accelerator; multi-accelerator logical slicing is not supported yet
Rule 3: Partition count A partition request must set <base>.partitioned to "1" and name a .partitioned.<kind>-<profile> key:
yamlCopy apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: name: invalid-partition-count spec: containers: - name: main image: ubuntu:24.04 resources: limits: nvidia.com/gpu.partitioned: "2" nvidia.com/gpu.partitioned.mig-1g.10gb: "1" spec.containers[0].resources.limits[nvidia.com/gpu.partitioned]: Invalid value: "2": a partition request is always a single accelerator; request one Pod per instance
Rule 4: Partition profile A Pod may request only one partition profile across all containers:
yamlCopy apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: name: invalid-partition-profiles spec: containers: - name: main image: ubuntu:24.04 resources: limits: nvidia.com/gpu.partitioned: "1" nvidia.com/gpu.partitioned.mig-1g.10gb: "1" nvidia.com/gpu.partitioned.mig-3g.40gb: "1" spec: Forbidden: a Pod may request only one partition profile, found [1g.10gb 3g.40gb]
Rule 5: Profile instance count Each .partitioned.<kind>-<profile> key must equal "1":
yamlCopy apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: name: invalid-profile-count spec: containers: - name: main image: ubuntu:24.04 resources: limits: nvidia.com/gpu.partitioned: "1" nvidia.com/gpu.partitioned.mig-3g.40gb: "2" spec.containers[0].resources.limits[nvidia.com/gpu.partitioned.mig-3g.40gb]: Invalid value: "2": a partition profile request must be exactly 1 instance
Rule 6: Slicing container count At most one container per Pod may request .sliced* or .partitioned* keys (.visibility sidecars are exempt):
yamlCopy apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: name: multi-sliced-pod spec: containers: - name: a image: ubuntu:24.04 resources: limits: nvidia.com/gpu.sliced: "1" nvidia.com/gpu.sliced.memory-percentage: "50" - name: b image: ubuntu:24.04 resources: limits: nvidia.com/gpu.sliced: "1" nvidia.com/gpu.sliced.memory-percentage: "50" spec: Forbidden: at most one container may request a slicing family, found 2
Rule 7: Native sidecar requests Restartable init containers (restartPolicy: Always) must not request accelerators because they overlap both later init containers and app containers:
yamlCopy apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: name: rejected-sidecar-pod spec: initContainers: - name: log-shipper image: ubuntu:24.04 restartPolicy: Always resources: limits: nvidia.com/gpu: "1" containers: - name: main image: ubuntu:24.04 spec.initContainers[0].resources.limits: Forbidden: a restartable init container (a native sidecar) may not request an accelerator; move the request to an app container
RDMA resource requests Node-level RDMA keys (device.gpustack.ai/rdma, rdma.shared at 64 tokens/endpoint, and rdma.partitioned for SR-IOV VFs) sit outside accelerator families, carry no .units keys, and are unmetered by Kueue (RDMA Operations and NIC record inspection ):
yamlCopy apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: name: shared-rdma-pod labels: kueue.x-k8s.io/queue-name: <local-queue> spec: containers: - name: main image: ubuntu:24.04 resources: limits: nvidia.com/gpu.shared: "1" device.gpustack.ai/rdma.shared: "1" NUMA alignment conditions Kubelet aligns an accelerator and an RDMA interface onto the same NUMA node only when all four conditions hold:
Same container: Both resource requests sit in the same container (topologyManagerScope: container). NUMA hints present: Whole, shared, and logical-slice accelerator tokens publish NUMA hints; fungible .partitioned tokens publish none. Enforcing kubelet policy: The Node runs restricted or single-numa-node (Enabling NUMA alignment and Result format ). Node-level capacity fit: Kube-scheduler sees only node totals; if a Node’s free GPU and HCA sit on different sockets, kubelet rejects the Pod without rescheduling. Legacy request migration Legacy .sliced.mig-* keys removed: Replace legacy <base>.sliced.mig-<profile> requests with <base>.partitioned: "1" and <base>.partitioned.mig-<profile>: "1". Remove stale capacity entries on development Nodes (/ escaped as ~1):
bashCopy kubectl get node <node> -o json | jq -r '.status.capacity | keys[] | select(contains("mig-"))' kubectl patch node <node> --subresource=status --type=json \ -p '[{"op":"remove","path":"/status/capacity/<escaped-key>"}]' Per-container allocation annotation: device.gpustack.ai/accelerator.allocated uses a per-container map; drain accelerator Pods before upgrading Device Manager from legacy flat builds.
.shared: N counts distinct cards: InstanceType SH onceMaxRequest now counts cards with a free share (1/10 on one free card instead of legacy 10/10).
Limitations Excluded MIG variants: Profiles containing + (+me, +me.all, +gfx) are omitted because Kubernetes resource names forbid +. Pool-wide whole-card cap: Whole-card requests above a single Node’s card count but within pool status.accelerator.capacity are admitted and remain queued. No manual nvidia-smi mig -cgi carving: Hand-carved instances lack Pod annotations, skewing node capacity until reclaimed when idle. Manual MIG mode toggle: Switching hardware partitioning mode requires draining workloads, running the vendor tool, and restarting the Device Manager DaemonSet (NVIDIA , T-Head , Hygon ). Shared card-count pin gaps: Unqueued .shared Pods on too few cards fail with UnexpectedAdmissionError, and template-derived Job / JobSet / RayJob Workloads or mixed partitioned Nodes are not narrowed by the Pod webhook’s .count affinity. Partition NUMA alignment: Under single-numa-node, CPU/memory may lock to one socket while the only free MIG slot sits on another socket. Pool troubleshooting Isolation mode selection bashCopy kubectl get instancetypes -o wide kubectl get devices <node> -o jsonpath='{.spec.groups[*].accelerators[*].status}' Mode Request key Expected signal Next action Exclusive <base> Non-zero EX on InstanceType Request integer cards on unpartitioned Nodes. Shared <base>.shared Non-zero SH (10 shares/card) Request N distinct cards on one Node (no VRAM cap). Logical slice <base>.sliced Non-zero SL; logicalSliced in Devices Set .sliced: "1" and one memory budget. Physical partition <base>.partitioned.<kind>-<profile> Non-zero PT; PARTITIONS in -o wide Set .partitioned: "1" and .partitioned.<kind>-<profile>: "1". Logical slicing mechanism and slice limits per manufacturer:
Manufacturer Enforcer Compute overcommit Max slices NVIDIA, Iluvatar HAMi-core libvgpu.so Yes 128 (100 Iluvatar) AMD libvrocm.so + HSA_CU_MASK Yes 128 T-Head hggc_quota.so + hgml_dlsym_hook.so Yes 128 Ascend vcann-rt libvruntime.so Yes 63 Cambricon cnDev sMLU profile No 16 MetaX sysfs sgpu subdevice No 16 MThreads Host sGPU kmod No 16 Hygon Host DTK vdev.conf No 4 Inspecting pools and quota bashCopy kubectl get instancetypes kubectl -n <namespace> get localqueues kubectl get clusterqueue <cluster-queue> -o yaml kubectl get resourceflavors -l resource.gpustack.ai/type=nodes Confirm InstanceType PHASE is Active, ENTRANCE exists in your namespace, and ClusterQueue has spec.stopPolicy: None, gpustack-node-devices in admissionChecksStrategy, and credits.gpustack.ai/<manufacturer> (1,600,000 per card) in resourceGroups. If ClusterQueue is on Hold (empty-plan-hold or spec.inactive: true), verify ResourceFlavors and gpustack.ai/managed=true Node labels.
Diagnosing Pending workloads Stage Command Expected signal Next action Webhook refusal kubectl apply or kubectl -n <ns> get events Forbidden, Invalid value, or Required value (no Pod created) Fix manifest against Request rules or offered pool profiles. Queued demand kubectl -n <ns> describe workload <name> Pod gated by kueue.x-k8s.io/admission; QuotaReserved=False Wait for quota, add Nodes, or reduce requested resources. Card fragmentation (affinity) kubectl -n <ns> describe workload <name> excluded: affinity despite free aggregate pool credits Wait for a contiguous card or request a smaller slice. Card fragmentation (check / kubelet) kubectl -n <ns> get workload <name> -o jsonpath='{.status.admissionChecks}' gpustack-node-devices in Retry, or Pod Failed (UnexpectedAdmissionError) Inspect Devices remaining / allocatedSlices and fit.gpustack.ai labels below; delete failed unqueued Pods. bashCopy kubectl get devices <node> -o yaml kubectl get node <node> -o json | jq '.metadata.labels | with_entries(select(.key | contains("fit.gpustack.ai")))' See also — NVIDIA MIG Operations (per-GPU MIG setup and capacity accounting) · Hygon MIG Operations (node-wide MIG on Hygon DCUs) · T-Head MIG Operations (MIG partitioning on T-Head PPUs) · Preflight Checks (bare-host detection and slicing verification) · RDMA Operations (RDMA endpoint pairing and NUMA alignment)
Next → Heterogeneous Devices Walkthrough — trace queued accelerator requests on a live cluster.
title: Accelerator Requests

content:
T-Head MIG Operations Administrators toggle T-Head PPU partitioning mode per card with ppu-smi and restart the Device Manager DaemonSet to re-detect. Once enabled, GPUStack dynamically creates and destroys GPU and Compute Instance pairs for scheduled workloads under alibabacloud.com/ppu.partitioned.mig-<profile> (Accelerator Requests ).
Contents Prerequisites Partition profile discovery Partition requests Operations Limitations Prerequisites Stop all accelerator Pods and the Device Manager Pod on the Node before toggling MIG mode. Any process opening the alixpu driver holds descriptors across all PPUs on the host (the worker Pod also opens PPU nodes briefly at startup), causing ppu-smi to fail with MIG resources are in use while dmesg logs [alixpu] PPU00<N> contains <k> active process (PPU00<N> is the card ordinal <N>).
Verify zero open alixpu file descriptors before switching (no device reset is required once holders exit):
bashCopy for p in /proc/[0-9]*; do pid=${p#/proc/}; n=$(ls -l "$p"/fd 2>/dev/null | grep -c alixpu); \ [ "$n" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null && echo "pid=$pid fds=$n $(tr -d '\0' < "$p"/cmdline)"; done Restart gpustack-operator-device-manager-thead after every mode change so Devices updates.
Partition profile discovery Device Manager queries profiles and static legal placements from hgml (excluding nameless, invalid-segment, subdivided, or placement-less profiles):
bashCopy ppu-smi mig -i <N> -lgip # profiles, memory, and live Instances Free/Total ppu-smi mig -i <N> -lgipp # static legal {Start,...}:Size placements (unchanged by occupancy) Normalized profile names: T-Head display names omit the dot separator (MIG 4g48gb, MIG 8g96gb). GPUStack normalizes two-number display names to match NVIDIA’s spelling in Kubernetes keys and InstanceType inventories (alibabacloud.com/ppu.partitioned.mig-4g.48gb and mig-8g.96gb), while ppu-smi and raw Devices records keep 4g48gb.
Partition requests Request alibabacloud.com/ppu.partitioned: "1" and alibabacloud.com/ppu.partitioned.mig-<profile>: "1" on a Kueue-labeled Pod, or set acceleratorPartitionedProfile on an Instance:
yamlCopy apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: name: thead-partition namespace: team-a labels: kueue.x-k8s.io/queue-name: <local-queue> spec: containers: - name: main image: ubuntu:24.04 command: - sleep - "86400" resources: limits: alibabacloud.com/ppu.partitioned: "1" alibabacloud.com/ppu.partitioned.mig-4g.48gb: "1" --- apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: Instance metadata: name: thead-instance namespace: team-a spec: type: <thead-instance-type> image: ubuntu:24.04 command: - sleep - "86400" resources: accelerator: "1" acceleratorPartitionedProfile: 4g.48gb volume: ephemeral: capacity: 1Gi Device-node injection: T-Head uses no environment variable hook; allocation injects the two shared control nodes, /dev/alixpu_ppu<ordinal> (built from the card ordinal, never the driver minor number ordinal + 1 which points to the next PPU), and /dev/alixpu-caps/alixpu-cap<minor> read live from /proc/driver/alixpu/capabilities/ppu<N>/mig/gi<G>{,/ci<C>}/access. Packing, SSH visibility, and reclaim: Follow the same fungible-token, sidecar-isolation, and reclaim rules as NVIDIA MIG Operations . Operations Enabling partitioning Consult T-Head’s PPU MIG documentation :
Satisfy Prerequisites (zero alixpu file-descriptor holders).
Enable MIG mode one PPU ordinal at a time using top-level -mig 1 (ppu-smi mig rejects -mig, and comma-separated -i lists fail with No devices were found):
bashCopy ppu-smi -i <N> -mig 1 ppu-smi -q -i <N> | grep -i -A2 "MIG Mode" Captured output:
textCopy Enable MIG mode for PPU <bus-id>. All done. MIG Mode Current : Enabled Pending : Enabled Restart gpustack-operator-device-manager-thead and verify Devices publishes partition profiles (logicalSliced drops on partitioned PPUs while unpartitioned PPUs keep logical slicing).
Disabling partitioning Drain partition Pods on the PPU so instances reclaim, or destroy remaining instances manually (Compute Instance first, and always pass -gi <G> because bare -dgi destroys all instances on the PPU):
bashCopy ppu-smi mig -i <N> -gi <G> -ci <C> -dci ppu-smi mig -i <N> -gi <G> -dgi Stop alixpu holders (Prerequisites ), run ppu-smi -i <N> -mig 0, and restart gpustack-operator-device-manager-thead.
Note: Leftover /dev/alixpu-caps/alixpu-cap<minor> device nodes are normal driver behavior after destroy; check live instances with ppu-smi mig -i <N> -lgi.
Node reboot recovery After a host reboot, re-verify and re-run Enabling partitioning , restart gpustack-operator-device-manager-thead, and delete/recreate pre-reboot partition Pods.
Limitations GPUStack creates and reclaims single-CI partition instances per Pod and cleans idle untracked instances. It never runs ppu-smi -mig, evicts Pods on mode switches, or serves subdivided instances.
Manual mode lifecycle and no out-of-band carving: Administrators own ppu-smi -mig switches; hand-carved instances skew node accounting and are reclaimed when idle, while hand-subdivided instances block node-wide reclaim. Single partition per PPU request: Request one Pod per partition (Rule 3 ), and leave a brief gap when replacing a deleted Pod to avoid the reclaim-debounce window. See also — NVIDIA MIG Operations (sibling MIG runbook and capacity math) · Hygon MIG Operations (node-wide MIG on Hygon DCUs) · Accelerator Requests (resource keys and request rules)
Next → Accelerator Requests — review the full accelerator request contract.
title: T-Head MIG Operations

content:
GPU Instances An Instance runs an interactive container workspace in a Kubernetes Pod on whole, sliced, or partitioned accelerators, or on CPU-only capacity. When you attach an InstanceSSHPublicKey, the operator adds an SSH sidecar that enters the workload container.
Contents Overview Configuration Operations Troubleshooting Overview InstanceType defines pool capacity and unit sizing, and Instance declares the workspace image, ports, and volumes. The worker reconciles the backing Pod through Kueue admission and maintains an optional NodePort Service.
Configuration Pool selection List available InstanceTypes (instype) and read-only InstanceTypeFlavors (instypeflavor) before creating a workspace:
bashCopy kubectl get instancetypes -o wide kubectl get instancetypeflavors Each InstanceType fronts one canonical pool ClusterQueue and reports onceMaxRequest/remaining across four accelerator views (EX whole cards, SH shared 10-slot cards, SL logical VRAM percentages, and PT hardware partitions). With -o wide, PARTITIONS lists remaining counts per MIG profile, and CPU reports capacity for CPU-only types.
With instance-type-derived-from-node enabled (default true), the operator creates one derived InstanceType per hardware pool (gpustack--<group>-<os>-<arch>). By default, accelerated nodes also contribute to the generic CPU pool (instance-type-mixed-on-node: true), and pools collapse CPU vendors (instance-type-aware-cpu-manufacturer: false).
Instance resource defaults Derived InstanceTypes stamp spec.unitResources (cpu, ram) per whole accelerator from hardware presets, plus a fixed 100Gi spec.localStorage. Unlisted accelerators fall back to 4 CPU and 16Gi RAM, and CPU-only derived types use 1 CPU and 2Gi RAM.
Default and cap: Omitted cpu or ram defaults from unitResources (scaled by card count or VRAM share) and caps explicit requests. Storage default: Omitted resources.localStorage defaults to 15Gi, capped at the InstanceType’s spec.localStorage. Overcommit: With instance-general-resources-overcommit true (default), limits keep the sized value while requests scale per unit: 100m CPU per rounded-up core on acceleratable types (800m per core on CPU-only types, capped at the limit — for example, a 4-core CPU-only limit requests 3200m), 128Mi RAM per GiB, and one-eighth localStorage. Disabling overcommit: Setting instance-general-resources-overcommit to false sets container requests equal to limits. Upgrade immutability: spec.unitResources and spec.localStorage freeze at creation; derived InstanceTypes are create-only and retain existing values across upgrades. Pool resizing: Author a custom sibling InstanceType to keep running Instances alive. Deleting a derived type persists spec.stop: true on its Instances so they remain Stopped even after the type is recreated; once the replacement type is Active, restart each workspace using Start workspace . Operations Step 1: Create workspace Select an Active InstanceType with free capacity, save this manifest as instance.yaml, and apply it in a non-reserved workload namespace:
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: Instance # namespaced, short name inst metadata: name: workspace-demo namespace: team-a spec: type: gpustack--nvidia-a10g-linux-amd64 # required; Active InstanceType name image: ubuntu:24.04 # required command: - sleep - infinity resources: accelerator: "1" # optional, default: "1" on acceleratable types ports: - name: http port: 8080 # allocates one NodePort on the Instance Service volume: # required; permanently immutable ephemeral: capacity: 1Gi bashCopy kubectl apply -f instance.yaml Step 2: Verify workspace Wait for the Instance phase to reach Ready and inspect its assigned access address and ports:
bashCopy kubectl -n team-a wait --for=jsonpath='{.status.phase}'=Ready instance/workspace-demo --timeout=5m kubectl -n team-a get instance workspace-demo Verification: PHASE reports Ready, ACCESS shows the host address, and PORT(S) lists 8080:<nodePort>/TCP. Configure SSH login, persistent storage, or node pinning in GPU Instance Configuration .
Troubleshooting If an Instance stays in Starting, read its phase message:
bashCopy kubectl -n team-a get instance workspace-demo -o jsonpath='{.status.phaseMessage}{"\n"}' See GPU Instance Operations for admission refusals, volume waits, and subresource checks, or Heterogeneous Devices Walkthrough for Kueue Workload diagnosis.
See also — GPU Instance Configuration (SSH keys, volumes, node pinning, and custom types) · GPU Instance Operations (stop/start lifecycle, isolation, logs, events, and metrics) · Heterogeneous Devices (accelerator pools and slicing)
Next → GPU Instance Configuration — configure resources, SSH access, and workspace volumes.
title: GPU Instances

content:
GPU Instance Configuration An Instance combines compute sizing from an InstanceType with container settings, optional node pinning, SSH or registry credentials, and workspace or model volumes.
Contents Resource requests Node pinning SSH access Private registries Workspace and persistent volumes Additional volumes Custom InstanceType Resource requests Configure whole accelerators, a logical slice, or a hardware partition in spec.resources. See Accelerator Requests for per-mode validation rules.
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: Instance metadata: name: sliced-workspace namespace: team-a spec: type: gpustack--nvidia-a10g-linux-amd64 # required; immutable while running image: ubuntu:24.04 # required; immutable while running imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent # optional, default: IfNotPresent; enum: Always, IfNotPresent, Never command: - sleep - infinity privileged: false # optional, default: false; gated by instance-privileged-allowed env: - name: WORKSPACE_ENV value: dev ports: - name: http port: 8080 protocol: TCP # optional, default: TCP; enum: TCP, UDP, SCTP resources: accelerator: "1" # must be "1" for sliced or partitioned requests acceleratorSlicedMemoryPercentage: 50 # optional, 0..100; copies to cores if cores omitted acceleratorSlicedCoresPercentage: 50 # optional, 0..100; copies to memory if memory omitted # acceleratorPartitionedProfile: 3g.40gb # optional; mutually exclusive with slice percentages # cpu: "4" # optional; capped by unitResources.cpu * unit share # ram: 32Gi # optional; capped by unitResources.ram * unit share localStorage: 20Gi # optional, default: 15Gi; capped by InstanceType spec.localStorage volumeMount: /workspace # optional, default: /workspace volume: # required; permanently immutable ephemeral: capacity: 10Gi Running immutability: spec.volume is permanently frozen. All other template fields, nodeName, and additionalVolumes freeze while running and become editable when spec.stop: true (Workspace stop and restart ). Privileged gate: Requesting spec.privileged: true requires the instance-privileged-allowed Setting (false by default). Already-privileged Instances stay editable if the Setting is disabled later. Node pinning Set spec.nodeName to pin an Instance to one Kubernetes Node while keeping Kueue quota and scheduler checks active:
diffCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: Instance metadata: name: sliced-workspace namespace: team-a spec: type: gpustack--nvidia-a10g-linux-amd64 + nodeName: gpu-node-01 # optional; max 253 chars, editable while stopped The controller renders spec.nodeName as nodeSelector["kubernetes.io/hostname"] on the backing Pod (using the Node’s hostname label), never as pod.spec.nodeName. status.nodeName reports where the Pod runs.
Admission checks only that the named Node exists on CREATE (including when spec.stop: true). Pinning a Node outside the InstanceType pool, or starting an Instance whose pinned Node was later removed, is admitted and leaves the Pod Pending.
SSH access Create an InstanceSSHPublicKey in the Instance namespace and reference it in spec.sshPublicKey. Each InstanceSSHPublicKey maps to a same-named Secret storing authorized_keys.
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: InstanceSSHPublicKey metadata: name: workspace-key namespace: team-a spec: displayName: Team A key # optional; max 64 chars data: ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIExamplePublicKey user@host # SSH public key line --- apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: Instance metadata: name: ssh-workspace namespace: team-a spec: type: gpustack--nvidia-a10g-linux-amd64 image: ubuntu:24.04 command: - tail - -f - /dev/null sshPublicKey: name: workspace-key # mounts authorized_keys and adds sshd sidecar resources: accelerator: "1" acceleratorSlicedMemoryPercentage: 20 acceleratorSlicedCoresPercentage: 100 volume: ephemeral: capacity: 1Gi When spec.sshPublicKey is set, the operator adds an sshd sidecar (instance-ssh-server-image Setting) that enters main’s namespaces. On accelerated workspaces, sshd requests device.gpustack.ai/<manufacturer>.visibility matching main’s card count so the device plugin grants narrow cgroup access to main’s allocated device or partition without extra quota (Pod request examples ).
Once PHASE is Ready, forward port 22 and connect as root:
bashCopy kubectl -n team-a wait --for=jsonpath='{.status.phase}'=Ready instance/ssh-workspace --timeout=5m kubectl -n team-a port-forward pod/ssh-workspace 2222:22 bashCopy ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 -p 2222 root@127.0.0.1 To expose SSH without port-forwarding, add port: 22 under spec.ports and connect to the host address in status.accessAddresses (instance-access-static-address or instance-access-wildcard-dns Settings) on the allocated NodePort in status.ports.
Private registries Create an InstanceImagePullSecret in the same namespace and reference it from spec.imagePullSecret. It maps to a same-named kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson Secret.
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: InstanceImagePullSecret metadata: name: registry-creds namespace: team-a spec: registry: registry.example.com # required on create/update; write-only username: robot-team-a # required on create/update; write-only password: <registry-token> # required on create/update; write-only email: ops@example.com # optional; write-only Set spec.imagePullSecret.name: registry-creds on the Instance. Credential fields are write-only and must be supplied together on every create or update.
Workspace and persistent volumes spec.volume mounts at spec.volumeMount (default /workspace) and accepts either ephemeral (EmptyDir capped at capacity) or persistent (an InstancePersistentVolume in the same namespace). Both cannot be set together.
An InstancePersistentVolume maps to a same-named PersistentVolumeClaim backed either by an existing Kubernetes StorageClass or by a cluster-scoped InstancePersistentVolumeType (which creates a StorageClass for NFS or S3):
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: InstancePersistentVolumeType # cluster-scoped; creates a StorageClass metadata: name: shared-nfs spec: nfs: # set exactly one of nfs or s3 server: 10.0.0.25 # required; immutable share: /exports/workspaces # required, default: /; immutable subDirectory: ${pvc.metadata.namespace}/${pvc.metadata.name} # optional; immutable mountPermissions: "0755" # optional octal string # s3: # endpoint: https://s3.example.com # required http or https URL # region: us-east-1 # optional; required for AWS # accessKey: <access-key> # write-only # secretKey: <secret-key> # write-only # bucket: team-workspaces # optional; immutable # prefix: ${pvc.metadata.namespace}/${pvc.metadata.name} # optional; immutable # mounter: geesefs # optional, default: geesefs; enum: geesefs, rclone, s3fs; immutable --- apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: InstancePersistentVolume # namespaced; creates a PVC metadata: name: team-a-home namespace: team-a spec: type: shared-nfs # StorageClass name; required only when no default StorageClass exists; immutable capacity: 50Gi # optional, default: 20Gi; immutable accessMode: ReadWriteMany # optional; enum: ReadWriteOnce, ReadWriteMany, ReadOnlyMany, ReadWriteOncePod Reference the volume on Instance with spec.volume.persistent.name: team-a-home. With instance-persistent-volume-placement true (default), the controller injects bound PV node affinity into the Instance Pod at creation and waits in Starting while an immediate-binding claim is unbound.
Additional volumes Use spec.additionalVolumes to mount extra volumes into the main container (also visible in SSH sessions). Each entry requires a unique canonical absolute mountPath distinct from spec.volumeMount and exactly one source:
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: Instance metadata: name: model-workspace namespace: team-a spec: type: gpustack--nvidia-a10g-linux-amd64 image: ubuntu:24.04 command: - sleep - infinity volume: ephemeral: capacity: 10Gi additionalVolumes: # optional; atomic list, editable while stopped - mountPath: /data readOnly: true # optional, default: false subPath: datasets # optional; relative path without ".." persistent: name: team-a-home # InstancePersistentVolume in this namespace - mountPath: /etc/workspace-config configMap: name: app-config # ConfigMap in this namespace (or secret.name for a Secret) - mountPath: /models/qwen model: artifactRef: name: qwen-7b # ModelArtifact in this namespace; always read-only, no subPath # - mountPath: /host-cache # hostPath: # requires instance-host-path-volume-allowed: "true" # path: /var/cache/shared # type: Directory Source Target resource Constraints persistent InstancePersistentVolume Same namespace; DNS-1123 name; respects PV node affinity. configMap / secret ConfigMap / Secret Same namespace; DNS-1123 name; missing objects surface on Pod events. model ModelArtifact Always read-only; subPath forbidden; mounts PVC directly, hub via model.csi.gpustack.ai, or OCI image via kubelet >= 1.35 and containerd >= 2.1 (Model Artifact ). hostPath Node path Canonical absolute path; adding or widening a grant requires instance-host-path-volume-allowed: "true" (default false). Custom InstanceType Create a custom InstanceType when you disable instance-type-derived-from-node or want custom CPU and RAM sizing beside an existing derived pool. Inspect kubectl get instancetypeflavors to read the pool’s acceleratorGroup (or generalGroup), os, and arch:
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: InstanceType # cluster-scoped, short name instype metadata: name: a10g-highmem spec: displayName: NVIDIA A10G High RAM # optional; editable description: Custom sibling with 128Gi unit RAM # optional; editable inactive: false # optional, default: false; editable (holds new queue admissions) acceleratable: true # required; immutable acceleratorGroup: nvidia-a10g # required when acceleratable is true; immutable generalGroup: generic # optional, default: generic; immutable os: linux # required; immutable arch: amd64 # required; immutable unitResources: # required; immutable cpu: "16" # positive integer without unit suffix ("1" required when acceleratable is false) ram: 128Gi # positive integer with case-sensitive "Gi" suffix localStorage: 200Gi # required; positive integer with case-sensitive "Gi" suffix; immutable Shared pool queue: A custom sibling with the same (acceleratable, acceleratorGroup, generalGroup, os, arch) shares the pool’s canonical ClusterQueue without interrupting running Instances. CPU-only types: Set acceleratable: false, omit acceleratorGroup, and set unitResources.cpu: "1" (supply a CPU generalGroup only when instance-type-aware-cpu-manufacturer is enabled). Inactive and empty queues: A new empty queue starts on Hold until its first flavor syncs. On a populated pool, admin-driven Hold activates only when every InstanceType and AcceleratorType fronting that pool sets spec.inactive: true. Drain recovery: With instance-type-drain-when-no-flavors=true (default), a marked migration drains before emptying and restores the saved stop policy when nodes return without backfilling spec.inactive. Outside migration, an external Hold on a populated active pool clears to None, while an external HoldAndDrain backfills spec.inactive: true. The InstanceType stays intact. Deleting a sibling: Deleting one custom InstanceType persists spec.stop: true on its own Instances. With other active siblings, the shared ClusterQueue stays active; with only inactive siblings on an active, non-deleting queue outside migration, the controller sets Hold; if it was the last fronting object on the pool, the controller requests ClusterQueue deletion. See also — GPU Instances (overview and unit resource presets) · Accelerator Requests (slice and partition request rules) · Model Artifact (cached model weights for model volumes)
Next → GPU Instance Operations — stop and start workspaces, isolate tenant networks, and query subresources.
title: GPU Instance Configuration

content:
GPU Instance Operations Manage Instance stop/start transitions and NodePort persistence, configure namespace network isolation, query live utilization, logs, and events, and diagnose stuck workspaces.
Contents Workspace stop and restart Tenant network isolation Metrics subresource Log and event subresources Troubleshooting Workspace stop and restart An Instance declaring spec.ports owns a NodePort Service of the same name and publishes allocated node ports in status.ports. The Service selects the backing Pod by its app.kubernetes.io/part-of UID label, surviving both stop/start cycles and spec.type changes.
Step 1: Stop workspace Patch spec.stop to true to delete the backing Pod and release accelerator and queue quota while keeping the Service and its NodePort allocations:
diffCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: Instance metadata: name: workspace-demo namespace: team-a spec: + stop: true Wait until status.phase transitions from Stopping to Stopped. If the referenced InstanceType is deleted or its ClusterQueue enters HoldAndDrain, the controller sets spec.stop: true automatically; setting spec.inactive: true on an InstanceType (Hold) blocks new admission without stopping running Instances.
Step 2: Edit stopped workspace While status.phase is Stopped, you can edit spec.type, spec.image, spec.resources, spec.ports, spec.nodeName, or spec.additionalVolumes (spec.volume stays immutable):
diffCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: Instance metadata: name: workspace-demo namespace: team-a spec: stop: true ports: - name: http port: 8080 # keeps its existing NodePort on restart + - name: metrics + port: 9090 # allocates a new NodePort on restart Unchanged (protocol, port) entries keep their allocated NodePort on restart, removed entries drop from the Service, and clearing spec.ports deletes the Service on the next start.
Step 3: Start workspace Set spec.stop: false once status.phase is Stopped (starting from Stopping is refused at admission):
diffCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: Instance metadata: name: workspace-demo namespace: team-a spec: - stop: true + stop: false bashCopy kubectl -n team-a wait --for=jsonpath='{.status.phase}'=Ready instance/workspace-demo --timeout=5m kubectl -n team-a get instance workspace-demo Verification: PHASE returns to Ready and unchanged ports report the same NodePort numbers. Deleting the Instance deletes both the Pod and the Service.
Tenant network isolation Cross-namespace Instance isolation is opt-in. While the instance-isolation-pod-cidrs Setting (worker.instanceIsolationPodCIDRs in Helm values) is blank (default), no policy is rendered.
Find your cluster’s IPv4 pod CIDRs from your CNI IPAM (kubectl get ippools.crd.projectcalico.org on Calico) or node specs (kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[*].spec.podCIDRs}'), then set the Setting:
diffCopy apiVersion: gpustack.ai/v1 kind: Setting metadata: name: instance-isolation-pod-cidrs namespace: gpustack-system spec: - value: "" + value: 10.244.0.0/16 The worker immediately reconciles a NetworkPolicy named gpustack-instance-isolation in every non-reserved namespace, selecting Pods labeled resource.gpustack.ai/type: instances:
Allowed traffic: Ingress and egress within the same namespace, ingress and egress to 0.0.0.0/0 except the configured pod CIDRs, and egress on UDP/TCP port 53 for DNS. Namespace ownership: Deleting the last Instance in a namespace leaves the policy in place, and manual edits to operator-rendered policies are overwritten. Clearing the Setting deletes only operator-rendered policies and leaves hand-authored same-named policies untouched. Boundaries: Enforcement requires a NetworkPolicy-capable CNI (such as Calico or Cilium). Other policies selecting the same Pods can add permissions, and Kubernetes allows traffic from the hosting node (including NodePort requests via a node IP). Metrics subresource Query live CPU, memory, ephemeral storage, and per-grant accelerator utilization through the worker’s read-only metrics subresource:
bashCopy kubectl get --raw "/apis/worker.gpustack.ai/v1/namespaces/<ns>/instances/<name>/metrics" yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: InstanceMetrics metadata: name: workspace-demo namespace: team-a uid: <instance-uid> sample: timestamp: "2026-08-13T12:00:00Z" cpuTotalMilliCores: 8000 # declared container limits (init containers excluded) cpuUsedMilliCores: 500 memoryTotalMiB: 65536 memoryUsedMiB: 2048 storageTotalMiB: 15360 storageUsedMiB: 256 accelerators: # one entry per grant (device, logical slice, or partition) - id: <device-or-mig-uuid> mode: Exclusive # enum: Exclusive, Shared, Sliced, Partitioned, Visibility memoryTotalMiB: 24576 memoryUsedMiB: 4096 memoryUtilizationPercent: 17 coresUtilizationPercent: 45 temperatureCelsius: 58 powerUsageWatts: 165 unhealthy: false Required RBAC: Callers need get on instances/metrics in worker.gpustack.ai; get on instances alone is insufficient. Pre-start zero: Before any container has started (unscheduled, Stopped, or Pod absent), the endpoint returns 200 with declared totals and 0 usage. Once started, 0 means idle. Unavailable sources (503): After a container has started, if both kubelet nodes/proxy stats and metrics.k8s.io fail, the endpoint returns 503 ServiceUnavailable naming the failed source. Omitted accelerator samples: If Device Manager is unreachable, not Ready, stale (over three monitor periods), or unable to measure a process or vendor counter, CPU/memory/storage still return while accelerators or unmeasured used fields are omitted rather than 0. Each Device Manager also exposes gpustack_instance_* Prometheus gauges on HTTPS port 32443 (/metrics), omitting unmeasured used series. On multi-tenant clusters, restrict port 32443 with deviceManager.networkPolicy.enabled: true and deviceManager.networkPolicy.scrapers.
Log and event subresources Stream main container logs or list Kubernetes Events for the current backing Pod through the log and events subresources:
bashCopy kubectl get --raw "/apis/worker.gpustack.ai/v1/namespaces/<ns>/instances/<name>/log?tailLines=100&timestamps=true" kubectl get --raw "/apis/worker.gpustack.ai/v1/namespaces/<ns>/instances/<name>/events" Required RBAC: Grant get on instances/log or instances/events in worker.gpustack.ai (instancepersistentvolumes/<name>/events serves the same view for persistent volumes). Log options: instances/<name>/log accepts follow, tailLines (>= 0), limitBytes (>= 1), timestamps, and at most one of sinceSeconds (>= 1) or sinceTime (RFC3339). Troubleshooting Inspect status.phase, status.phaseMessage, and Pod events first:
bashCopy kubectl -n <ns> get instance <name> -o jsonpath='{.status.phase}: {.status.phaseMessage}{"\n"}' kubectl get --raw "/apis/worker.gpustack.ai/v1/namespaces/<ns>/instances/<name>/events" Symptom Reason Resolution Refused on create (reserved namespace or inactive) System namespace or held InstanceType Create in a workload namespace and select an Active InstanceType. Retryable error (not ready yet; retry) Slice or partition requested before InstanceType status.detail synced Wait a few seconds for InstanceType reconciliation and re-apply. Refused on update (is immutable) Edited template, ports, node pin, or volumes while running Set spec.stop: true, wait for Stopped, apply the edit, then set spec.stop: false (recreate to change spec.volume). Refused on privileged or hostPath Cluster host-access gate is false Ask an administrator to enable instance-privileged-allowed or instance-host-path-volume-allowed, or remove the field. Stuck in Starting naming a volume or runtime floor Unresolved ModelArtifact, missing CSIDriver, unbound claim, or pinned node below kubelet 1.35 / containerd 2.1 Check ModelArtifact Resolved=True, model.csi.gpustack.ai, InstancePersistentVolume binding, or pin a compatible node. Stuck in Starting or Pod Failed (UnexpectedAdmissionError) Queued behind capacity, incompatible spec.nodeName, or persistent device-plugin rejection past the 5-minute retry window Inspect the Kueue Workload, verify spec.nodeName labels, and follow scheduling troubleshooting . See also — GPU Instances (pool selection and instance resource defaults) · GPU Instance Configuration (SSH access, volumes, and custom InstanceTypes) · Heterogeneous Devices Walkthrough (queue and device scheduling diagnosis)

content:
KV Cache A shared KV cache lets compatible inference workloads reuse cached prefix blocks. A KVCacheBackend runs the store, while KVCachePool and KVCachePoolBinding grant capacity to namespaces. Cache quota is separate from accelerator quota.
Contents Overview Configuration Operations Troubleshooting Overview A KVCachePoolBinding provisions capacity and registers a reuse domain, not network access control. Review Limitations before sharing one backend across distrusting tenants.
Configuration Start with the backend manifest to deploy or attach a store, then configure pools and bindings for namespace quotas and reuse domains. Pod injection covers opt-in Pod labels, annotations, and verification.
For an end-to-end deployment sequence, follow the Shared Cache Walkthrough .
Operations Step 1: Configure storage Choose memory segments and optional local disk offload in KV Cache Backend and KV Cache Local Disk Tier (including disk and memory sizing ).
Step 2: Verify backend readiness Inspect backend readiness and conditions:
bashCopy kubectl get kvcb kubectl describe kvcb <backend-name> Verification: Confirm PHASE is Ready against Status and conditions . For leader probes and failover, see KV Cache Election and Failover .
Troubleshooting If a workload cannot attach or write to the cache, inspect the backend, pool, and binding status:
Condition Reason Resolution MembersMounted=False AmbiguousMemberIdentity Place host-network member groups on separate Nodes via nodeSelector. Engine writes fail with RPC_FAIL (-900) Store and client minor versions differ Align store and engine versions in Version compatibility . Use Refused engine launch for admission refusals, Pod binding verification to inspect admitted Pods, and Quota and deletion checks for deletion holds.
See also — Model Deployment (managed serving consumers) · RDMA Networking (fabric endpoints)
Next → Shared Cache Walkthrough — deploy and verify a shared cache.
title: KV Cache

content:
KV Cache Backend A KVCacheBackend configures shared KV cache storage for inference workloads. On a managed backend, the operator runs a metadata leader and one store member per selected Node in each member group. An external backend connects to an existing service.
Mooncake calls the leader a master, and its flags, environment variables, and metrics retain that name.
Contents Configuration Backend images Hardware requirements Status and conditions Group resizing Operations Configuration Connections and storage media spec.connection selects either operator-managed workloads or an external endpoint pair. On managed backends, members[].medium selects host memory (DRAM) or device memory (VRAM).
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: KVCacheBackend # cluster-scoped, short name kvcb metadata: name: mooncake-dram spec: type: Mooncake # required; enum: Mooncake image: docker.io/kvcacheai/mooncake:0.3.13 # optional; defaults from kv-cache-backend-image Setting connection: managed: # required: set exactly one of managed or external leader: electionBackend: None # upstream image lacks Kubernetes Lease support members: - nodeSelector: kubernetes.io/os: linux medium: DRAM # required, immutable; enum: DRAM, VRAM capacityPerMember: 4Gi # required per-node segment size Cluster scope: KVCacheBackend is cluster-scoped because it claims host memory, host paths, and fabric devices. Multiple KVCachePools can share one backend (Limitations ). Member groups: Declare one or more groups; at most one group can configure a local disk tier . Medium immutability: members[].medium cannot change in place; add a separate group to mix host and device memory. Value Meaning Constraints DRAM Host RAM segment Adds capacityPerMember + localBufferSize to Pod requests.memory and sets void device visibility. VRAM Device memory segment Accounting-only for custom USE_VRAM_SEGMENT=ON images; charges only localBufferSize and omits void hiding. Metadata discovery The metadata plane always uses peer-to-peer handshakes (P2PHANDSHAKE) and needs no external etcd or Redis service (spec.metadata does not exist). Configure leader election separately through leader.electionBackend (default Kubernetes).
Member groups Each members[] entry reconciles one OnDelete DaemonSet matching members[].nodeSelector. Two groups can select the same Node when their network identities do not collide.
spec.transport.protocol accepts Auto (default, resolving to TCP), TCP, RDMA, EFA, CANN, ROCM, MUSA, and MACA. members[].transport.protocol overrides the protocol for one group; see Engine Compatibility .
TCP: Needs no host privileges, but copies payloads through the kernel network stack. Host fabrics (RDMA, EFA): Enable hostNetwork: true, IPC_LOCK, SYS_RESOURCE, and fabric resource requests (device.gpustack.ai/rdma.shared for 1, device.gpustack.ai/rdma for > 1, or vpc.amazonaws.com/efa) sized by members[].fabricInterfaceCount (default 1). Do not mount /dev/infiniband manually. Ports: Group <i> serves HTTP on 8080 + <i> (bound on the host network when hostNetwork is active). Data transfers use ephemeral ports negotiated via P2PHANDSHAKE, so open ephemeral port ranges in firewalls and NetworkPolicy rules. Extra flags: members[].extraArgs renders as -D key=value and leader.extraArgs renders as -key=value; CXL flags are refused. Never place secrets in extraArgs. Disk offload retries: Clients writing to a local disk tier must retry when a memory segment fills ahead of asynchronous bucket eviction. External Mooncake endpoints connection.external attaches to an existing Mooncake service without creating workloads. Supply both Client and Admin endpoints as host:port:
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: KVCacheBackend metadata: name: external-mooncake spec: connection: external: endpoints: - name: Client # engine RPC endpoint address: mooncake.example:50051 - name: Admin # operator health, metrics, and tenant API endpoint address: mooncake.example:9003 Immediate error state: Unreachable external endpoints report phase: Error immediately (never Provisioning), and HTTP 3xx redirects from Admin are refused. Single-backend ownership: Never point two KVCacheBackend objects at the same external leader with overlapping domain.name bindings; ceilings will oscillate and mismatched blockSize or dtype values corrupt tensors. Backend images members[].image overrides spec.image, which falls back to the kv-cache-backend-image Setting (defaulting to the project’s -cpu build). Admission refuses create when all three are empty; clearing the Setting later does not block unrelated updates or deletion.
Set spec.imagePullSecrets and spec.imagePullPolicy on the backend to apply registry pull settings across the leader and all member groups.
GPUStack build variants GPUStack publishes mirrored-mooncake variants tagged <mooncake-version>-<variant><toolchain> (such as 0.3.13.post1-cuda13.0). All official builds set USE_VRAM_SEGMENT=OFF, allocate Host RAM (DRAM) only, and compile Kubernetes Lease high availability :
-cpu default: Bundles libibverbs and AWS libfabric for TCP, RDMA, and EFA Host-RAM stores on NVIDIA and AMD Nodes. -cann variant: Required on Ascend because vllm-ascend uses HIXL (protocol: ascend) over ACL/HIXL Host RAM. -rocm variant: Adds ROCm transport support alongside Host-RAM storage. 0.3.10.post2 variant: Supports legacy engines below the supported floor ; set leader.electionBackend: None and leader.multiTenancy: false. Version compatibility Match the store image and the engine’s embedded Mooncake client to the same minor line. The wire handshake reports 2.0.0 across 0.3.x releases, so mismatched lines (such as 0.3.12 and 0.3.13) pass probes and fail transfers with RPC_FAIL (-900). Check runner pairings in Engine Compatibility .
Direct prefill/decode (PD) transfer (MooncakeConnector without spec.kvCache) runs engine to engine and does not use a store. Leader Lease election requires Mooncake 0.3.12 or newer.
Hardware requirements Ascend vllm-ascend requires protocol: CANN and a -cann member image (USE_ASCEND_DIRECT) with medium: DRAM. Starting a -cann image on TCP or RDMA fails with cannot allocate local segment, ret: -1. Idle CANN members use zero AICore compute.
Ascend A2/A3 and A5 UB/UBG/UBoE: Omit fabricInterfaceCount. For A5 UBG or UBoE, set ASCEND_GLOBAL_RESOURCE_CONFIG in members[].extraEnv with "comm_resource_config.protocol_desc" set to ["ub_rtp:device"] or ["uboe:device"]. Ascend A5 Host RoCE (roce:host): Set fabricInterfaceCount: 1 (or higher) on protocol: CANN after preparing Ascend host prerequisites . The operator grants hostNetwork, IPC_LOCK, SYS_RESOURCE, device.gpustack.ai/rdma*, read-only /etc/hixlep, and defaulted ASCEND_LOCAL_COMM_RES="" plus ASCEND_GLOBAL_RESOURCE_CONFIG. yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: KVCacheBackend metadata: name: ascend-shared-cache spec: transport: protocol: CANN connection: managed: leader: {} # uses default replicas, allocationStrategy, and multiTenancy members: - nodeSelector: kvcache-ascend: "true" medium: DRAM image: gpustack/mirrored-mooncake:0.3.14-cann9.1-910b # match 910B, 910C, or A5 SoC capacityPerMember: 32Gi # fabricInterfaceCount: 1 # enable for Ascend A5 Host RoCE (roce:host) hostPaths: - path: /usr/local/Ascend/driver mountPath: /usr/local/Ascend/driver type: Directory readOnly: true - path: /usr/local/dcmi mountPath: /usr/local/dcmi type: Directory readOnly: true - path: /usr/local/bin/npu-smi mountPath: /usr/local/bin/npu-smi type: File readOnly: true AWS EFA Verify EFA support on the instance type with fi_info -p efa before deploying an EFA group, and never mount /dev/infiniband (partial device visibility causes No available EFA devices). Place all members and engines in one AWS cluster placement group and build an EFA-capable engine image per RDMA Operations .
Custom VRAM builds medium: VRAM is accounting-only for user-built USE_VRAM_SEGMENT=ON images. Grant user-space driver access via runtimeClassName, extraEnv, or hostPaths, and deduct capacityPerMember from the engine’s gpu_memory_utilization budget:
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: KVCacheBackend metadata: name: shared-cache spec: connection: managed: leader: {} members: - nodeSelector: kvcache-vram: "true" medium: VRAM # custom USE_VRAM_SEGMENT=ON image required image: custom-registry.example/mooncake-vram:0.3.14-cuda13.0 capacityPerMember: 8Gi extraEnv: - name: NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES value: all # requires accept-nvidia-visible-devices-envvar-when-unprivileged or runtimeClassName: nvidia Status and conditions Inspect backend phase, client endpoint, observed capacity, and conditions:
bashCopy kubectl get kvcb kubectl describe kvcb <name> Captured output:
textCopy NAME TYPE PHASE ENDPOINT CAPACITY mooncake-dram Mooncake Ready mooncake-dram-leader.gpustack-system.svc:50051 12Gi Phases are Provisioning, Ready, Degraded, Error, and Deleting. Status polls the leader every 15 s; status.capacity comes from live leader metrics once service_ready is true, never from multiplying capacityPerMember.
Condition Moves phase Meaning and action LeaderAvailable Yes Leader health check passed. If False, inspect leader Deployment Pods or external Admin reachability. MembersMounted Yes Ready member Pods match listed segments. On AmbiguousMemberIdentity, move host-network groups onto disjoint Nodes; pre-0.3.12 masters report Unknown/SegmentListingNotServed. CapacityObserved Yes Leader :9003/metrics scraped while ready. If False, check leader admin port reachability. PoolWrites Yes True after a put completes or allocator_used_bytes > 0; False if puts revoke with zero allocated bytes (retry initial writes after tenant ledger propagation). Deletable Yes False while status.usedBy names live KVCachePool or KVCachePoolBinding objects; delete those consumers first. RolloutComplete No Informational: False while an OnDelete member DaemonSet rollout is incomplete. ElectionObserved No Informational (under electionBackend: Kubernetes): confirms Lease holder observation. TierWasEmpty No Informational (when localDisks is set): records whether the disk directory started empty. Pool and binding usage fields lag leader :9003/metrics and /api/v1/tenant_quotas by one reconcile pass. For disk-tier write checks, see Bucket writes .
Group resizing Widening members[].nodeSelector adds member Pods without restarting existing ones; existing keys do not rebalance (allocationStrategy: FreeRatioFirst steers new writes toward emptier members). Editing image, argv, environment, resources, or fabric settings updates the OnDelete DaemonSet, requiring manual Pod deletion to roll each Node.
Shrinking a group or narrowing nodeSelector discards cached keys on removed Nodes. Member groups are indexed by list position:
Edit Outcome Reordering entries or deleting an entry before the tail Refused at admission Appending or removing at the end of members Allowed Editing in place (including narrowing nodeSelector to zero Nodes) Allowed To retire a middle group without shifting later indices, narrow its nodeSelector to match zero Nodes. Before shrinking a group with localDisks, set scaleIn.gracePeriodSeconds (0 to 3600, setting Pod termination grace to gracePeriodSeconds + 60) and roll the Pods so the preStop hook deregisters segments cleanly:
diffCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: KVCacheBackend metadata: name: mooncake-dram spec: connection: managed: + scaleIn: + gracePeriodSeconds: 30 # 0..3600; applies to localDisks groups Operations Benign client warning: E transfer_metadata.cpp:991] Local segment descriptor not found logs once on engine startup and is harmless. Reserved metrics env: MC_TE_METRIC=1 is rendered on every member group and refused in members[].extraEnv. Configure replica_num on the engine client, not on KVCacheBackend. Consumer holds: While status.usedBy is non-empty, deletion waits in Deleting (leaving workloads running) and disabling leader.multiTenancy is refused. See also — KV Cache Election and Failover (metadata leader, probes, and Lease election) · KV Cache Local Disk Tier (disk buckets, cleanup, and disk-heavy Nodes) · KV Cache Pools and Bindings (namespace grants and reuse domains) · Installation Modes (chart and worker CRD ownership)
Next → KV Cache Local Disk Tier — add local NVMe offload to a member group.
title: KV Cache Backend

content:
KV Cache Election and Failover Each managed KVCacheBackend runs a metadata leader (Deployment and ClusterIP Service), health probes, and optional Kubernetes Lease election. GPUStack APIs call this component the leader; Mooncake flags, environment variables, and metrics call it master.
Contents Leader configuration Election configuration Update strategy Health checks High availability Leader configuration The leader Service exposes port 50051 for engine RPCs and port 9003 for Prometheus metrics and the HTTP admin API.
Use leader.extraArgs (-key=value) and leader.extraEnv (unique name keys) to pass upstream settings that are not owned by the operator:
metrics_host (IPv6 required): Moves the admin bind address without changing port 9003. Mooncake defaults to IPv4-only 0.0.0.0, so set -metrics_host=:: on IPv6 or dual-stack clusters so kubelet probes succeed. Any concrete IP other than 0.0.0.0 or :: breaks kubelet probes. default_kv_lease_ttl (override allowed): The operator renders 5m (instead of upstream’s 10s) to protect recently read blocks from eviction across multi-turn prefix reuse. An entry in leader.extraArgs renders after the default and overrides it. Refused flags: Admission rejects port (deprecated alias of rendered rpc_port), CXL flags, enable_oplog, etcd_endpoints, rpc_address, rpc_interface, memory_allocator, and all enable_snapshot* / snapshot_* flags (restoring stale memory offsets after an engine reset returns wrong KV bytes). Identity variables rendered by the operator are also refused in leader.extraEnv. Election configuration leader.replicas defaults to 1 (max 5), and leader.electionBackend defaults to Kubernetes even at replicas: 1. Only one replica serves traffic; additional replicas stand by for failover.
Scaling without restarts: Because electionBackend: Kubernetes is already active at 1 replica, raising replicas to 3 adds standbys without restarting the active leader or rolling member Pods. (If a legacy Deployment still carries an unelected template, the controller rolls 1 elected replica first and reports RolloutComplete=False/ReplicasPending before scaling out.) Single-replica None: Set electionBackend: None only for images without Kubernetes Lease support (replicas > 1 with None is refused at admission and clamped to 1). Switching between None and Kubernetes changes leader and member Pod templates, restarting them and clearing DRAM segments. Update strategy At replicas: 1, the leader Deployment uses Recreate, creating a brief service gap during image or flag updates while members retain their segments and remount afterward. Above 1 replica, it uses RollingUpdate (maxSurge: 1, maxUnavailable: replicas) so standbys are already scheduled and pulled before taking the Lease.
Health checks Readiness and liveness probes target separate endpoints on port 9003:
Probe Path Gated Readiness GET /get_all_segments Yes (503 until active) Liveness GET /health No (200 on standbys and activating leaders) In the /health JSON response ({"status":"ok","role":"leader","ha_state":"serving","service_ready":true}), status is always "ok"; inspect service_ready to determine whether the leader is active.
High availability Under electionBackend: Kubernetes, replicas campaign for the Lease <backend>-leader in the operator namespace. Scale an elected leader with a replicas patch:
diffCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: KVCacheBackend metadata: name: shared-mooncake spec: connection: managed: leader: - replicas: 1 + replicas: 3 Image requirement: Upstream kvcacheai/mooncake images compile leadership backends off (leaders stay in UNAVAILABLE_IN_CURRENT_MODE and members crash with Invalid HA backend entry). Use gpustack/mirrored-mooncake (>= 0.3.12, built from pack/mirrored-mooncake ) for spec.image and every members[].image (0.3.11 exits on rendered -pod_name and -pod_namespace flags).
All official mirrored-mooncake variants (-cpu, cuda, cann, rocm, including built-in EFA via libfabric) compile the Lease backend in; custom MUSA or MACA builds must enable it themselves.1
Steady-state readiness (N desired, 1 ready): Standbys intentionally fail readiness so the leader Service routes only to the active holder (kubectl get deploy briefly shows 2 ready during handover). Identify the active leader Pod by its self-applied label:
bashCopy kubectl -n gpustack-system get pod -l mooncake.io/store-role=leader RBAC separation: The operator provisions separate ServiceAccounts, Roles, and RoleBindings in its namespace so members cannot claim the Lease:
Component Permissions Purpose Leader leases (create, get, update), pods (patch) Acquire the Lease and label the winning Pod. Member leases (get) Follow the Lease holder when memberAddressing: Lease is set. If RBAC is missing, leaders retry silently at 0/N ready (liveness stays 200), while members exit after 20 retries (CrashLoopBackOff). Verify both ServiceAccounts before debugging the store.
Member addressing: leader.memberAddressing selects how members locate the elected leader (changing it while HA is active rolls all member groups):
Value Member MOONCAKE_MASTER Trade-off Service (default) <backend>-leader.<namespace>.svc:50051 Waits for Kubernetes Endpoints propagation on failover. Lease k8s://<namespace>/<lease> Reads the Lease directly; requires member API-server reachability and a Lease-enabled image. Failover behavior: Standbys hold no metadata index. After failover (~16 s on a single-node cluster versus ~30 s for a single-leader restart), the new leader rebuilds segment mounts from members; DRAM-only keys miss until rewritten, and local disk tier keys recover once disk segments re-register (unless a restarted member’s new client ID collides with a stale replica record).
See also — KV Cache Backend (member groups, transports, and conditions) · KV Cache Local Disk Tier (offload flags derived from member disk declarations) · High Availability Operations (control-plane replica settings)
Next → KV Cache Backend — configure member storage groups and inspect backend status.
Build targets verify Lease support at build time; multi-leader failover over live RDMA, ROCM, or CANN fabrics has not been hardware-measured. ↩︎
title: KV Cache Election and Failover

content:
KV Cache Local Disk Tier At most one member group on a managed KVCacheBackend can declare a single localDisks entry to offload evicted memory blocks onto node-local storage. Declaring localDisks automatically enables deferred offload (-enable_offload=true -offload_on_evict=true) on the leader.
Contents Configuration Bucket writes Eviction Cleanup on deletion Disk and memory sizing Configuration yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: KVCacheBackend metadata: name: shared-mooncake spec: connection: managed: members: - nodeSelector: kvcache: "true" medium: DRAM # official images use DRAM; custom VRAM images see Backend guide capacityPerMember: 500Gi # must be >= 16Mi when localDisks is set localDisks: # at most one group per backend, single entry keyed by path - path: /var/lib/kvcache # required; must pre-exist on every selected Node capacity: 4Ti # optional; defaults to store ceiling (>= 16Mi when set) keyLimit: 10000000 # optional; defaults to store limit (>= 64 when set) cleanAfterDelete: false # optional, default: false eviction: # optional enabled: true # optional, default: true when eviction block is set policy: LRU # optional, default: FIFO; enum: FIFO, LRU watermark: # optional; percentages of capacity (low < high) high: 90 low: 80 Rendered setting Target MOONCAKE_OFFLOAD_ENABLED, ..._FILE_STORAGE_PATH, ..._BUCKET_SIZE_LIMIT_BYTES (16 MiB), ..._BUCKET_KEYS_LIMIT (64) Member container ..._TOTAL_SIZE_LIMIT_BYTES, ..._BUCKET_MAX_TOTAL_SIZE (from capacity), ..._TOTAL_KEYS_LIMIT (from keyLimit) Member container ..._BUCKET_EVICTION_POLICY, ..._ENABLE_DISK_WATERMARK_EVICTION, watermark ratios Member container Directory hostPath mount at localDisks[].path, preStop hook, and scaleIn.gracePeriodSeconds window Member Pod -enable_offload=true, -offload_on_evict=true (refused in leader.extraArgs) Leader argv The tier always runs in deferred mode, keeping queued objects in memory until their disk bucket flushes.
Why — Mooncake’s write-through mode (-offload_on_evict=false) can evict an object’s last in-memory replica before its offload has landed, so a failure in that window loses the object. The leader’s -enable_offload=true -offload_on_evict=true pair therefore renders together, and admission refuses both keys in leader.extraArgs.
Host directory requirements localDisks[].path mounts with hostPath.type: Directory (fsGroup does not apply to hostPath). Pre-create the directory on every selected Node, owned by the member image’s UID (65532 on official images):
bashCopy docker run --rm --entrypoint id <your-member-image> install -d -o 65532 -g 0 -m 0750 /var/lib/kvcache Path validation: Must be an absolute path without leading/trailing whitespace or .., not /, not overlapping /dev/infiniband, and (on CANN groups with fabricInterfaceCount) not overlapping /etc/hixlep. Tier immutability: Adding, removing, or repathing localDisks on an existing group is refused (capacity, keyLimit, cleanAfterDelete, and eviction remain editable). To remove a tier without deleting the whole KVCacheBackend, place the tier on the last entry in members[] so that group can be removed from the tail (Group resizing ). Symptom Signal Resolution Refused at kubectl apply Admission error on localDisks Fix the path rule violation, or avoid adding/removing/repathing localDisks in place. Member Pod stuck Pending / ContainerCreating FailedMount ... hostPath type check failed Create localDisks[].path on the Node before starting the member. Member Pod running, 0/1 Ready (MembersMounted=False) Log: FileStorageConfig: no write permission on directory chown the host directory to the member container’s UID. Bucket writes Mooncake batches offloaded objects per member and writes to disk only when a member’s bucket reaches the operator-rendered threshold of 16 MiB or 64 keys (upstream’s 256 MB / 500-key defaults leave smaller workloads unwritten; bucket env vars are owned and refused in extraEnv).
Admission enforces a one-bucket floor so no declared ceiling silently disables offload: capacityPerMember (>= 16Mi), localDisks[].capacity (>= 16Mi when set), and localDisks[].keyLimit (>= 64 when set).
Because status.capacity reports declared capacity rather than written bytes, verify actual disk writes with master_allocated_file_size_bytes on the leader:
bashCopy kubectl exec -n gpustack-system deploy/<backend>-leader -- \ python3 -c "import urllib.request;print([l for l in \ urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:9003/metrics').read().decode().splitlines() \ if l.startswith('master_allocated_file_size_bytes')])" Offered data Zero gauge meaning Below 16 MiB / 64 keys per member Expected: no member bucket has closed yet. At least one bucket per member (after ~30 s) Disk tier is not writing: inspect member logs and directory permissions. Eviction localDisks[].eviction controls full-disk behavior:
Setting Full-disk behavior Omitted Uses Mooncake’s default (FIFO eviction). enabled: true (block default) Evicts FIFO (oldest written) or LRU (least recently read) entries between watermark.high and watermark.low. enabled: false Stops accepting new disk writes while keeping existing disk entries readable. Admission rejects four no-op combinations: enabled: false with policy, enabled: false with watermark, watermark without localDisks[].capacity, and watermark.low >= watermark.high. Unmodeled Mooncake file-storage variables can be passed in members[].extraEnv (non-rendered keys only; world-readable, so never pass credentials).
Cleanup on deletion By default (cleanAfterDelete: false), deleting a KVCacheBackend leaves localDisks[].path untouched. Set cleanAfterDelete: true (requires sh in the member image, present in official builds) to empty the directory’s contents on selected Nodes during backend deletion while keeping the directory itself:
diffCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: KVCacheBackend metadata: name: shared-mooncake spec: connection: managed: members: - medium: DRAM capacityPerMember: 500Gi localDisks: - path: /var/lib/kvcache capacity: 4Ti + cleanAfterDelete: true Retained cache files Pointing a new KVCacheBackend at a non-empty directory lets Mooncake adopt leftover buckets, which can serve stale bytes on key collisions. Each backend’s initial member Pods survey the directory once at first start and write TierWasEmpty=False (with a Warning Event) if any Node had prior files, or TierWasEmpty=True once all desired Nodes report empty:
bashCopy kubectl get kvcachebackend <name> -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions[?(@.type=="TierWasEmpty")]}{"\n"}' Cleanup limitations Delete the KVCacheBackend before narrowing nodeSelector; cleanup runs only on Nodes still matched at deletion time. Cleanup does not block backend deletion indefinitely and records Node Warning Events when skipped or cut short:
Per-node 5m deadline: Unreachable Nodes (KVCacheTierNotCleaned) or large directories exceeding 5m (KVCacheTierPartlyEmptied) cancel their cleanup Pod so a new backend cannot lose fresh data. Overlapping path guard: If another live KVCacheBackend uses an identical or nested localDisks[].path, cleanup skips or stops (KVCacheTierSharedPath). bashCopy kubectl describe node <node> | grep -E 'KVCacheTierNotCleaned|KVCacheTierSharedPath|KVCacheTierPartlyEmptied' Disk and memory sizing A Node with terabytes of NVMe and limited spare RAM still requires a memory segment on the same member group. Mooncake routes offload tasks to the client holding the key’s memory replica, so a group without memory would report disk capacity while storing nothing.
Kubernetes ephemeral-storage limits do not track or evict hostPath usage. Monitor the backing filesystem yourself and set localDisks[].capacity inside the disk’s free space.
Configure one group combining a thin DRAM segment with a large localDisks[].capacity:
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: KVCacheBackend metadata: name: mooncake-disk spec: type: Mooncake connection: managed: leader: {} members: - nodeSelector: kvcache: "true" medium: DRAM # required memory segment fronting the disk tier capacityPerMember: 8Gi # sized for in-flight offload buckets plus hot reads localDisks: - path: /var/lib/kvcache capacity: 4Ti eviction: enabled: true policy: LRU Minimum memory segment Admission enforces capacityPerMember >= 16Mi (one bucket) whenever capacityPerMember is created or edited on a group with localDisks (existing smaller values are not re-judged on unrelated edits).
16Mi only prevents silent non-writes; it leaves room for one in-flight bucket and zero memory cache. Size capacityPerMember to hold concurrent in-flight offload buckets plus your hot memory working set, while keeping capacityPerMember + localBufferSize within the Node’s allocatable RAM so the member Pod schedules.
See also — KV Cache Backend (leader, member transports, and group resizing) · KV Cache Pools and Bindings (namespace grants and reuse domains)
Next → KV Cache Pools and Bindings — grant namespaces quota on this backend.
title: KV Cache Local Disk Tier

content:
KV Cache Pools and Bindings A KVCacheBackend runs the store, a cluster-scoped KVCachePool publishes its capacity, and a namespaced KVCachePoolBinding grants a namespace a byte ceiling under one reuse domain.
A Binding provisions capacity; it does not enforce network isolation. Review Limitations before sharing one backend across untrusted tenants. In GPUStack APIs, the tenant partition is called a reuse domain; Mooncake flags, metrics, and errors call it a tenant.
Contents Pools and bindings Cache reuse domains Capacity grants Pod injection Quota and deletion checks Limitations Pools and bindings KVCachePool and KVCachePoolBinding mirror ClusterQueue and LocalQueue: the cluster object owns backend capacity, and the namespaced object grants quota and RBAC scope to one namespace.
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: KVCachePool # cluster-scoped, short name kvcp metadata: name: shared-dram spec: backends: # required; single-item list naming one KVCacheBackend - mooncake-dram quota: total: 900Gi # optional pool quota target --- apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: KVCachePoolBinding # namespaced, short name kvcpb metadata: name: team-a namespace: team-a spec: poolRef: # required; immutable name: shared-dram quota: # required ceiling: 600Gi # requested ceiling; effective grant scales proportionally on oversubscription domain: # required; all fields are immutable name: qwen-72b-v2 # optional, default: "default" blockSize: 64 # required dtype: fp8_e4m3 # required; "auto" refused on new Bindings Cache reuse domains Each KVCachePoolBinding registers one reuse domain on its backend’s leader:
Default name: Omitting spec.domain.name registers default. Two Bindings omitting domain.name on the same backend collide, so name each domain when multiple Bindings share a leader. Per-leader uniqueness: Admission rejects a Binding whose domain.name is already claimed by another Binding on the same KVCacheBackend (even across different KVCachePools). Separate backends keep separate ledgers and can reuse names. Multi-tenancy requirement: Admission rejects a second distinct domain when the backend has no tenant ledger (leader.multiTenancy: false or observed absent).
