When ledger support is unconfirmed, admission warns and requires an engine image meeting Tenant compatibility . Admin-only registration: Workloads cannot mint new tenants at runtime; an unregistered domain receives TENANT_NOT_REGISTERED. The pool lists registered domains in status.domains. On the Binding, DomainExclusive confirms name ownership and QuotaGranted confirms a positive effective grant.
Immutable domain fields spec.poolRef and every field under spec.domain (name, blockSize, and dtype) are immutable after creation because changing them strands ledger entries or corrupts cached block layouts. Delete and recreate the Binding to change them; existing cached blocks do not carry over.
Engine cache precision When the model-deployment-kv-cache-dtype-owned Setting is true (default), the operator passes spec.domain.dtype verbatim as --kv-cache-dtype <dtype> to every managed ModelDeployment role and injected Pod , refusing conflicting user flags (Operator-owned keys ).
Why: Store keys omit the element type, and an engine reading a narrower cached block into a wider buffer receives a partial payload without an error.
auto refusal: Admission rejects dtype: auto on new Bindings because different models resolve auto to different types. Legacy auto Bindings remain updatable; see Upgrading to an Enforced Binding Dtype . Cross-engine spelling: When both engines share one Binding, pick a shared spelling (bfloat16, fp8_e4m3, fp8_e5m2, or nvfp4). Engine Accepted dtype values Rejected aliases vLLM (including Ascend) bfloat16, float16, fp8, fp8_e4m3, fp8_e5m2, fp8_inc, fp8_ds_mla, nvfp4 bf16 SGLang bfloat16, bf16, fp8_e4m3, fp8_e5m2, mxfp8, nvfp4, fp4_mx_block16 fp8, float16 Values above reflect vLLM v0.29.0 and SGLang v0.5.18; the running engine image is authoritative.
Capacity grants A namespace has no quota on a pool until an administrator creates a KVCachePoolBinding in that namespace. The Binding registers spec.domain.name as a tenant ID in the store’s ledger and sets its ceiling.
At runtime, workloads send the reuse domain name, not the Binding name. Workloads sharing a domain name share cached blocks and one quota ledger; workloads with distinct domains keep separate caches and ledgers.
Requested and effective quota spec.quota.ceiling is the requested namespace limit (required because the store rejects tenants without a policy). status.effectiveQuota is the byte grant computed by the store:
Within allocatable capacity: effectiveQuota equals ceiling. Oversubscribed: The store scales each domain’s grant proportionally to its requested ceiling. On KVCachePool, QuotaWithinTotal turns False (Oversubscribed) when Binding ceilings exceed spec.quota.total without blocking writes. QuotaWithinTotal=True compares ceilings only against spec.quota.total; if mounted member capacity is smaller, effectiveQuota still scales down to what members mounted.
Full-quota behavior Reaching effectiveQuota triggers per-domain eviction rather than immediate write failures:
Silent replacement: New writes discard unleased objects in the same domain (in arbitrary shard order) while global eviction counters remain 0 and status.usage stays at effectiveQuota. Lease exhaustion (TENANT_QUOTA_EXCEEDED): Reading an object leases it (5m by default; see KV Cache Election and Failover ). Writes fail only when every object in a full grant holds an active lease. status.overQuota meaning: Because writes cannot push usage past the grant, overQuota turns true only when a proportional recalculation cuts effectiveQuota below bytes the domain already holds. Compare status.usage against status.effectiveQuota to detect saturation. Neither KVCachePool nor KVCachePoolBinding exposes eviction settings or counters because store eviction watermarks and metrics are process-global on the leader. Configure global eviction flags in spec.connection.managed.leader.extraArgs (KV Cache Election and Failover ).
Quota policy file The pool controller renders all Binding ceilings on a backend into one seed ConfigMap. An init container copies that seed onto a writable volume (writing an empty policy document if no pool has bound the backend yet) so the leader can atomically rename updated policy files on admin API writes.
If QuotaPolicyWritable on KVCachePool is False, policy updates have stopped reaching the leader; inspect the pool condition message and leader logs.
Unavailable store capacity When no member segments are mounted (on initial startup or for ~5–30 s while members remount after a leader restart), allocatable capacity is zero. Both the pool (CapacityAllocatable=False, reason NothingToAllocate) and its Bindings (QuotaGranted=False) leave Ready until segments remount so workloads do not treat a zero-grant store as healthy.
Single-tenant backends (leader.multiTenancy: false or external masters without a ledger) are the one exception: QuotaLedgerAvailable reports False/MultiTenancyDisabled while the pool stays Ready for its single domain.
Pod injection Standalone Pods can attach to a KVCachePoolBinding via the opt-in mutating webhook. Pods without kvcache.gpustack.ai/inject: "true" are ignored.
Pod injection configuration yamlCopy apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: name: chat-0 namespace: team-a labels: kvcache.gpustack.ai/inject: "true" # required opt-in label; immutable annotations: kvcache.gpustack.ai/binding: team-a # required KVCachePoolBinding in this namespace kvcache.gpustack.ai/engine: vLLM # required; enum: vLLM, SGLang kvcache.gpustack.ai/manufacturer: ascend # optional; vLLM only (selects vLLM-Ascend) kvcache.gpustack.ai/role: Prefill # optional; vLLM only (Prefill or Decode; omit for plain server) kvcache.gpustack.ai/container: server # required when Pod has multiple containers spec: containers: - name: server image: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.29.0 command: - vllm args: - serve - --model - Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct resources: requests: memory: 16Gi # include +128 MiB (vLLM) or +16 MiB (SGLang) staging overhead limits: memory: 16Gi Same-namespace scope: kvcache.gpustack.ai/binding resolves only in the Pod namespace (/ is refused), and inject, injected, and client-config freeze after creation. Injected flags: vLLM receives --kv-transfer-config, MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH, --kv-cache-dtype, and /etc/gpustack/kvcache (never pass kv_offloading_size). SGLang receives --hicache-storage-backend mooncake, --enable-hierarchical-cache, --kv-cache-dtype, and MOONCAKE_* variables (reserving hicache_ratio 2.0 × device KV pool + 10 GiB host RAM). Refused engine launch The webhook fails closed when injection or pool readiness is invalid. Inspect Warning events on the owning controller (Deployment or ReplicaSet) and container logs:
bashCopy kubectl -n <namespace> get events --field-selector type=Warning kubectl -n <namespace> describe rs <replicaset-name> kubectl -n <namespace> logs <pod-name> -c <container-name> Symptom Expected signal Resolution Missing required annotation Refusal naming binding or engine Set kvcache.gpustack.ai/binding (same namespace) and kvcache.gpustack.ai/engine (vLLM or SGLang). Invalid role or target container Refusal naming Server, missing container, or init container Omit role on standard servers (Server is refused); name an app container in kvcache.gpustack.ai/container. Pool or ledger not ready Refusal naming QuotaLedgerAvailable or status.clientEndpoint Restore the KVCacheBackend leader and wait for KVCachePool status.clientEndpoint. Conflicting flag, env, or mount Refusal naming --kv-transfer-config, MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH, --hicache-storage-backend, --kv-cache-dtype, or /etc/gpustack/kvcache Remove the duplicate flag, env var, or mount from the Pod spec so it matches spec.domain.dtype. Shell -c or env -S launch Refusal rejecting sh -c, bash -c, or env -S Put the engine binary in command and its flags in args; the forwarding annotation does not override shell -c refusals. Wrapper script or bare args Refusal rejecting bare args or a .sh wrapper Launch the engine binary directly, or set kvcache.gpustack.ai/launch-args-forwarded: "true" only when the wrapper forwards appended arguments ("$@"). Transport mismatch Admission NotSupportedTransport or vLLM-Ascend NotImplementedError for tcp Set spec.transport.protocol: CANN on Ascend backends or align member group protocols. Pod binding verification Verify injection on an admitted Pod by reading kvcache.gpustack.ai/injected:
bashCopy kubectl -n <namespace> get pod <pod-name> -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations.kvcache\.gpustack\.ai/injected}{"\n"}' Captured output:
textCopy {"binding":"chat","engine":"vllm","vehicle":"file","domain":"team-a-chat", "tenantInjected":true,"launchProgram":"vllm","launchArgsForwarded":false} Confirm "binding" and "domain" match your KVCachePoolBinding and "tenantInjected" is true (for a ModelDeployment, also check CacheAttached in status.conditions). On vLLM Pods, confirm the image carries the Mooncake store connector:
bashCopy kubectl -n <namespace> exec <pod-name> -- python3 -c \ "import vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.mooncake.store.worker; print('reader present')" Cache transfer troubleshooting A ModelDeployment bound through a KVCachePoolBinding reports on status.conditions whether its engines write to the pool. The verdict judges the keys of save_put and load_get alone: a replica fails when every key of every transfer fails. Lookups answer over TCP and stay successful while a fabric-only pool refuses every transfer, and vLLM records a fully refused transfer as partial_failure, so neither the lookup status nor the transfer status alone decides it.
Symptom Expected signal Resolution CacheAttached=False with reason CacheOperationsFailing The deployment stays Ready and serves every request. The message names the pool, its transports and, per replica, the transfer operations attempted and how many keys failed. If the message says the engine has no RDMA interface, set spec.roles[i].resources.interface on the named role and let the replicas roll. Otherwise read the engine logs and the KVCacheBackend member logs for the transport error. Admission warning that a role writes to a pool whose every transport is rdma, efa or Ascend A5 Host RoCE and needs a fabric interface The request is admitted. The warning names the role, the pool and spec.roles[i].resources.interface. Set resources.interface on the named role before sending traffic. Without it every engine-to-store transfer is refused while the deployment keeps reporting Ready. Tenant compatibility tenantInjected: true confirms only that the webhook wrote tenant_id (vLLM) or MOONCAKE_TENANT_ID (SGLang); the engine image must also support tenant arguments:
Minor-line match: Verify pip show mooncake-transfer-engine (or mooncake-transfer-engine-npu on Ascend) matches the backend store’s minor line (Version compatibility ). Non-default domain floor: A spec.domain.name other than default requires mooncake-transfer-engine >= 0.3.13; older builds fail startup with TypeError: setup(): incompatible function arguments. Legacy image fallback: Omit spec.domain.name (or set default) when running pre-0.3.13 engine images. Quota and deletion checks Compare effectiveQuota and usage with kubectl get kvcpb (EFFECTIVE and USAGE stay blank when multiTenancy is false):
textCopy NAME POOL DOMAIN EFFECTIVE USAGE PHASE AGE team-a shared-dram qwen-72b-v2 450Gi 280Gi Ready 6d When deleting a KVCachePoolBinding or KVCachePool stays in Deleting, inspect Releasable=False and act on the owner named by its reason:
Releasable reason Cause Resolution HeldByWorkloads Workloads in status.usedBy still reference the Binding Delete or detach the named workloads in the namespace. LedgerNotReleased Domain still holds bytes on the leader, or leader is unreachable during pool teardown Drain the domain or restore leader :9003 reachability (retries every 30 s). LedgerRequestFailed Admin API call failed, leaving ledger state unknown Inspect KVCachePool and KVCacheBackend conditions and restore the leader. If an external or permanently destroyed leader will never return, clear the pool finalizer manually (this orphans quota entries if the leader is still live):
bashCopy kubectl patch kvcp <pool> --type=merge -p '{"metadata":{"finalizers":null}}' Limitations A Binding is a provisioning and accounting record, not an access boundary. Any Pod in the cluster that can reach the leader Service and knows a registered domain name can read or write that domain’s blocks without credentials. Do not place mutually distrusting tenants on a shared backend without external network isolation.
Managed backends enable the tenant ledger by default unless leader.multiTenancy: false is set (required below Mooncake 0.3.12; see GPUStack build variants ). When a backend runs without a tenant ledger:
Admission allows a KVCachePool on a managed single-tenant backend with a warning that per-tenant quotas are inactive (external backends are discovered at reconcile time). Workloads omit the tenant ID and share the store’s single default tenant. See also — KV Cache Backend (store configuration and member transports) · Model Deployment Configuration (attaching roles through spec.kvCache.poolRef) · Shared Cache Walkthrough (end-to-end setup and verification)
Next → Accelerator Requests — request whole, sliced, or partitioned accelerators.
title: KV Cache Pools and Bindings

content:
Model Delivery ModelArtifact gives model weights a stable, content-addressed or volume-backed identity. Workloads consume weights via engine download, verified node cache (NodeModelStore), PersistentVolumeClaim, OCI image volume, or remote host-memory transfer without repeating URIs or tokens.
Contents Overview Configuration Operations Troubleshooting Overview Model Artifact defines weight sources, resolution, and workload mounts. Remote Weight Delivery covers streaming tensors from prepared source Nodes.
Configuration Start with the artifact manifest to declare hub, PVC, or OCI image weights. Configure Model Prefetch for namespace cache budgets, warm-up placement, and node-to-node peer sync .
For an end-to-end cache run, follow the Model Prefetch Walkthrough .
Operations Step 1: Configure cache Set deploy-time and runtime cache policies in Model Store Operations , and inspect per-node state in Node cache inspection .
Step 2: Inspect delivery Check artifact resolution and node cache status:
bashCopy kubectl -n <namespace> get modelartifact <artifact-name> -o yaml kubectl get nodemodelstores Verification: Confirm Resolved=True on the ModelArtifact (Status ) and Ready=True on target NodeModelStore objects. See Progress subresource for live download progress and RBAC.
Troubleshooting If weights do not reach a ModelDeployment, inspect the artifact, deployment conditions, and Pod events:
bashCopy kubectl -n <namespace> describe modelartifact <artifact-name> kubectl -n <namespace> get modeldeployment <deployment-name> -o yaml kubectl -n <namespace> describe pod <pod-name> Condition Reason Resolution WeightsReady=False NodeDeliveryUnavailable Enable modelManager.enabled and verify the model.csi.gpustack.ai CSIDriver. WeightsReady=False FilterNeedsNodeDelivery Switch model-artifact-delivery-mode to Node or remove file patterns. Use Model Store Operations for CSI mount diagnosis and Remote Weight Delivery for remote transfer failures.
See also — Model Deployment (serving workloads) · GPU Instances (mounting weights in workspaces)
Next → Model Artifact — configure weight sources, digests, and workload delivery.
title: Model Delivery

content:
Model Artifact A ModelArtifact records a model’s source, credentials, and verified identity once per namespace. ModelDeployment references it via spec.model.artifactRef, and Instance mounts it via a model volume, keeping URIs, revisions, and hub tokens out of workload specs.
Contents Configuration Image source Workload consumption Weight delivery Status Prerequisites and limitations Configuration Omit status when applying a ModelArtifact (status values below are illustrative). Set expectedDigest only when anchoring a hub source to a known manifest digest:
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelArtifact # namespaced, short name mart metadata: name: qwen-7b namespace: team-a spec: # immutable after creation source: # required; set exactly one source huggingFace: repository: Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct # required revision: main # optional, default: main (branch, tag, or commit) secretRef: # optional Secret in this namespace; key: token name: hf-token # modelScope: # repository: qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct # revision: master # optional, default: master # secretRef: # name: ms-token # persistentVolumeClaim: # claimName: models # PVC in this namespace # path: qwen # optional subdirectory; empty mounts volume root # image: # reference: registry.example.com/team/qwen@sha256:669ed7b1...48 # digest-pinned OCI image allowPatterns: # optional; hub sources only (1..32 entries, 1..256 chars each) - "*.safetensors" - "*.json" - "tokenizer*" ignorePatterns: # optional; hub sources only, wins over allowPatterns - "original/" # expectedDigest: sha256:<64-lowercase-hex-characters> # optional; hub sources only status: resolved: revision: 7ae557604adf67be50417f59c2c2f167def9a775 manifestDigest: sha256:669ed7b128b6ad1658d735326bd172a33497ecdb8bbd72dd0b23c98b58469448 digestSource: Hub # Hub or Expected fileCount: 10 sizeBytes: 999604126 nodes: # hub sources only; NodeModelStore counts across cluster ready: 3 downloading: 1 failed: 0 downloadingPercent: 45 # mean across downloading nodes, in 5% steps conditions: - type: Resolved status: "True" reason: Resolved - type: Degraded status: "False" reason: Healthy Immutability and protection: spec is immutable after creation. The worker.gpustack.ai/model-artifact-protection finalizer holds deletion while any same-namespace ModelDeployment or Instance references the artifact. Filter matching: Patterns use Python fnmatch.fnmatchcase (* and ? cross /; trailing / matches subtree). Filters keeping zero files set Resolved=False/EmptyManifest, and filtered artifacts require Node delivery. Missing references: Referenced Secret or PersistentVolumeClaim objects need not exist at admission; missing objects report SecretNotFound or ClaimNotFound in status.conditions. Resolution and revalidation Hub sources resolve once using the namespace’s token, pinning branches or peeled tags to an exact commit and building the file manifest:
Hugging Face: Non-existent, private, or ungranted gated repositories (which mask file digests) all fail with AccessDenied. Missing refs fail with RevisionNotFound, and network/5xx/429 errors fail with SourceUnavailable. ModelScope: Cross-checks resolved branches/tags against git refs (disagreement fails as SourceUnavailable), re-lists directories up to 3000 direct children (larger directories fail as SourceUnavailable), requires sha256 per file, and emits an InvalidToken Warning Event when a token probe is rejected. Access revalidates every model-artifact-revalidate-interval (default 24h) and on Secret edits via a single-file HEAD (redirects disabled):
Refusal staircase: An access refusal sets Degraded=True first and Resolved=False if repeated 1m later. Deleting the Secret or its token key sets Resolved=False immediately. Outage resilience: SourceUnavailable (or a transient Secret read error) sets only Degraded=True and retries every 1m without revoking Resolved=True. Expected digest anchor: With expectedDigest (sha256:<64-hex>), resolution rejects mismatches (DigestMismatch) and revalidation re-lists the full tree. After two SourceUnavailable checks (1m apart) without a refusal, resolution sets digestSource: Expected (Resolved=True, no commit); Engine delivery is refused (AnchorNeedsNodeDelivery) while Node delivery pulls from peers. Never treat digests as secret (NodeModelStore digests are cluster-visible). Resolved=False blocks new Pod creation, replacements, and scale-out without terminating running Pods. PVC sources resolve once the claim exists (no revision or digest).
Manifest digest For hub sources, manifestDigest is the SHA-256 of a canonical gpustack-manifest v1 document with one LF-terminated <algorithm>:<hex> <size> <path> line per sorted file (sha256 for LFS and all ModelScope files, gitsha1 for non-LFS Hugging Face git blobs):
textCopy gpustack-manifest v1 gitsha1:4ff64fe5... 807 config.json sha256:8111d5af... 453864 model.safetensors Authorization is per namespace: Identical public and private repositories produce the same digest; mounting still requires Resolved=True in the consumer’s namespace. No cross-hub deduplication: Non-LFS files hash differently on Hugging Face (gitsha1) and ModelScope (sha256), yielding distinct digests. Image source Package weights into an OCI image pinned by manifest digest (@sha256:...). Mutable tags, file patterns, and expectedDigest are refused at admission; status.resolved records only resolvedTime.
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelArtifact metadata: name: qwen-image namespace: team-a spec: source: image: reference: registry.example.com/team/qwen@sha256:669ed7b128b6ad1658d735326bd172a33497ecdb8bbd72dd0b23c98b58469448 Image build and delivery Place all required weight shards, shard index (model.safetensors.index.json), tokenizer, and config files at the image root (no subPath is supported), then pin the resulting manifest digest in spec.source.image.reference.
Build one mountable OCI image from a local model directory (copying shards and metadata to /) and capture its immutable @sha256:... digest:
bashCopy cat <<'EOF' > Dockerfile FROM scratch COPY model.safetensors.index.json config.json generation_config.json tokenizer.json tokenizer_config.json / COPY *.safetensors / EOF docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64 --push \ --iidfile /tmp/model.iid \ -t registry.example.com/team/qwen:v1 . docker buildx imagetools inspect registry.example.com/team/qwen:v1 --format '{{.Manifest.Digest}}' The operator does not inspect registry contents; build integrity is owned by the image producer.
Image sources always deliver as read-only Kubernetes image volumes at /var/lib/gpustack/model without model.csi.gpustack.ai or ephemeral-storage adjustments. Pull errors surface on Pod events while WeightsReady stays False/WeightsNotMounted. Node-pinned Instances verify node kubelet and containerd floors before creating a Pod.
Image prerequisites Component Minimum version Reason kube-apiserver 1.35 ImageVolume is beta on by default in 1.35 (GA in 1.36); artifact creation is refused below 1.35. kubelet 1.35 Required to mount image volumes on target Nodes. containerd 2.1 Required runtime for image volumes (subPath would require 2.2, so root-only mounts are used). Pod Security Admission Restricted permits image volumes on Kubernetes >= 1.33 (kubernetes#130394). Private registries use the workload’s existing imagePullSecrets, and standard containerd mirrors (Harbor, Spegel, Dragonfly) work transparently (overlapping layer digests pulled in 112 ms / 11.8 MB versus 2m10s / 7.89 GB cold).
Disk usage and cleanup With containerd’s default discard_unpacked_layers = false, a pulled model image stores both compressed content blobs and unpacked snapshots (kubelet CRI image size reports only the compressed blobs, undercounting a 15.24 GB model by ~2.26×):
Layer format Content store Snapshots Total disk Ratio to raw Gzip-compressed 12.07 GB 15.24 GB ~27.3 GB 1.79× Uncompressed 15.24 GB 15.24 GB ~30.5 GB 2.00× Kubelet image GC behavior:
Protected while mounted: Running containers protect mounted model images (kubelet >= 1.31, containerd >= 2.1); completed Pods do not. Collected after scale-to-zero: Once the last Pod exits, the next 5m GC pass can remove the image because imageMinimumGCAge checks first-detected time rather than release time. High-threshold cascade: Pushing disk usage past imageGCHighThresholdPercent (85% default) triggers GC across all unused images on the Node. Workload consumption ModelDeployment reference Set spec.model.artifactRef when creating a ModelDeployment (spec.model is immutable):
diffCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeployment metadata: name: qwen-7b-serving spec: model: name: qwen-7b # served model name + artifactRef: + name: qwen-7b # ModelArtifact in this namespace Hub sources follow the model-artifact-delivery-mode Setting (Engine default; Node when the chart enables modelManager, rolling hub deployments once on switch). PVC and OCI image sources always mount directly:
Aspect PVC (Pvc) Hub (Engine) Hub (Node) OCI image (Image) Mount / cache Read-only PVC at /var/lib/gpustack/model (subPath = path) Engine downloads into /var/lib/gpustack/model-cache Read-only CSI model.csi.gpustack.ai at /var/lib/gpustack/model Read-only image volume at /var/lib/gpustack/model Engine argv /var/lib/gpustack/model <repository> --revision <commit> /var/lib/gpustack/model /var/lib/gpustack/model Served name --served-model-name <spec.model.name> Same Same Same Take-over roles (roles[].command set) receive PVC, Node, or Image volume mounts without argv changes, and receive nothing under Engine. While artifactRef is set, admission refuses manual model/revision/download flags, HF_* or MODELSCOPE_* variables, and custom mounts overlapping /var/lib/gpustack/model or /var/lib/gpustack/model-cache. Keep --served-model-name equal to spec.model.name so router routing and prefix scoring match.
Instance model volumes Mount a ModelArtifact into an Instance at creation or while stopped (Additional volumes and Workspace stop and restart ):
diffCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: Instance metadata: name: workspace-demo spec: + additionalVolumes: + - mountPath: /models/qwen + model: + artifactRef: + name: qwen-7b The mount is always read-only and forbids subPath. Hub artifacts always use Node CSI delivery on Instances (waiting in Starting if model.csi.gpustack.ai is absent), PVC artifacts follow claim placement, and OCI image artifacts use Kubernetes image volumes.
KV reuse domain When both artifactRef and spec.kvCache are set (outside vLLM-Ascend), the operator prefixes KV store keys (cache_prefix on vLLM, extra_backend_tag on SGLang) with m- plus 32 hex chars of manifestDigest (or the SHA-256 of the artifact UID for PVC and OCI image sources).
PVC and image identity: Replacing files inside an existing PVC keeps the same artifact UID and KV prefix; create a new ModelArtifact when changing PVC weights. Two ModelArtifacts naming the same OCI image have distinct UIDs and do not share KV blocks. Weight delivery Engine delivery Under Engine delivery, the engine downloads the pinned commit into an emptyDir sized to max(sizeBytes * 1.1, sizeBytes + 1 GiB), raising the container’s ephemeral-storage limit (not request) by the same amount:
Injected environment: Hugging Face sets owned HF_HOME, HF_ENDPOINT, and HF_TOKEN (secretKeyRef token). ModelScope sets owned MODELSCOPE_CACHE, MODELSCOPE_DOMAIN (bare host), MODELSCOPE_API_TOKEN, and VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE=true / SGLANG_USE_MODELSCOPE=true. Defaulted HTTPS_PROXY and NO_PROXY yield to user roles[].env. Rollouts and CA bundles: Editing hub endpoint or proxy Settings rolls Engine-delivered deployments (model-artifact-ca-bundle is not mounted into tenant namespaces; mount a tenant ConfigMap and set REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE instead). Ensure any namespace LimitRange allows the raised ephemeral-storage limit. PVC binding and placement Because Kueue topology-aware scheduling (TAS) ignores Pod volumes, the operator aligns Pod creation with PVC binding and node affinity:
Claim state Operator behavior Bound Injects the PV’s required node affinity into every Pod at creation. Pending (WaitForFirstConsumer with provisioner) Creates Pods so the first scheduled Pod binds the volume. Pending (no-provisioner or Immediate) Holds Pod creation with ClaimNotBound (pre-bind static local PVs via spec.volumeName). Multi-Pod mount without ROX or RWX Holds Pod creation with AccessModeConflict. On a single-accelerator node with cold page caches (1000 GiB boot SSD; 2 TiB network disks), a 7B model loaded in 32.6 s over S3 CSI (geesefs, 467 MB/s cold, ~455 MB/s warm without page cache), 34.8–35.7 s from boot disk (479 MB/s cold, 7.4–7.8 GB/s warm), and 40.2 s over NFS CSI (~312 MB/s cold).
Point geesefs S3 PV endpoints at a ClusterIP instead of *.svc.cluster.local. Host systemd mounts resolve names through the host DNS resolver rather than cluster DNS.
Status On ModelDeployment, status.model echoes the artifact delivery mode (PVC, Engine, Node, or Image) and WeightsReady summarizes weight availability (holding rollouts with ReplicasUpToDate=False/RolloutHeldByWeights when new Pods are blocked):
WeightsReady Reason Action True NotApplicable, Mounted, Downloaded Healthy: no artifact configured, or all Pods have weights. False ArtifactNotFound, ArtifactNotResolved Create the ModelArtifact or resolve its hub/secret/claim error. False ClaimNotBound, AccessModeConflict Bind the PVC or use ReadOnlyMany / ReadWriteMany for multi-Pod mounts. False NodeDeliveryUnavailable Enable modelManager (model.csi.gpustack.ai CSIDriver) or switch delivery mode. False FilterNeedsNodeDelivery, AnchorNeedsNodeDelivery Switch model-artifact-delivery-mode to Node for patterned or expectedDigest artifacts. False Materializing, Downloading, WeightsNotMounted Wait for node cache download, engine download, or image pull; inspect Pod events if stalled. False MaterializationFailed Read the NodeModelStore failure reason and retryTime (Model Store Operations ). Progress subresource Query on-demand download progress across up to 64 downloading Nodes (13 s timeout, node names omitted for tenant safety; administrators inspect kubectl get nms directly):
bashCopy kubectl get --raw "/apis/worker.gpustack.ai/v1/namespaces/<ns>/modelartifacts/<name>/progress" Required RBAC: Callers need get on modelartifacts/progress in worker.gpustack.ai (get on modelartifacts alone is insufficient, and the chart grants no tenant RBAC by default):
yamlCopy apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 kind: Role metadata: name: model-artifact-reader namespace: team-a rules: - apiGroups: - worker.gpustack.ai resources: - modelartifacts - modelartifacts/progress verbs: - get - list - watch Grant nodemodelstores (get, list, watch, delete) only to cluster administrators and the GPUStack server via ClusterRole.
Failed mount inspection When WeightsReady stays False, inspect Pod FailedMount events (kubectl -n <ns> describe pod <pod>) and kubectl get nms <node> -o yaml:
Permanent refusal (PermissionDenied): Namespace, artifact UID, or manifestDigest mismatch, or Resolved!=True (cached bytes on disk never authorize another namespace). Transient wait (Aborted or Unavailable): Active background materialization, plugin informer startup sync, or failure backoff before retryTime (Mount refusal vs unavailability ). Prerequisites and limitations Kubernetes 1.29+: PodReadyToStartContainers (default on since 1.29) drives WeightsReady on mounted deliveries. ModelScope Engine SDK floor: Requires runner modelscope >= 1.39.1 for commit-pinned downloads (present in cann9.1-*-vllm0.23.0 and sglang 0.5.18; older CUDA vllm0.25.1 / vllm0.29.0 runners fail with NotExistError unless using Node delivery or a custom image). Engine quirks: sglang-gateway logs one benign 404 tokenizer warning on local mount paths and routes by text; vLLM 0.29.0 requires --enforce-eager for InternLM2 trust_remote_code. See also — Model Store Operations (Node cache settings, watermarks, and mount diagnosis) · Model Prefetch (cache budgets, warm-up, and peer sync) · Model Deployment Configuration (role and rollout contract) · KV Cache Pools and Bindings (reuse domains prefixed by weight identity)
Next → Model Prefetch — warm cached weights and synchronize peers across nodes.
title: Model Artifact

content:
Model Store Operations The model-manager DaemonSet maintains one verified weight cache per Node. It downloads each hub ModelArtifact digest once and mounts it read-only via model.csi.gpustack.ai after verifying namespace authorization.
Contents Prerequisites Configuration Node cache inspection Operations Troubleshooting Prerequisites Operator namespace Pod Security: The plugin container runs privileged (Bidirectional mount propagation), so the operator namespace requires pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: privileged. Tenant namespaces can enforce restricted. Image mode defaults: Image mode deploys model-manager unless --disable-applications includes model-manager (Installation Modes ), leaving model-artifact-delivery-mode at Engine until changed and requiring standard /var/lib/kubelet. Custom kubelet root: Distributions using non-standard kubelet paths (such as /var/snap/... or /var/lib/k0s/kubelet) require chart mode with modelManager.kubeletDir matching that path. Configuration The Helm chart enables modelManager.enabled: true by default, deploying the model.csi.gpustack.ai CSIDriver, per-node DaemonSet, and least-privilege RBAC (the plugin reads no Secrets directly; kubelet passes each mount’s ModelArtifact token):
yamlCopy modelManager: enabled: true rootPath: /var/lib/gpustack/models # mount a dedicated filesystem here in production kubeletDir: /var/lib/kubelet securePort: 32444 # HTTPS /metrics, /readyz, and /livez registrar: image: repository: docker.io/gpustack/mirrored-csi-node-driver-registrar tag: v2.17.0 nodeSelector: {} tolerations: - operator: Exists The worker merges cluster Settings and matching ModelStore overrides into every NodeModelStore.spec within 1m; plugins read only NodeModelStore.spec and the optional CA ConfigMap in the operator namespace.
Settings and precedence Non-empty GPUSTACK_* environment variables on the worker Deployment overwrite stored Setting values on every worker restart (modelManager.enabled: true sets GPUSTACK_MODEL_ARTIFACT_DELIVERY_MODE=Node; modelTransfer.enabled: false sets GPUSTACK_MODEL_ARTIFACT_REMOTE_DELIVERY_POLICY=Disabled). Persist changes to chart-seeded settings in Helm values.yaml, and check overrides on startup:
bashCopy kubectl -n gpustack-system get settings kubectl -n gpustack-system get deploy -o yaml | grep -A1 'GPUSTACK_' kubectl -n gpustack-system logs deploy/gpustack-operator-worker | grep 'setting overridden on start' Setting (GPUSTACK_* env) Default Effect and constraints model-artifact-delivery-mode (..._DELIVERY_MODE) Engine (Node in chart) Immediate; Engine or Node (Node requires CSIDriver). model-artifact-remote-delivery-policy (..._REMOTE_DELIVERY_POLICY) Prefer Immediate; Disabled, Require, or Prefer. model-artifact-huggingface-endpoint (..._HUGGINGFACE_ENDPOINT) https://huggingface.co Next trigger; hub URL for resolution and downloads. model-artifact-modelscope-endpoint (..._MODELSCOPE_ENDPOINT) https://www.modelscope.cn Next trigger; bare host passed to engines as MODELSCOPE_DOMAIN. model-artifact-https-proxy (..._HTTPS_PROXY) (blank) Next trigger; http/https URL without embedded credentials. model-artifact-no-proxy (..._NO_PROXY) (blank) Next trigger; comma-separated hosts bypassing the proxy. model-artifact-ca-bundle (..._CA_BUNDLE) (blank) Next trigger; ConfigMap (ca.crt) in operator namespace (plugin and worker only). model-artifact-revalidate-interval (..._REVALIDATE_INTERVAL) 24h Next trigger; minimum 1m. model-store-high-watermark (..._STORE_HIGH_WATERMARK) 80 Immediate; integer above low watermark, max 95. model-store-low-watermark (..._STORE_LOW_WATERMARK) 70 Immediate; integer >= 1, below high watermark. model-store-download-concurrency (..._STORE_DOWNLOAD_CONCURRENCY) 8 Immediate; concurrent HTTP requests per Node (1..64). model-store-download-bandwidth (..._STORE_DOWNLOAD_BANDWIDTH) 0 Immediate; byte rate (200Mi); 0 means unlimited. model-store-peer-sync (..._STORE_PEER_SYNC) true Immediate; enables peer pulls on port 32445 (Node-to-node sync ). model-prefetch-warmup-image (..._PREFETCH_WARMUP_IMAGE) gpustack/mirrored-python:3.12-alpine Immediate; warm-up Pod image (sh, find, sha256sum). Invalid GPUSTACK_* seeds stop worker startup; invalid NodeModelStore.spec values set Ready=False/InvalidConfiguration on the Node and halt new downloads while keeping published mounts readable. Update an unseeded runtime Setting directly:
diffCopy apiVersion: gpustack.ai/v1 kind: Setting metadata: name: model-store-download-bandwidth namespace: gpustack-system spec: - value: "0" + value: 200Mi ModelStore overrides A cluster-scoped ModelStore overrides watermarks and download limits field by field on matched Nodes (writing the winning store name to NodeModelStore.spec.store). If two ModelStores match the same Node, both report SelectorOverlap and the alphabetically first name wins; make selectors disjoint instead of relying on tie-breaking.
Node cache inspection bashCopy kubectl get nms kubectl get nms gpu-node-01 -o yaml kubectl get nms gpu-node-01 -o jsonpath='{.metadata.generation} {.status.observedGeneration}{"\n"}' kubectl get --raw "/apis/worker.gpustack.ai/v1/namespaces/<ns>/modelartifacts/<name>/progress" kubectl get --raw "/api/v1/namespaces/gpustack-system/pods/https:<plugin-pod>:32444/proxy/metrics" kubectl -n gpustack-system logs -l app.kubernetes.io/component=model-manager --tail=100 Applied config: status.observedGeneration matching metadata.generation confirms the plugin applied spec; the Ready message notes any kubelet watermark cap. Cached digests: status.models lists each digest (Ready, Downloading, or Failed), mounted state, and downloadedBytes (updated every 30 s on 5% steps) without exposing tenant names. Retry backoff: Failed entries record reason and retryTime; fix the underlying cause and wait past retryTime for the next mount retry. Model Manager options model-manager (alias mm) runs beside node-driver-registrar and reads runtime policy from NodeModelStore.spec. Only --model-manager-service-account (default gpustack-operator-model-manager) can update nodemodelstores/status:
bashCopy gpustack-operator model-manager --node-name="$(hostname)" --cache-root=/mnt/models Flag Default Purpose --node-name — Target Node and NodeModelStore name. --kubelet-dir /var/lib/kubelet Kubelet root containing pods mount directories. --cache-root /var/lib/gpustack/models Host directory storing cached model trees. --csi-socket <kubelet-dir>/plugins/model.csi.gpustack.ai/csi.sock CSI Unix domain socket path. --secure-port 32444 HTTPS port serving /metrics, /readyz, and /livez. Cache collection rules Collection runs above the high watermark, when a reservation does not fit, and every 5m. It evicts oldest lastUsedTime entries down to the low watermark while skipping mounted trees and ModelPrefetch pins (spec.pinned):
Published trees: Eligible 10m after the last Pod unmounts them. Stale partials and failures: Idle partial downloads and disk-absent Failed status entries expire after 24h. Cache capacity accounting Watermarks measure total filesystem usage (including root-reserved blocks), and active downloads reserve their full size upfront. If nothing unpinned and unmounted can be evicted, the Node sets CapacityLow=True.
Mount a dedicated filesystem at modelManager.rootPath. When rootPath shares kubelet’s pods filesystem, the plugin caps the high watermark at the lowest of 100 - nodefs.available - 5, 100 - imagefs.available - 5, and imageGCHighThresholdPercent - 5.
The worker reads those thresholds from kubelet configz (spec.kubelet) and defaults to an 80% cap (10%, 15%, 85) when unset or unreachable. Model downloads never trigger kubelet DiskPressure or image GC.
Operations Delivery mode changes Switching model-artifact-delivery-mode between Engine and Node rolls hub-backed ModelDeployments once. PVC artifacts always mount directly, and Instances always use Node CSI for hub artifacts:
KV cache miss on switch: vLLM’s KV key includes the final segment of --model (model under Node versus the repository name under Engine), so switching invalidates prior vLLM KV hits. Guardrails: Node without model.csi.gpustack.ai blocks new Pods with NodeDeliveryUnavailable; Engine on patterned artifacts blocks new Pods with FilterNeedsNodeDelivery. Remote Weight Delivery layers inside the active delivery mode without changing Engine or Node semantics. Replica placement Node-delivered Pods receive preferred node affinity toward Nodes holding their digest (unless the Pod sets a preferred topology level; see Topology Operations ). Compute capacity keeps higher priority than cache locality:
bashCopy kubectl get pod <replica> -o jsonpath='{.spec.affinity.nodeAffinity.preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution}{"\n"}{.spec.nodeName}{"\n"}' kubectl get nms -o custom-columns='NODE:.metadata.name,DIGESTS:.status.models[*].digest' Cold downloads occur when warm Nodes are full or no Node held the digest at Pod creation. They also occur if TASRespectNodeAffinityPreferred (enabled by default) is disabled in custom Kueue YAML.
Upgrade defaults Chart Node default: With modelManager.enabled: true, the chart seeds GPUSTACK_MODEL_ARTIFACT_DELIVERY_MODE=Node on every worker start. Upgrades from pre-node-delivery releases roll hub deployments once unless modelManager.enabled=false is set. Rolling model-manager: Rolling the DaemonSet leaves running Pod bind mounts active; concurrent new mounts retry automatically once the replacement plugin Pod becomes Ready. Removal and cache migration Disabling modelManager: Switch model-artifact-delivery-mode to Engine before setting modelManager.enabled=false so hub deployments keep scaling after CSIDriver and NodeModelStore removal. Host disk cleanup or rootPath change: Uninstalling or repathing rootPath leaves existing files on disk; remove /var/lib/gpustack/models manually after all Pods unmount it. Troubleshooting Symptom Signal Resolution No new Pod under Node delivery WeightsReady=False (NodeDeliveryUnavailable) Verify modelManager.enabled: true and CSIDriver model.csi.gpustack.ai. Patterned artifact creates no Pod WeightsReady=False (FilterNeedsNodeDelivery) Set model-artifact-delivery-mode to Node or remove patterns. Pod waiting on cold cache WeightsReady=False (Materializing) Check FailedMount byte progress; Pod starts within ~2m of download completion. Node cache download failed WeightsReady=False (MaterializationFailed) Inspect NodeModelStore.status.models[] reason, message, and retryTime. Container mount blocked WeightsReady=False (WeightsNotMounted) Inspect Pod FailedMount events (PermissionDenied or image pull error). Failed mount inspection bashCopy kubectl -n <ns> get md <deployment> -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions[?(@.type=="WeightsReady")]}{"\n"}' kubectl -n <ns> get events --field-selector involvedObject.name=<pod>,reason=FailedMount kubectl get nms <node> -o yaml kubectl -n gpustack-system logs <model-manager-pod> --tail=100 Mount refusal vs unavailability FailedMount signal Cause Next action PermissionDenied Missing inline CSI volume, missing or unresolved ModelArtifact in Pod namespace, or UID/manifestDigest mismatch Ensure ModelArtifact in the Pod namespace is Resolved=True; recreate the Pod if the artifact was recreated. Aborted (materializing sha256:...) Background download in progress Wait for kubelet retry (Pod starts up to ~2m after publication). Unavailable right after plugin restart Plugin informer still syncing initial artifacts Confirm model-manager Pod is Ready and wait for kubelet retry. Unavailable with Failed digest Earlier download failed (1m to 1h backoff) Fix the NodeModelStore failure cause below and wait past retryTime. NodeModelStore reason Cause Resolution InvalidRequest Invalid hub URL, proxy, or CA bundle (Ready=False/InvalidConfiguration) Fix the Setting or ModelStore so NodeModelStore.spec updates. AccessDenied Hub rejected token (1m–1h backoff) Update the ModelArtifact Secret token and wait past retryTime. SourceUnavailable Hub unreachable/5xx/429, or no peer holds an Expected digest Check network/proxy or seed one peer Node for Expected anchors. IntegrityMismatch File or manifest hash mismatch Check upstream mirror integrity; corrupted partials are discarded. InsufficientCapacity Download exceeds high watermark (CapacityLow=True/NothingToRemove) Unpin unused models, add disk space, or reduce concurrent cold mounts. Canceled No Pod requested the digest for 5m None required; partial files remain and resume immediately on the next mount. See also — Model Artifact (artifact contract and progress RBAC) · Model Prefetch (cache budgets, warm-up, and peer sync) · Remote Weight Delivery (host-memory remote weight loading)
Next → Remote Weight Delivery — stream weights from prepared source nodes into serving replicas.
title: Model Store Operations

content:
Model Prefetch Declare model cache policies, namespace byte budgets, and warm-up targets across ModelStore, ModelStoreBinding, and ModelPrefetch. Once one Node caches a digest, peer model-manager plugins distribute it over TCP without repeating upstream hub downloads.
Resource Scope Owner Purpose ModelStore Cluster Administrator Overrides cache watermarks and download limits on matched Nodes. ModelStoreBinding Namespaced Administrator Grants a namespace a byte budget, pinning rights, and optional source RAM over named stores. ModelPrefetch Namespaced Tenant Warms an artifact onto target Nodes, manages retention, and optionally prepares remote sources. Contents Cache resources Prefetch placement Cache quota and retention Prefetch status Node-to-node sync Cache resources A ModelStore selects cache Nodes via spec.nodeSelector and overrides cluster Settings field by field. kubectl get modelstores shows policy watermarks; check kubelet-capped watermarks on NodeModelStore .
A ModelStoreBinding grants store access, a monotonic quota.bytes budget, optional allowPinned, and optional sourceMemory (Source preparation ):
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelStore # cluster-scoped metadata: name: rtx6000-models spec: nodeSelector: # required; avoid overlapping selectors across ModelStores matchLabels: kubernetes.io/hostname: gpu-node # watermarks: # optional overrides; omitted fields inherit cluster Settings # highPercent: 80 # lowPercent: 70 # download: # concurrency: 8 # bytesPerSecond: 0 # 0 means unlimited on this pool --- apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelStoreBinding # namespaced metadata: name: rtx6000-models namespace: gpustack-elastic spec: storeRefs: # required; 1..8 ModelStore names, immutable - name: rtx6000-models quota: bytes: 64Gi # required; can grow, cannot shrink allowPinned: false # optional, default: false; can turn true, cannot turn false Condition Reason Resolution Multiple ModelStores match one Node SelectorOverlap Make spec.nodeSelector sets disjoint across stores. ModelPrefetch targets ungranted Nodes Target outside storeRefs Restrict prefetch placement or create a Binding covering those stores. Update shrinks quota.bytes or clears allowPinned Monotonic grant rule Keep or increase quota.bytes (recreate the Binding to reduce it). Deleting a ModelPrefetch deletes its warm-up Pods, clears its pins on the next union pass, and leaves cached bytes to ordinary watermark collection.
Prefetch placement spec.placement selects Nodes via acceleratorTypes or nodeSelector (mutually exclusive). Omitting both inherits accelerated pools from same-namespace ModelDeployments referencing the artifact (CPU-only roles excluded):
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelPrefetch metadata: name: qwen-prefetch namespace: gpustack-elastic spec: artifactRef: # required; ModelArtifact in this namespace name: qwen-7b bindingRef: # required; ModelStoreBinding in this namespace name: rtx6000-models placement: # set at most one of acceleratorTypes or nodeSelector acceleratorTypes: - gpu-pool # nodeSelector: # matchLabels: # accelerator: "true" Explicit placement is required whenever spec.source is set for remote weight delivery .
Warm-up Pod The prefetch controller creates one restricted warm-up Pod per target Node using the model-prefetch-warmup-image Setting (requires sh, find, and sha256sum). Each Pod mounts the artifact’s CSI volume, verifies files, and exits once the Node publishes the digest.
Warm-up Pods omit kueue.x-k8s.io/queue-name so Kueue and accelerator Pod webhooks never hold cache warming behind compute quota.
Cache quota and retention A Binding’s budget charges the full resolved byte size per distinct digest on every target Node (shared digests across namespaces charge each namespace independently). On ModelStoreBinding:
status.usedBytes reports measured usage (omitted while any referenced artifact is unresolved). OverQuota turns True when measured usage exceeds quota.bytes (Unknown while unresolved). Admission rejects missing artifacts or Bindings, ungranted target Nodes, and unauthorized pins. It also rejects projected footprints (resolved size × widest node count per digest) above quota.bytes.
Pinning and expiry spec.retention.pinned (requires allowPinned: true) protects digests from eviction while still counting toward disk usage (Cache collection rules ). The controller merges pins across all namespaces into each NodeModelStore.spec.pinned list.
spec.retention.ttlAfterLastUse unpins a Node’s copy once unmounted past that duration (evaluated at the 1-hour granularity of lastUsedTime).
Prefetch status ModelPrefetch reports desiredNodes, readyNodes, downloadingNodes, and conditions Progressing, Available, Degraded, and Lapsed. Available checks readyNodes >= minReady (0 means all desired Nodes); Lapsed indicates ttlAfterLastUse unpinned copies below minReady.
With spec.source set, SourceReady (SourceServing) and status.transfer track active host-memory source leases. Up to 16 generations display (SourceSummaryTruncated=True when capped), while full observations drive readiness and reservedBytes:
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelPrefetch metadata: name: warm-model namespace: team-a status: transfer: generations: [] # capped at 16 display entries serving: artifactUID: artifact-uid artifactGeneration: 1 digest: sha256:aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa readyLeaseExpiresAt: "2026-11-07T12:01:00Z" conditions: - type: SourceReady status: "True" observedGeneration: 2 reason: SourceServing - type: SourceSummaryTruncated status: "False" observedGeneration: 2 reason: CompleteSummary Node-to-node sync With modelManager.enabled: true, plugins serve published cache trees to cold peers over TCP port 32445. One seed Node downloads from the hub, and cold Nodes pull from peers even during hub outages.
yamlCopy modelManager: port: 32445 # peer TCP port; 0 disables peer serving and pulling peerSync: maxServingStreams: 8 # concurrent outbound file streams per seed node streamsPerSource: 4 # concurrent inbound range streams per puller The model-store-peer-sync Setting defaults to true; set false to pull from the hub without restarting plugins. Standalone model-manager keeps peer sync off until port and peer auth flags are set.
Peer authentication and network Pulling plugins send a projected ServiceAccount token (gpustack-model-peer audience). Serving plugins verify it via TokenReview, caching positive answers until the earlier of 2 minutes and token expiry, and never caching refusals. Peer clients skip TLS verification on the plugin’s self-signed certificate; use trusted Pod networks or set modelManager.port: 0.
The default NetworkPolicy limits plugin ingress to the worker and peer model-manager Pods. On CNIs where hostNetwork bypasses podSelector rules, TokenReview still blocks unauthorized callers; add scrapers under modelManager.networkPolicy.scrapers.
Checkpoint resume and metrics Before pulling bytes, a cold Node verifies the peer’s manifest against the artifact’s manifestDigest (skipping older manifestless trees). Downloads stream HTTP byte ranges from one peer and checkpoint hashes every 64 MiB, resuming on another peer or the hub if a seed fails.
Source tracking: NodeModelStore.status.models[].source reports Hub or Peer (majority bytes), and plugin :32444/metrics exposes gpustack_model_manager_download_bytes_total split by the source label (hub or peer). Trade-offs: Peer sync cuts hub egress and hub dependency rather than fan-out time on slower east-west fabrics. Each concurrent puller uses ~0.25 vCPU on 2-vCPU seed Nodes. See also — Model Artifact (artifact digests and progress subresource) · Model Store Operations (settings, node status, and watermark collection) · Remote Weight Delivery (host-memory sources prepared via ModelPrefetch)
Next → Model Store Operations — configure node cache settings and inspect NodeModelStore state.
title: Model Prefetch

content:
Remote Weight Delivery Remote weight delivery streams model tensors from a prepared source Node’s host RAM directly into serving replicas without writing a full checkpoint onto the target Node’s disk. Sources register verified node-cache weights, targets mount a metadata-only CSI view, and a cluster-wide Setting governs activation.
H2H means Host-to-Host and H2D means Host-to-Device. Bounded host-memory windows are reused across batches so successful remote loads write zero checkpoint shards to target storage.
Contents Configuration Source preparation Replica startup Hardware requirements NVIDIA ModelExpress Results Verification Troubleshooting Configuration The model-artifact-remote-delivery-policy Setting controls cluster-wide activation:
Value Behavior Requirements Prefer (default) Streams remotely when a prepared source is SourceReady; falls back to local delivery otherwise. model.csi.gpustack.ai CSIDriver for metadata mounts. Require Streams remotely and waits within startup limits; never downloads locally. model.csi.gpustack.ai CSIDriver and an allowlisted role/backend. Disabled Disables remote delivery, leaving Pod specs and status fields unchanged. None (modelTransfer.enabled: false seeds Disabled on start). modelTransfer.images configures per-vendor source DaemonSets (nvidia, amd, ascend, matched by pci-<vendor>.present under OnDelete). Use cert-manager when rendering manifests offline (helm template | kubectl apply) so repeated syncs do not rotate source TLS certificates.
Remote delivery applies to hub ModelArtifacts on managed vLLM and SGLang roles (nixl on NVIDIA and hixl on Ascend). Take-over roles[].command, PVC, and OCI image artifacts keep their local paths. Treat source Pods and vendor images as trusted cluster infrastructure.
Fallback policies Policy Allowlisted, source ready Allowlisted, source unavailable Outside allowlist Ineligible role Require Loads remote Waits within startup timeout; never downloads Blocked (UnqualifiedTransferBackend) Blocked (RoleIneligibleForModelTransfer) Prefer Loads remote Uses local delivery unless a remote replica is running Falls back unless rolling a loaded replica Falls back to local delivery Under Prefer, failed remote loads recreate the replica and increment fallbackAttempts. After three attempts, reason turns FallbackAttemptsSpent and local Node or Engine delivery runs; loaded remote replicas keep their spec if the source disappears.
Control and payload networks Control traffic uses authenticated broker HTTPS, while payload traffic uses UCX/InfiniBand or shared memory (nixl) and CANN fabric (hixl). Pass NIC selection variables on sources via modelTransfer.env or modelTransfer.extraArgs, and apply RDMA selection policies on serving targets.
Source preparation Add spec.source: {} and explicit placement on a Model Prefetch to pin verified disk weights (status.readyNodes) and register a host-memory source (status.transfer).
Source admission enforces the minimum of three bounds (including 10% reservation overhead): the broker’s node budget, the per-generation resident window, and any shared Binding spec.sourceMemory grant. Checkpoints larger than the window page in batches; the window must fit at least 1 GiB and the largest safetensors shard (shards are never split):
yamlCopy modelTransfer: source: maxMemoryBytes: 0 # 0 uses 1/16 of MemTotal, floored at minMemoryBytes minMemoryBytes: 1073741824 # 1 GiB floor maxSessions: 64 # max concurrent sessions per source Pod workerResources: {} # explicit memory limits must include non-transfer overhead env: GPUSTACK_MODEL_TRANSFER_SOURCE_RESIDENT_BUDGET_BYTES: "0" GPUSTACK_MODEL_TRANSFER_HIXL_RESIDENT_BUDGET_BYTES: "17179869184" # 16 GiB HIXL default Source memory examples Label source Nodes gpustack.ai/model-transfer-source: "true", optionally cap sourceMemory on ModelStoreBinding, and declare source: {} on ModelPrefetch:
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelStoreBinding metadata: name: qwen-source namespace: gpustack-default spec: storeRefs: - name: model-source-pool quota: bytes: 128Gi # disk cache budget (separate from source RAM) allowPinned: true sourceMemory: # optional; omit to use node-derived limits bytes: 64Gi # shared across prefetches, nodes, and vendors; monotonic upward registrations: 4096 # monotonic upward sessions: 64 # editable in both directions --- apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelPrefetch metadata: name: qwen3-8b-source namespace: gpustack-default spec: artifactRef: name: qwen3-8b bindingRef: name: qwen-source placement: nodeSelector: matchLabels: gpustack.ai/model-transfer-source: "true" retention: pinned: true source: {} # registers host-memory source alongside disk cache Model Checkpoint 16 GiB budget Paging behavior Qwen3-8B 15.27 GiB Pages (~14.54 GiB net after 10% overhead) Fits whole when broker budget exceeds ~17.6 GiB. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 66.99 GiB Pages resident batches Window must fit largest shard; 64 GiB Binding grant cannot widen a 16 GiB resident cap. Keep source disk caches intact for page-in and restore. Drain and delete OnDelete source Pods after chart flag or env changes, and keep operator, source SDK, and engine SDK on contract version 2.
Replica startup Remote-enabled replicas mount a metadata-only CSI view (model-transfer.gpustack.ai/delivery: metadata), a gpustack-model-transfer token, and the host-staged wheel when absent. Tune tensor parallelism (TP) mode and target staging RAM in spec.roles[].env:
diffCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeployment metadata: name: qwen3-8b namespace: gpustack-default spec: roles: - kind: Server name: server + env: + - name: GPUSTACK_MODEL_TRANSFER_TP_MODE + value: broadcast # broadcast (or tp0): rank 0 streams and broadcasts; all: every rank opens a session + - name: GPUSTACK_MODEL_TRANSFER_MAX_WINDOW_BYTES + value: "8589934592" # 8 GiB target staging cap (split across ranks in all mode; 1 GiB/rank floor) The client caps pinned staging RAM at the minimum of its window, the source window, and the tensor span. It closes the session after load_weights, retries peers on HTTP 409, and leaves loaded replicas untouched when a source drains.
Hardware requirements Ascend Ascend (hixl) supports vLLM and SGLang on CANN 9.2+ images (remove stale preinstalled gpustack_model_transfer wheels so the host-staged wheel loads). On Ascend A5 (status.detail.family "950"):
UB / UB H2H / UBG / UBoE: Keep modelTransfer.ascend.hostRoCE.enabled: false and target interface: 0. Set ASCEND_GLOBAL_RESOURCE_CONFIG ("comm_resource_config.protocol_desc": ["ub_ctp:host"], ["ub_rtp:device"], or ["uboe:device"]) in modelTransfer.env and roles[].env for non-default UB modes. Host RoCE (roce:host): Prepare Ascend host prerequisites , enable modelTransfer.ascend.hostRoCE.enabled: true on the source DaemonSet, and set resources.interface >= 1 on Server or symmetric prefill/decode (PD) roles (Encode and asymmetric PD are refused): yamlCopy modelTransfer: nodeSelector: ascend.gpustack.ai/generation: a5 # drain non-matching nodes before narrowing; applies to all vendors ascend: hostRoCE: enabled: true # mounts RO /etc/hixlep, enables hostNetwork, and defaults roce:host yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeployment metadata: name: qwen3-8b-a5-roce namespace: gpustack-default spec: model: name: Qwen/Qwen3-8B artifactRef: name: qwen3-8b engine: name: vLLM # vLLM or SGLang on CANN 9.2+ image: example/vllm-ascend:cann9.2 roles: - name: server replicas: 1 acceleratorType: atlas-950 # status.detail.family: "950" resources: accelerator: 1 interface: 1 # grants RDMA, RO /etc/hixlep, and roce:host default NVIDIA NVIDIA (nixl) supports vLLM and SGLang, choosing LIBFABRIC when aws-efa-enabled is true or an attached KVCachePool uses EFA, and UCX otherwise. Supply a custom EFA-built source image in modelTransfer.images.nvidia on AWS EFA clusters.
NVIDIA ModelExpress ModelExpress streams GPU tensors peer-to-peer over NIXL device-to-device (D2D) transfers and shares torch.compile and Triton caches across NVIDIA vLLM and SGLang replicas (HIXL D2D is not supported).
Role configuration Pass --load-format=modelexpress (or mx) in roles[].extraArgs on a Hugging Face-backed role:
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeployment metadata: name: qwen-chat namespace: team-a spec: model: name: Qwen/Qwen3-8B # required artifactRef: name: qwen-weights # required Hugging Face ModelArtifact engine: name: vLLM # required; enum: vLLM, SGLang image: example/engine:tag # required roles: - name: server replicas: 2 acceleratorType: gpustack--nvidia-a10g-linux-amd64 resources: accelerator: 1 extraArgs: - --load-format=modelexpress # mx is also accepted Each TP rank tries RdmaStrategy (NIXL D2D from a matching TP/PP peer) before GpustackLoadStrategy (prefetch source), falling back locally only under Prefer. User MX_* entries in roles[].env override defaults (MX_ARTIFACT_TRANSFER: "0" disables compile-cache sharing).
Metadata server The operator deploys an unauthenticated in-memory gRPC metadata server and Service (<md-name>-modelexpress) in the deployment namespace; restrict network access to trusted Pods. Server restarts clear descriptors without interrupting running replicas; the next replica reloads via GpustackLoadStrategy and re-registers. Pin or mirror the server image via Setting:
yamlCopy apiVersion: gpustack.ai/v1 kind: Setting metadata: name: model-deployment-modelexpress-server-image namespace: gpustack-system # use the system namespace spec: value: gpustack/mirrored-modelexpress-server:v0.8.0 # default image Results Tables compare Weight Transfer Time (slowest rank load) and Target Storage (0 GiB on remote rows) against a cold TCP peer sync + local load phase-sum baseline. Source preparation, scheduling, and warm-up are excluded:
Choose TP0 + broadcast when source RAM is smaller than the checkpoint: Rank 0 streams shards sequentially (1.32×–4.26× faster than the TCP peer sync + local load sum). Exception: do not use TP all under a 16 GiB paged window: concurrent rank paging regresses to 0.28× (1380.52 s vs 393.14 s baseline) on 80B NVIDIA and trails TP0 + broadcast on 35B Ascend (2.79× vs 4.26×). Choose TP all when source RAM holds the full checkpoint: Parallel per-rank sessions cut Weight Transfer Time by 4.84×–16.21× on NVIDIA (eager mode) and 2.57×–7.69× on Ascend (eager mode; confounder: Ascend 235B 16 GiB paged and 256 GiB full-resident runs used different SDK builds). Choose ModelExpress D2D for multi-replica NVIDIA scale-out: Peer D2D loads 235B weights in 16.78 s (66.82× vs the 1121.30 s baseline, 0 GiB host transfer RAM) and cuts torch.compile from 77.67 s to 0.28 s (277.39×), confounded against eager-mode NIXL runs because ModelExpress runs in graph mode (296.82 s → 90.25 s total engine init, 3.29×). Ascend (HIXL) Two Ascend 910B2 Nodes, vLLM-Ascend cann9.2-910b-vllm0.30.0, eager mode (8B = Qwen/Qwen3-8B at TP = 2; 35B = Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and 235B = vllm-ascend/Qwen3-235B-A22B-W8A8 at TP = 8 plus expert parallelism (EP); 235B 16 GiB and 256 GiB rows used different SDK builds):
Model Mode Source RAM Target RAM Target Storage Weight Transfer Time 8B (TP = 2) TCP peer sync + local load (sum) 0 GiB 0 GiB 15.27 GiB 82.90 s (baseline) 8B (TP = 2) TP0 + broadcast (16 GiB source, 8 GiB target) 15.26 GiB 3.72 GiB 0 GiB 15.31 s (5.41×, −81.5% time) 8B (TP = 2) TP all (16 GiB source, 8 GiB target) 15.26 GiB 7.45 GiB 0 GiB 10.78 s (7.69×, −87.0% time) 35B (TP = 8 + EP) TCP peer sync + local load (sum) 0 GiB 0 GiB 66.99 GiB 282.60 s (baseline) 35B (TP = 8 + EP) TP0 + broadcast (16 GiB source, 8 GiB target) 15.66 GiB 3.72 GiB 0 GiB 66.33 s (4.26×, −76.5% time) 35B (TP = 8 + EP) TP all (16 GiB source, 8 GiB target) 15.66 GiB 8.00 GiB 0 GiB 101.39 s (2.79×, −64.1% time) 35B (TP = 8 + EP) TP all (80 GiB source, 64 GiB target) 67.05 GiB 29.81 GiB 0 GiB 46.39 s (6.09×, −83.6% time) 235B (TP = 8 + EP) TCP peer sync + local load (sum) 0 GiB 0 GiB 220.54 GiB 599.05 s (baseline) 235B (TP = 8 + EP) TP0 + broadcast (16 GiB source, 8 GiB target) 15.99 GiB 4.00 GiB 0 GiB 452.83 s (1.32×, −24.4% time) 235B (TP = 8 + EP) TP0 + broadcast (256 GiB source, 32 GiB target) 220.67 GiB 4.00 GiB 0 GiB 253.58 s (2.36×, −57.7% time) 235B (TP = 8 + EP) TP all (256 GiB source, 32 GiB target) 220.67 GiB 32.00 GiB 0 GiB 232.93 s (2.57×, −61.1% time) NVIDIA (NIXL) Nebius H100 80 GB Nodes, vLLM 0.30.0, eager mode (80B = Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8 at TP = 4; 235B = Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507-FP8 at TP = 8 + EP):
Model Mode Source RAM Target RAM Target Storage Weight Transfer Time 80B (TP = 4) TCP peer sync + local load (sum) 0 GiB 0 GiB 76.45 GiB 393.14 s (baseline) 80B (TP = 4) TP0 + broadcast (16 GiB source, 8 GiB target) 16.00 GiB 8.00 GiB 0 GiB 160.59 s (2.45×, −59.2% time) 80B (TP = 4) TP all (16 GiB source, 8 GiB target) 16.00 GiB 8.00 GiB 0 GiB 1380.52 s (0.28×, +251.2% time) 80B (TP = 4) TP all (80 GiB source, 64 GiB target) 76.42 GiB 40.00 GiB 0 GiB 81.16 s (4.84×, −79.4% time) 235B (TP = 8 + EP) TCP peer sync + local load (sum) 0 GiB 0 GiB 220.21 GiB 1121.30 s (baseline) 235B (TP = 8 + EP) TP0 + broadcast (16 GiB source, 8 GiB target) 16.00 GiB 8.00 GiB 0 GiB 287.97 s (3.89×, −74.3% time) 235B (TP = 8 + EP) TP0 + broadcast (256 GiB source, 64 GiB target) 220.19 GiB 9.31 GiB 0 GiB 108.89 s (10.30×, −90.3% time) 235B (TP = 8 + EP) TP all (256 GiB source, 32 GiB target) 220.19 GiB 32.00 GiB 0 GiB 69.16 s (16.21×, −93.8% time) ModelExpress GPU transfers Nebius H100 80 GB Nodes, vLLM 0.30.0, graph mode on 235B (TP8 + EP) (Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507-FP8):
Model Mode Source RAM Target RAM Target Storage Weight Transfer Time 235B (TP8 + EP) TCP peer sync + local load (sum) 0 GiB 0 GiB 220.21 GiB 1121.30 s (baseline) 235B (TP8 + EP) Seed replica: GpustackLoadStrategy (256 GiB source, 8 GiB target) 220.19 GiB 8.00 GiB 0 GiB 232.10 s (4.83×, −79.3% time) 235B (TP8 + EP) Peer replica: RdmaStrategy (NIXL D2D + compile cache) 0 GiB 0 GiB 0 GiB 16.78 s (66.82×, −98.5% time) 235B (TP8 + EP) Restart fallback: GpustackLoadStrategy (256 GiB source, 8 GiB target) 220.19 GiB 8.00 GiB 0 GiB 109.08 s (10.28×, −90.3% time) Verification Inspect per-role and per-replica remote loading state on ModelDeployment:
bashCopy kubectl -n <ns> get modeldeployment <name> -o jsonpath='{.status.model.remote}' | jq status.model.remote echoes the active policy and each replica’s delivery (Remote, Node, or Engine), load (Unknown, AwaitingMetadata, AwaitingSource, Loading, or Loaded), reason, and fallbackAttempts. Source readiness lives on ModelPrefetch (Prefetch status ).
Troubleshooting Observation Cause Resolution SourceWindowFallback (Progressing=True) on prefetch Source grant below 1 GiB floor under Prefer Raise ModelStoreBinding sourceMemory or broker RAM budget. SourceWindowBelowFloor (Progressing=False) on prefetch Source grant below 1 GiB floor under Require Raise ModelStoreBinding sourceMemory or broker maxMemoryBytes. SourceGrantMissing (Progressing=False) on prefetch Missing ModelStoreBinding Create the ModelStoreBinding named in spec.bindingRef. load: AwaitingSource No SourceReady prefetch serves the digest Inspect ModelPrefetch status.transfer and source Pod logs. load: AwaitingMetadata Metadata CSI mount pending Inspect Pod FailedMount events and model.csi.gpustack.ai. RemoteLoadFailed (load: Unknown) Remote load exited; replica recreating Inspect previous container logs and fallbackAttempts. FallbackAttemptsSpent Remote load failed more than 3 times under Prefer Diagnose fallback Node or Engine delivery on the recreated Pod. RoleIneligibleForModelTransfer or UnqualifiedTransferBackend Custom command, unsupported engine, or unallowlisted backend under Require Switch to a managed NVIDIA (nixl) or Ascend (hixl) role, or set policy to Prefer. WeightsReady=False (NodeDeliveryUnavailable) Require active without model.csi.gpustack.ai Enable modelManager.enabled: true or roll back remote policy. Rollback Patch model-artifact-remote-delivery-policy to Disabled (or set modelTransfer.enabled: false in Helm values):
diffCopy apiVersion: gpustack.ai/v1 kind: Setting metadata: name: model-artifact-remote-delivery-policy namespace: gpustack-system spec: - value: Prefer + value: Disabled New replicas revert to model-artifact-delivery-mode (Node or Engine) while already-loaded replicas continue serving until their next rollout.
