title: Remote Weight Delivery

content:
Model Deployment A ModelDeployment declares the model, engine and serving roles of an inference workload. Each role sets its own replicas and accelerator resources.
Contents Overview Configuration Operations Troubleshooting Overview Configuration Model Deployment Configuration defines the base manifest, role fields, override tiers and operator-owned keys. Engine Compatibility lists minimum engine releases, Mooncake versions, supported transports and known limits. Prefill and Decode pairs split prefill/decode (PD) roles; Prefill and Decode Benchmark compares PD against an equal-GPU aggregated group. Encode, Prefill and Decode adds multimodal disaggregation; Encode, Prefill and Decode Benchmark compares encode/prefill/decode (EPD) against PD and aggregated serving. Follow Prefill and Decode Walkthrough , Encode, Prefill and Decode Walkthrough and Multi-Host Serving Walkthrough for step-by-step runs. Operations Online Runtime Control covers live parameter tuning, role pause and retirement windows. Model Deployment Routing covers endpoint eligibility, router defaults and per-worker metrics. Model Deployment Scaling plans replica counts from engine metrics and coordinates graceful retirement. Pair it with Scaling Walkthrough and Scaling Benchmark . Elastic EP grows one running collective in place. Pair it with Elastic EP Walkthrough (tensor parallelism (TP) = 2, data parallelism (DP) width 2 → 4) and Elastic EP Benchmark . External DP exposes one HTTP endpoint per rank behind a managed router. Pair it with External DP Walkthrough and External DP Benchmark . Troubleshooting If a deployment does not become ready, inspect its phase, conditions and role status:
bashCopy kubectl -n <namespace> get modeldeployment <name> -o yaml Match status.phase, conditions and role status against Readiness and status and Model Deployment Routing . For scaling holds, inspect the ModelDeploymentScaler using Scaling Walkthrough .
See also — KV Cache (shared prefix reuse) · Model Delivery (weights)
Next → Model Deployment Configuration — create a serving workload.
title: Model Deployment

content:
Configuration A ModelDeployment runs one or more inference-engine roles, and each role has its own replicas. Roles can share cached prefixes through a KV cache pool, form a direct prefill/decode (PD) pair, or do both.
The operator creates the Pods for each replica. The ModelDeployment webhook checks KV cache transport compatibility. Generated Pods skip KV cache Pod injection, but ordinary Pod admission still applies.
Contents Deployment configuration Engine overrides Rollout behavior Admission refusals Operations Deployment configuration yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeployment # namespaced, short name md metadata: name: qwen-chat namespace: team-a spec: model: name: Qwen/Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct # required; served, never provisioned engine: name: vLLM # required; enum: vLLM, SGLang image: <a runner image your cluster can pull> # required kvCache: # optional; omit to run without a shared pool poolRef: name: team-a-dram # KVCachePoolBinding in this namespace connector: Mooncake # optional, default: Mooncake (the only value); immutable roles: # 1 to 10 roles - name: server replicas: 4 # independent serving instances size: 1 # optional, default: 1; fate-sharing Pods per instance acceleratorType: gpustack--nvidia-a10g-linux-amd64 # omit for a CPU-only role resources: # per Pod accelerator: 2 # cards cpu: "8" # optional ram: 32Gi # optional localStorage: 100Gi # optional ephemeral storage Field Constraints model.name Supply the weights from the hub, role volumes or model.artifactRef (Model Artifact ). resources Mirrors Accelerator Requests . The operator injects only the cpu, ram and localStorage values you set, with no unit preset. acceleratorType If omitted, kube-scheduler places the Pods directly without Kueue, and admission rejects accelerator requests. resources.interface Optional. Requests device.gpustack.ai/rdma.shared for 1, device.gpustack.ai/rdma for > 1, or vpc.amazonaws.com/efa, per Pod. A role that writes to a pool whose every transport is rdma, efa or Ascend A5 Host RoCE needs it, and admission warns when it is unset or 0 on such a role. See Rollout behavior for how edits to replicas and size apply. Request resources.interface only when an effective RDMA or EFA transfer path exists; see RDMA Operations . On Ascend A5 (family "950"), follow Ascend A5 topologies .
Multi-member instances If size is greater than 1, Pods are named <deployment>-<role>-r<replica>-m<member>. Each instance has its own headless Service, and member m0 is the HTTP leader.
The operator reserves GPUSTACK_REPLICA_LEADER_ADDRESS, GPUSTACK_REPLICA_SIZE and GPUSTACK_MEMBER_INDEX at every size. It injects them only when size > 1. Declare the engine parallelism flags yourself.
Prefill and decode Admission handles all roles in one deployment atomically. Each replica forms its own Kueue Pod group. An admission check holds every group until the whole set reserves quota.
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeployment metadata: name: example-model spec: model: name: Qwen/Qwen3-8B engine: name: vLLM image: example/engine:tag roles: - name: prefill # becomes the Kueue PodSet name kind: Prefill # enum: Server (default), Prefill, Decode, Encode replicas: 2 acceleratorType: gpustack--nvidia-h20-linux-amd64 resources: accelerator: 2 - name: decode kind: Decode replicas: 2 acceleratorType: gpustack--nvidia-h20-linux-amd64 resources: accelerator: 2 Only Server roles can repeat a kind under different names. Pass parallelism degrees in roles[].extraArgs, or in roles[].command on a take-over role. Admission parses those degrees and checks them against the card counts. Prefill and Decode covers connectors, spec.router, direct transfer transports and per-role Services.
Topology placement roles[].topology.requiredLevel takes a configured topology label key, such as a region, zone, rack or Topograph level. All size Pods of each replica group must then fit in one domain at that level.
Omit the field for unconstrained placement. kubernetes.io/hostname is implicit, and admission rejects it. A change rolls only that role’s replicas. See Topology-Aware Scheduling Operations .
KV cache reuse domain The reuse domain (name, blockSize, dtype) is an immutable block on the KVCachePoolBinding. ModelDeploymentSpec has no domain field. A workload therefore cannot mint tenants outside its Binding’s quota (Cache reuse domains ).
ModelDeployments that share a Binding share KV. Separate Bindings get separate tenant identifiers. status.kvCache echoes the attached binding, pool and domain block. The operator renders the tenant identifier on managed roles. Select a compatible engine image to enforce isolation (KV Cache Pools and Bindings ). Role images Each replica uses roles[].image if set, then the required spec.engine.image. The operator never infers an image tag from node driver versions. Set a pullable tag that fits the configuration; see Engine Compatibility .
Engine overrides Customize the engine through three tiers. Do not patch rendered Pods.
Tier Trigger Behavior Owned Managed role and operator-owned key Admission rejects owned arguments in roles[].extraArgs (including unique prefixes; on vLLM also underscores and dotted members) and owned variables in roles[].env. Use roles[].command to own the line. Defaulted Managed role and no user value The operator injects --host 0.0.0.0, --port, --served-model-name, compile caches, transfer defaults and tuning variables. A user extraArgs or env entry wins without refusal. Take-over Non-empty roles[].command You own the full argv (there is no args field, and extraArgs is ignored). The operator skips CLI synthesis, KV and transfer client environment, default cache mounts and health probes. It sets status.roles[].unmanaged to true, reports CacheAttached=Unknown and assigns no reuse domain. yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeployment metadata: name: example-model spec: model: name: Qwen/Qwen3-8B engine: name: vLLM image: example/engine:tag roles: - name: server acceleratorType: gpustack--nvidia-h20-linux-amd64 extraArgs: # Defaulted tier: user values win over operator defaults - --enable-prefix-caching env: - name: EXAMPLE value: "true" image: example/engine:tag # optional; overrides spec.engine.image imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent imagePullSecrets: [] privileged: false ports: [] additionalVolumes: [] shmSize: 32Gi # optional; see Shared memory terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30 startupTimeoutSeconds: 1800 # optional, default: 1800; range 10..86400 # command: # optional; triggers Take-over tier # - /usr/local/bin/server Do not pass engine authentication (--api-key or VLLM_API_KEY) in extraArgs. Managed direct decoders probe /v1/models, receive 401 and never become ready. Put north-south authentication at the cluster gateway.
Shared memory spec.roles[].shmSize sets the size of the memory-backed EmptyDir at /dev/shm in the main container. The default is 16Gi. It applies to both engines, take-over roles and Elastic Ray members.
An explicit /dev/shm mount in additionalVolumes takes precedence. Shared memory counts toward the container memory limit but does not raise requests.memory.
Engram host memory If a non-privileged role enables Engram host-memory offload, the operator grants IPC_LOCK and SYS_RESOURCE on the main container. vLLM enables offload through --engram-config with cpu_offload. SGLang enables it through SGLANG_ENABLE_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_TABLE=1.
Compilation cache and timeout Managed roles mount the DirectoryOrCreate HostPath volume gpustack-compile-cache at /var/lib/gpustack/cache. The operator also defaults VLLM_CACHE_ROOT or SGLANG_CACHE_DIR and seven startup cache paths: HF_HUB_CACHE, HF_XET_CACHE, PIP_CACHE_DIR, TORCH_HOME, FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BASE, TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR and TRITON_CACHE_DIR.
HF_HOME credentials stay on container storage. To override the mount, use additionalVolumes. To override a variable, set it in roles[].env.
spec.roles[].startupTimeoutSeconds sets startupProbe.failureThreshold to ceil(startupTimeoutSeconds / 10) at periodSeconds: 10. If cold graph compilation needs more time than the default timeout, raise it.
Operator-owned keys The operator owns each key per engine. Admission refuses these keys in extraArgs and env on a managed role:
Engine Owned arguments Owned environment vLLM --kv-transfer-config, --kv-events-config (including unique prefixes, underscores, and dotted members) MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH, VLLM_MOONCAKE_BOOTSTRAP_PORT, VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_HOST SGLang --hicache-storage-backend, --hicache-storage-backend-extra-config, --disaggregation-mode, --disaggregation-transfer-backend, --disaggregation-bootstrap-port, --kv-events-config (including unique prefixes) SGLANG_HICACHE_MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH, MOONCAKE_MASTER, MOONCAKE_TE_META_DATA_SERVER, MOONCAKE_PROTOCOL, MOONCAKE_DEVICE, MOONCAKE_GLOBAL_SEGMENT_SIZE, MOONCAKE_LOCAL_HOSTNAME, MOONCAKE_TENANT_ID Encoder-stage keys (including vLLM --ec-transfer-config and SGLang encoder flags) are also owned per engine; see Keys the operator owns . --kv-cache-dtype is owned on both engines while spec.kvCache is set and model-deployment-kv-cache-dtype-owned is true (Engine cache precision ). These keys are defaulted, so a user entry wins without refusal: MC_TE_METRIC=1, MC_FORCE_TCP=1 on TCP paths, SGLang hierarchical-cache flags, and compilation and runtime cache paths. Ascend transfer defaults ASCEND_LOCAL_COMM_RES and ASCEND_MF_TRANSFER_PROTOCOL are also defaulted. roles[].env accepts ASCEND_GLOBAL_RESOURCE_CONFIG. vLLM reads its client configuration from /etc/gpustack/kvcache/mooncake.json. The file is a read-only downwardAPI projection, so do not mount an overlay over /etc/gpustack/kvcache. SGLang reads its whole cache configuration from environment variables.
Routed cache-producing vLLM roles (llm-d-router single-Pod DP and vllm-router kv_aware) and SGLang roles behind sgl-router render --kv-events-config on ZMQ ports 5557 and 5558 (or 5557 + dpSpan when dpSpan > 1) and report KVEventsPublishing=True/Publishing. SGLang behind llm-d-router or deprecated sglang-gateway reports KVEventsPublishing=True/NotApplicable.
Rollout behavior A change to replicas adds or removes instances and leaves survivors running. An edit to any field that changes the rendered Pod rolls that role’s replicas. These fields are size, acceleratorType, resources, command, image, extraArgs, env, ports, additionalVolumes, shmSize, terminationGracePeriodSeconds and startupTimeoutSeconds.
Each rollout deletes and recreates one replica per role per pass. It waits for fresh Kueue admission before it deletes the next healthy replica.
A user spec edit changes pod-spec-hash and rolls at once. An operator rendering upgrade changes render-version. Compatible running replicas stay in place, and new Pods use the new rendering.
To move running replicas to a newer rendering baseline on your own schedule, set the minimum render version. When replicas run an older rendering, the ReplicasUpToDate message reports the current render version:
diffCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeployment metadata: name: qwen-chat namespace: team-a + annotations: + modeldeployment.gpustack.ai/min-render-version: "<render version>" # integer Live fields in roles[].runtimeControl.parameters, roles[].pause and mutable spec.router subfields do not roll worker Pods (Online Runtime Control ).
Replacement Pods get fresh names, so select replicas by label:
bashCopy kubectl get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/name=model-deployment,app.kubernetes.io/instance=<deployment> Deployment identity fields Identity fields are frozen. To change one, create a new ModelDeployment. Runtime fields are editable:
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeployment metadata: name: example-model labels: {} # Editable annotations: {} # Editable spec: model: name: Qwen/Qwen3-8B # Frozen loraAdapters: [] # Reserved; non-empty values currently rejected engine: name: vLLM # Frozen image: example/engine:tag # Editable kvCache: # Frozen poolRef: name: cache-binding kvTransfer: {} # Editable router: # Block may be added or removed name: llm-d-router # Frozen in place replicas: 1 # Editable without rolling worker Pods extraArgs: [] # Editable without rolling worker Pods roles: # Role set is frozen - name: server # Frozen kind: Server # Frozen replicas: 1 # Editable pause: false # Editable without rolling worker Pods size: 1 # Editable, except on Elastic EP acceleratorType: gpu-pool # Editable, except on Elastic EP resources: {} # Editable, except on Elastic EP command: [] # Editable, except on Elastic EP runtimeControl: # Editable without rolling Pods; elastic.dataParallelWidth presence frozen parameters: {} extraArgs: [] # Editable env: [] # Editable image: example/engine:tag # Editable shmSize: 32Gi # Editable terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30 # Editable startupTimeoutSeconds: 1800 # Editable Use JSON patch for one role field. kubectl patch --type=merge replaces the whole roles array. It drops omitted fields and can reset kind to Server. Patch one field with JSON patch, or restate the full role:
bashCopy kubectl patch modeldeployment qwen-chat -n team-a --type=json \ -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/roles/0/size","value":2}]' Replica admission groups For an accelerated role, each replica is its own Kueue Pod group with one Workload of total size size. CPU-only roles bypass Kueue.
Scale-down removes the highest ordinals first. It deletes each departing replica’s Pods and Workload together, which releases quota and finalizers.
Admission refusals Schema and validating webhook checks reject these configurations at apply time:
Category Rejected cases Role structure > 10 roles, duplicate role name, replicas > 1024, size > 64, kind: Server mixed with other kinds, frozen identity edits, DNS-1035 / colliding <deployment>-<role> Service names, unnameable members Resources and placement Unsupported accelerator mode or whole-card count over pool capacity, accelerator request without acceleratorType, slice percentage paired with partition profile, PD both logically slicing the same group, invalid topology.requiredLevel Transfer and interfaces Negative/fractional or unsupported resources.interface, incompatible kvTransfer.backend (HIXL off Ascend, NIXL on Ascend, mixed Ascend/non-Ascend PD), new binding to mixed-protocol backend Owned keys and ports Owned arguments/env on managed roles (including conditional --kv-cache-dtype; see Operator-owned keys ), --port mismatching first ports entry, reserved listener ports (5557/5558, 8998), unparseable parallel flags or per-member width exceeding cards Rules that read AcceleratorType are skipped during deletion, so a missing type cannot block finalizer removal. If AcceleratorType.status has not converged, admission passes. The deployment then gets a RenderFailed warning Event until the status converges.
Operations Replicas serve on port 8000 unless roles[].ports or --port sets another container port. If you pass only --port, the operator updates the container port and the Service targetPort. The external Service port stays 8000. Managed native-vLLM decoders put routing-proxy on the external port and vLLM on an internal port. Transfer engines pick random ports, so allow ephemeral port ranges in NetworkPolicy. AscendDirect picks ports within ASCEND_BASE_PORT + physical_id * 100. The startup ERROR line "Local segment descriptor not found" is benign on clients. Readiness and status Check the phase and the ROLES summary, such as 1R2S or 1R1E1P1D. Then list the conditions:
bashCopy kubectl -n <namespace> get modeldeployment <name> kubectl -n <namespace> get modeldeployment <name> \ -o jsonpath='{range .status.conditions[*]}{.type}={.status} {.reason}: {.message}{"\n"}{end}' For per-role readiness, read status.roles with -o yaml. Managed roles probe GET /health, or the sentinel endpoints /gpustack/v1/live and /gpustack/v1/ready. So ready counts replicas whose engine answered on all size members.
The operator omits probes for a take-over roles[].command, a custom --host, a conflicting --port, a client-cert --ssl-cert-reqs outside 0/1, or UDP or SCTP ports.
Condition Reason Resolution QuotaReserved Pending, PreemptedInPart, Parked Check pool ClusterQueue capacity and Workload status. Free capacity on PreemptedInPart, or recreate or reactivate Parked sets. QuotaReserved PodGroupIncomplete Inspect missing replica Pods and events. Kueue creates no Workload for missing replicas. QuotaReserved NoQueueInReservedNamespace Recreate the ModelDeployment in a workload namespace. Reserved namespaces have no LocalQueue and never schedule workloads. ReplicasUpToDate UpToDate, RolloutInProgress, ReplacementInProgress, RolloutHeldByCache, RolloutHeldByWeights Wait for one-per-pass turnover. If a rollout is held, repair the KVCachePoolBinding or the ModelArtifact (WeightsReady). RoleKindsReady AllKindsReady, KindsNotReady Inspect Pod logs and events for any role kind (Encode, Prefill, Decode, Server) with zero ready replicas. CacheAttached CacheActive, CacheOperationsFailing, NoObservationAvailable, Unmanaged On CacheOperationsFailing, inspect engine and KVCacheBackend logs. NoObservationAvailable is normal while idle. For RouterReady, EndpointEligibility and per-group router qualification, see Model Deployment Routing .
See also — KV Cache Pools and Bindings (namespace Binding grants and reuse domains) · Elastic EP (in-place collective expansion) · Prefill and Decode (pairing prefill and decode roles) · Accelerator Requests (request fields mirrored in roles[].resources) · Model Deployment Routing (endpoint eligibility and router policies) · Online Runtime Control (live parameter tuning and role pause) · Model Deployment Scaling (ModelDeploymentScaler and graceful retirement).

title: Configuration

content:
Elastic EP Benchmark On one H100 SXM5 node, an expert parallelism (EP) collective expanded in place from four GPUs to eight. At concurrency 64 over TCP, time to first token (TTFT) p50 fell 2.50× (6,509.231 ms to 2,598.867 ms), while single-request generation slowed and output throughput fell in all six cells. The live expansion stream completed 439/439 requests with zero errors.
The initial suites describe cross-Pod TCP. The separate InfiniBand RDMA comparison records the matched follow-up.
Contents Summary Environment Results Verification InfiniBand RDMA comparison Limitations Summary One ModelDeployment (b2-elastic-ep in gpustack-bench) kept tensor parallelism (TP) = 2 per member while data parallelism (DP) width grew from 2 to 4 (EP world size 4 → 8 GPUs). Existing Pods kept their UIDs and zero restart counts. Elastic EP defines the profile and resize contract.
Doubling the GPU count over TCP did not raise throughput. Only one API server accepted requests in both states.
Choose online width growth when process continuity and concurrency-64 first-token relief justify extra GPUs (especially over InfiniBand RDMA, where width 4 also led concurrency-64 output). Choose width 2 on TCP for lower concurrency, throughput and token-generation latency. Even at concurrency 64 on TCP, end-to-end p50 rose at width 4 (11,487.169 to 12,154.350 ms). Benefits Expanded 4 → 8 GPUs in place while keeping the serving master and original GPU worker; live load completed 439/439 requests with zero errors. Cut concurrency-64 TTFT p50 2.50× (6,509.231 to 2,598.867 ms) and TTFT p95 (8,708.596 to 4,789.148 ms). End-to-end p50 still rose from 11,487.169 to 12,154.350 ms at concurrency 64.
Trade-offs Single-request ITL p50 rose 83.0% (8.566 to 15.675 ms), and concurrency-64 ITL p50 rose from 16.522 to 30.270 ms across the four-Pod TCP collective. Output throughput fell in all six TCP cells (109.586 to 61.020 tok/s at concurrency 1; 1,145.131 versus 1,121.379 tok/s at concurrency 64). The capture does not isolate collective, TCP and single-API-server overhead separately.
Environment Item Captured value Cluster Kubernetes v1.35.7; one CPU node and one GPU node Hardware 8 × NVIDIA H100 80 GB HBM3 SXM5 on one node; physical NVLink bandwidth 900 GB/s GPUStack Operator v0.9.1 Runner gpustack/runner:cuda13.0-vllm0.30.0, Ray V2 executor enabled Model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat, revision 85864749cd611b4353ce1decdb286193298f64c7 Model delivery ModelArtifact deepseek-v2-lite-chat, mounted at /models through node delivery Captured InstanceType Custom bench-gpu, selecting the H100 accelerator group Engine limits --max-model-len 8192, --max-num-seqs 16, --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 Collective --all2all-backend allgather_reducescatter, --elastic-ep-max-dp-size 4 Serving --api-server-count 1; no managed Router The deployment used one Server role (replicas: 1, size: 1). Only elastic.dataParallelWidth changed. The CPU Ray head and all GPU members shared one GPU node. See the walkthrough for the manifest and checks.
Each GPU Pod exposed only its two assigned GPUs with private IPC and /dev/shm, hostIPC disabled and no remote direct memory access (RDMA) interface. NVLink carried intra-Pod TP traffic; all cross-Pod EP collective traffic used TCP sockets over eth0.
State Width GPU members GPUs TP EP world size State 1 2 2 4 2 4 State 2 2 → 4 2 → 4 4 → 8 2 4 → 8 State 3 4 4 8 2 8 Results Suite 1: Serving width comparison Each state ran one sweep of target 1,024-input / 256-output-token requests (observed prompts 1,021–1,025 tokens). Concurrency 1, 4 and 8 used 32 requests; concurrency 16 used 64; concurrency 32 and 64 used 128, each excluding four warm-up requests. All 416 measured requests per state completed with zero errors. Output throughput divides actual generated tokens by cell wall time.
Over TCP with one API server, width 4 (8 GPUs) beat width 2 (4 GPUs) on TTFT only at concurrency 64 (2.50× lower TTFT p50: 6,509.231 to 2,598.867 ms; TTFT p95 8,708.596 to 4,789.148 ms), with ITL p99 nearly flat (157.753 versus 155.538 ms).
Across all six concurrencies, width 4 slowed ITL p50 (up 83.0% at concurrency 1: 8.566 to 15.675 ms) and lowered output throughput, and end-to-end p50 still rose at concurrency 64 (11,487.169 to 12,154.350 ms).
Time per output token (TPOT) measures per-request generation time per token; inter-token latency (ITL) measures streamed-token gaps. Bold values mark lower latency or higher throughput within each matched pair.
Concurrency Width GPUs Requests TTFT p50 (ms) TTFT p95 (ms) TPOT p50 (ms) ITL p50 (ms) ITL p99 (ms) Output (tok/s) 1 2 4 32/32 108.853 137.983 8.531 8.566 9.134 109.586 1 4 8 32/32 167.142 189.872 15.687 15.675 17.600 61.020 4 2 4 32/32 153.733 340.863 9.912 8.651 12.290 352.630 4 4 8 32/32 219.585 1,022.254 16.898 15.941 19.204 214.606 8 2 4 32/32 263.820 628.698 12.773 11.279 88.721 524.388 8 4 8 32/32 328.685 779.087 22.957 22.430 132.667 307.574 16 2 4 64/64 384.459 1,090.247 17.781 15.178 91.049 751.199 16 4 8 64/64 502.015 1,454.118 29.047 23.305 141.867 470.798 32 2 4 128/128 660.074 2,118.262 23.106 16.109 99.608 1,140.701 32 4 8 128/128 1,096.666 2,645.267 36.916 29.288 156.532 721.243 64 2 4 128/128 6,509.231 8,708.596 22.780 16.522 157.753 1,145.131 64 4 8 128/128 2,598.867 4,789.148 38.357 30.270 155.538 1,121.379 Live resize A concurrency-8 stream (1,024/256 shape) ran across the width 2 → 4 patch and completed 439/439 requests in 264.227 seconds (264.23 s) with zero client errors. The capture recorded zero client-facing HTTP 503 responses and 10 /health HTTP 503 responses on the master during re-rendezvous.
Observation Captured result Phase check 12 seconds from patch submission; the harness still read Ready while serving continued Role readiness About 189 seconds from the patch to RoleKindsReady and EndpointEligibility becoming True Final native width Desired, admitted, allocated, Ray and effective width all known at 4 Final phase Ready, with one desired and one ready replica group Existing Pods CPU Ray head, serving master and existing GPU member retained Container restarts 0 across all five final Pods Added members 2 GPU Pods, each with 2 GPUs Client completion 439/439; 0 errors The 12-second timer checked phase only, not effective-width convergence. The patch arrived at 08:16:11Z, and RoleKindsReady and EndpointEligibility became True at 08:19:20Z (about 189 seconds later), covering startup and Ray join for the two new GPU Pods. Final observation.json confirmed effective width 4 without a convergence timestamp.
The watch capture polled every 16–21 seconds (up to 28 seconds):
Time (UTC) Phase Role summary 08:18:50Z Ready 1S 08:19:09Z Starting 0S 08:19:30Z Ready 1S The Starting sample fell between Ready samples 40 seconds apart, so the exact withdrawal duration is unknown. See the walkthrough for effective-width verification.
Verification Final observation reported generation 2, stable width 4 and reason native ranks and forwards agree. ReplicasUpToDate stayed Unknown/RolloutNotObserved. The master, CPU head and original GPU worker kept their UIDs and zero restart counts.
Master completion access logs rose from 880 before State 3 to 1,320 at finish (including warm-up and calibration). No Router was configured; client JSON establishes completion and errors. After deletion, Devices reported all eight H100 GPUs with remaining = 1600000.
A later runtime-acceptance run repeated width 2 → 4 on an eight-GPU H100 node:
Observation Captured result Ready at width 2 about two minutes after the apply State-1 sweep six concurrency cells, zero errors Load through the resize 471 requests over 260 seconds, zero errors Width patch 2 → 4 to Ready ten seconds Ray cluster three active nodes and four GPUs → five nodes and eight GPUs Final observation effective width 4, stable width 4, reason native ranks and forwards agree ElasticResize condition True / NoRefusal State-3 sweep six concurrency cells at width 4, zero errors The operator deletes the operation record after completion, leaving terminal state in the condition and observation. An earlier attempt on the same image did not converge and remains unexplained.
InfiniBand RDMA comparison A follow-up on the ConnectX-7 InfiniBand node from Prefill and Decode Benchmark expanded width 2 → 4 at TP = 2. Selected final cells completed 416/416 requests per width with zero errors.
Transport verification Update elastic-ep.yaml from the TCP walkthrough (the diff shows current interface allocation; the capture used manual device exposure):
diffCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeployment metadata: name: b2-elastic-ep namespace: gpustack-bench spec: roles: - name: server kind: Server size: 1 resources: accelerator: "2" + interface: "2" runtimeControl: parameters: elastic.dataParallelWidth: "2" extraArgs: - --gpu-memory-utilization - - "0.90" + - "0.85" NCCL logged Using network IB with GPU Direct RDMA enabled, moving the cross-Pod allgather_reducescatter collective onto InfiniBand while intra-Pod TP stayed on NVLink. Because --gpu-memory-utilization also changed (0.90 → 0.85), the runs do not isolate transport alone.
RDMA serving widths In this separate InfiniBand follow-up (--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85), RDMA cut width-4 concurrency-64 TTFT p50 6.96× (2,598.867 to 373.486 ms), raised output 3.35× (1,121.379 to 3,755.290 tok/s) and cut ITL p50 (30.270 to 10.838 ms). Within RDMA at concurrency 64, width 4 beat width 2 by 8.23× on TTFT p50 and 1.64× on output, reversing TCP.
Exceptions remain: width 2 kept higher RDMA output at concurrencies 1–32 and lower single-request ITL p50 (6.111 versus 6.979 ms), and RDMA width 2, concurrency 4 regressed ITL p99 from 12.290 to 68.396 ms.
Bold values mark lower latency or higher throughput within each matched TCP/RDMA pair at the same width. The width-4 sweep ran twice; the table records the second pass.
Width Concurrency TCP TTFT p50 (ms) RDMA TTFT p50 (ms) TCP ITL p50 (ms) RDMA ITL p50 (ms) TCP ITL p99 (ms) RDMA ITL p99 (ms) TCP output (tok/s) RDMA output (tok/s) 2 1 108.853 87.879 8.566 6.111 9.134 8.765 109.586 151.749 2 4 153.733 89.464 8.651 6.312 12.290 68.396 352.630 502.750 2 8 263.820 91.644 11.279 7.049 88.721 69.554 524.388 813.467 2 16 384.459 221.884 15.178 8.062 91.049 70.393 751.199 1,469.541 2 32 660.074 195.639 16.109 8.759 99.608 74.344 1,140.701 2,343.859 2 64 6,509.231 3,073.825 16.522 8.823 157.753 75.314 1,145.131 2,292.536 4 1 167.142 94.186 15.675 6.979 17.600 9.336 61.020 133.567 4 4 219.585 153.424 15.941 7.146 19.204 12.235 214.606 473.118 4 8 328.685 119.673 22.430 8.302 132.667 73.833 307.574 687.993 4 16 502.015 190.883 23.305 8.905 141.867 79.967 470.798 1,322.207 4 32 1,096.666 185.406 29.288 10.088 156.532 76.300 721.243 2,000.530 4 64 2,598.867 373.486 30.270 10.838 155.538 81.544 1,121.379 3,755.290 Resize verification Live expansion load completed 813/813 requests in 261.794 seconds with zero errors. Surviving Pods kept their UIDs with zero restarts across all five final Pods, and generation-2 observation confirmed effective and stable width 4.
Observation Captured interval New GPU Pods created About 5 seconds after the patch Both new workers registered with Ray About 13 seconds after the patch RoleKindsReady and EndpointEligibility became True About 167 seconds after the patch Final observation Effective width 4; exact convergence time not recorded Ray registration does not prove collective readiness. The harness timer polled a missing current_width field, so its 748-second value is not a convergence time; read effective.Value and stableWidth instead. The 2,134 total completion lines span width 2, expansion load and both width-4 passes.
RDMA width trade-offs Choose RDMA width 4 for high-concurrency peaks (concurrency 64), where it led both TTFT and output throughput. Choose RDMA width 2 for concurrencies 1–32 or lowest single-request ITL p50. The follow-up supports high-concurrency InfiniBand expansion without proving linear scaling or transport-only causality.
Limitations Single-node H100 captures with one sweep per width give no confidence intervals for small deltas. State 1 used four GPUs and State 3 used eight (in-place capacity growth, not equal-GPU efficiency). Only width 2 → 4 at TP = 2 ran; cross-node expansion, other collectives and scale-down were not tested. Neither capture measures cross-Pod NVLink or isolates transport cost from collective size and memory-utilization changes. Single-API-server internal load balancing (Internal LB) ran; per-rank HTTP serving was not measured here. The 12-second phase check is not an effective-width timer; zero client errors do not guarantee uninterrupted readiness or stable token gaps during every resize. Retained UIDs and restart counts prove Pod continuity, not unchanged engine internals; Ready does not imply every condition was true. See also — Elastic EP (profile and resize contract) · Elastic EP Walkthrough (manifest and effective-width verification) · Prefill and Decode Benchmark (equal-GPU disaggregation measurements)

title: Elastic EP Benchmark

content:
Elastic EP An elastic expert parallelism (Elastic EP) deployment keeps one vLLM serving instance and expands its GPU collective in place inside one Ray cluster without restarting surviving Pods. The operator creates a CPU-only Ray head Pod (--num-gpus=0) and Service alongside whole-GPU master and worker Pods whose readiness checks verify TP, allocated devices, and Pod identity.
Contents Configuration Resize procedure Troubleshooting Limitations Configuration yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeployment metadata: name: qwen3-ep namespace: gpustack spec: model: name: Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B artifactRef: name: qwen3-30b-a3b-artifact router: name: llm-d-router engine: name: vLLM image: gpustack/runner:cuda13.0-vllm0.30.0 roles: - name: server kind: Server replicas: 1 size: 1 acceleratorType: elastic-gpu resources: accelerator: "1" # defaults to declared TP size (1 here) when omitted runtimeControl: parameters: elastic.dataParallelWidth: "2" extraArgs: - --elastic-ep-max-dp-size - "4" # required on vLLM 0.30.0+ to allow expansion up to width 4 ports: - name: http port: 8000 protocol: TCP Engine image: Use a vLLM image with a full Ray installation matching your mixture of experts (MoE) model and single-node TP width (see Elastic EP Walkthrough and Elastic EP Benchmark ). CPU Ray head: Created without AcceleratorType, LocalQueue, or container resource requests (namespace LimitRange rules still apply). Weights: Delivered through standard ModelArtifact and node cache paths (Model Delivery ). Explicit TP and resources: For TP = 2, set --tensor-parallel-size 2 and resources.accelerator: "2" (or omit accelerator to default to TP). Explicit values must equal TP; CPU and RAM never auto-scale. Fabric: Optional resources.interface enables RDMA or EFA; see InfiniBand RDMA comparison . Elastic EP settings Set roles[].runtimeControl.parameters["elastic.dataParallelWidth"] to a string integer from "2" to "64" to select Elastic EP:
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeployment metadata: name: deepseek-ep namespace: gpustack spec: model: name: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1 engine: name: vLLM # required; SGLang is not supported image: gpustack/runner:cuda13.0-vllm0.30.0 roles: - name: server acceleratorType: elastic-gpu runtimeControl: parameters: elastic.dataParallelWidth: "4" # target DP engines ("2".."64"), including master elastic.dataParallelWidth counts data parallelism (DP) engines (one GPU Pod each, including the HTTP master). Total GPU demand is width × TP, where tensor parallelism (TP) comes from --tensor-parallel-size in extraArgs (default 1).
Admission freezes and enforces these profile rules once created:
Single managed role: Exactly one Server role with replicas: 1, size: 1, and no custom command. Whole-GPU members: Each member requests TP whole unsliced GPUs inside one Pod and one Ray node; pipeline and prefill context parallel sizes stay 1. Frozen fields: Profile presence, effective TP, size, acceleratorType and resources cannot change after creation. Only elastic.dataParallelWidth changes (scale-up or unchanged only; width decreases are refused, tracked in #741 ). Master HTTP ingress: Only member 0 serves HTTP; workers join Ray and hold expert parallelism (EP) collective state. Shared memory The CPU head, master and each GPU worker mount a separate /dev/shm EmptyDir. Changing roles[].shmSize affects new or replacement Pods only; see Shared memory .
Maximum width On vLLM 0.30.0+, declare --elastic-ep-max-dp-size in extraArgs at creation to permit future expansion (immutable after creation; omitting it blocks growth past the initial width, and older vLLM releases reject the flag).
Resize procedure Patch only elastic.dataParallelWidth and wait for convergence before submitting another change:
diffCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeployment metadata: name: qwen3-ep namespace: gpustack spec: roles: - name: server runtimeControl: parameters: - elastic.dataParallelWidth: "2" + elastic.dataParallelWidth: "4" bashCopy kubectl patch modeldeployment qwen3-ep -n gpustack --type=json \ -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/roles/0/runtimeControl/parameters/elastic.dataParallelWidth","value":"4"}]' The operator retains the master’s command, UID and bootstrap width while adding GPU workers around it. If quota, GPU allocation or Ray membership is incomplete, the resize holds while the running master keeps serving.
Resize status The operator tracks five layers independently in a deployment-owned diagnostic ConfigMap (observation.json, each layer carrying Known, Value and Reason):
Observation Meaning desired Width requested in spec admitted Members admitted by Kubernetes and Kueue allocated Members holding verified whole-GPU allocations Ray Members joined to the Ray cluster effective Width proved by runtime identities and rank forwards Layers legitimately diverge mid-resize; unreadable layers report Known: false rather than copying a neighbor. During native resize, the engine returns HTTP 503: liveness accepts 200 and 503 to avoid restarts, while readiness withdraws to shield traffic.
Resize hold conditions The operator records intent before sending a resize request to the engine:
Ambiguous send (timeout / controller restart): Never resent automatically, preventing double application. Recovery waits for live observation proof. Definite refusal (408, 5xx, busy 503, rejected command): Retried with exponential backoff (15 s initial, doubling up to 4 min, max 5 attempts) only when the engine reports it is not mid-resize. After five refusals, ElasticResize turns False (ScaleRefused) with the engine’s last refusal. Common holds: Pending quota/allocation/Ray join, unreadable actor state, a newer spec generation arriving over an unresolved operation, or an ambiguous send. Automatic recovery: A narrower spec retires a stale widening hold, and full member loss re-derives state once the spec advances and live native width is proved. Partial survival holds until live proof clears. Troubleshooting Signal Owner Action ElasticResize=False (ScaleRefused) ModelDeployment / engine Read the condition message for the engine’s last refusal, inspect master Pod logs and fix the engine/flag constraint. ElasticResize=Unknown (WorldUnprovable) ModelDeployment / observation Inspect the deployment-owned observation.json ConfigMap and verify master/Ray reachability so live width can be proved. admitted lags desired Kueue / ClusterQueue Inspect QuotaReserved (Readiness and status ) and pool queue capacity. Ray lags allocated Ray worker Pods Check joining worker Pod logs (kubectl logs) for Ray head connection errors. effective lags Ray vLLM master Pod Do not resend after an ambiguous timeout; inspect master logs and /gpustack/v1/ready to confirm reported width. Ray logs The Ray head and GPU workers stream Ray logs to stdout/stderr at info level (kubectl logs). Set these variables in roles[].env before creation (edits apply only to new Pods, not existing elastic Pods):
Variable Default Scope RAY_LOG_TO_STDERR 1 Ray system logs (0 writes Ray log files instead) RAY_LOGGER_LEVEL info Python components (debug, info, warning, error, critical) RAY_BACKEND_LOG_LEVEL info C++ components (trace, debug, info, warning, error, fatal) RAY_DEDUP_LOGS Ray default Set 0 to disable driver log deduplication Set VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL separately for vLLM logs on GPU members.
Limitations Supports managed vLLM with a full Ray installation only; SGLang uses ordinary replica scaling. Width range is 2–64; scale-down is rejected at admission (#741 ), and only a pre-existing in-flight narrowing can complete. A resize affects only the patched ModelDeployment; sibling deployments keep serving their own endpoints. Profile presence, TP, size, acceleratorType and resources are frozen after creation. One serving instance per deployment (replicas: 1, size: 1); only member 0 serves HTTP. Adds GPU Pods on existing cluster capacity; it does not provision cloud nodes. See also — Model Deployment Configuration (role contract and status conditions) · Prefill and Decode (disaggregated role pairing) · Model Deployment Routing (replica selection and observations) · Online Runtime Control (live parameter replay, role pause and drain) · Elastic EP Benchmark (measured width change under load)

Encode, Prefill and Decode Benchmark On one H100 SXM5 node, encode/prefill/decode (EPD) cut long-prompt generation stalls and repeated-image latency relative to aggregated serving and prefill/decode (PD). Aggregated serving, PD and EPD used one, two and three GPUs, respectively, so these results compare unequal GPU budgets.
At 8k and concurrency 8 over TCP, EPD cut inter-token latency (ITL) p99 by 21.8× (296.710 ms to 13.607 ms) while raising time to first token (TTFT) p50 (3,963.085 to 4,182.324 ms). Encode, Prefill and Decode defines the role contract.
The initial suites describe cross-Pod TCP. The separate InfiniBand RDMA comparison records the matched follow-up.
Contents Summary Environment Results Verification InfiniBand RDMA comparison Limitations Summary Choose EPD when three GPUs are available and large-image generation isolation, repeated-image reuse or mixed vision/decode latency matters most. Choose aggregated when one GPU or small-prompt first-token latency matters most; cross-role TCP transfers and unequal GPU budgets prevent an equal-cost claim. Benefits Long-prompt ITL p99 fell 15.1×–21.8× at 4k and 8k, concurrency 8, against aggregated serving. Repeated-image traffic reached 536.280 tok/s at concurrency 8 with 5.9× lower TTFT p50. Mixed traffic finished in 5.217 s versus 8.473 s for aggregated serving, with lower TTFT and ITL tails. Trade-offs EPD allocated three GPUs, versus one for aggregated serving and two for PD. Small prompts (1k) favored aggregated serving on first-token latency in every cell. Over TCP at 8k, concurrency 8, EPD TTFT p50 stayed higher than aggregated serving despite much lower ITL p99. Environment Property Captured value Cluster Kubernetes v1.35.7; one CPU node and one GPU node Hardware 8 × NVIDIA H100 80 GB HBM3 SXM5 on one node GPUStack Operator v0.9.1 Captured InstanceType bench-gpu, selecting the H100 accelerator group Runner gpustack/runner:cuda13.0-vllm0.30.0 Router gpustack/llm-router:v0.3.1; disaggregation sidecar v0.11.0 Model Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct, revision cc594898137f460bfe9f0759e9844b3ce807cfb5 Model delivery ModelArtifact qwen2-5-vl-7b-instruct; node delivery mount /var/lib/gpustack/model, served as /models Engine limits --max-model-len 16384, --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 Parallelism Tensor parallelism (TP) = 1 per role The operator added --enforce-eager and --no-enable-prefix-caching only to Encode. Prefill and Decode retained CUDA graphs. Aggregated serving and PD set --enable-scale-out for router token rendering; EPD did not.
Configuration Each configuration ran one ModelDeployment on gpu-node-0 with one replica per role and one GPU per Pod.
Configuration Roles GPUs KV connector Encoder connector Aggregated 1 Server 1 None None PD 1 Prefill + 1 Decode 2 MooncakeConnector, TCP None EPD 1 Encode + 1 Prefill + 1 Decode 3 MooncakeConnector, TCP ECCPUConnector, NIXL Each Pod exposed only its assigned GPU with a private /dev/shm and IPC namespace. hostIPC was disabled, and no remote direct memory access (RDMA) interface was attached. All cross-Pod NIXL encoder-cache and Mooncake KV transfers used TCP sockets over eth0. Host NVLink carried no cross-role traffic.
Variable image sizes Suite 1 varied image and text length with a 128-token completion limit. Image dimensions are pixels; text-token values are generator targets. Measured prompts include multimodal formatting.
Context Image Text target Measured prompt tokens 1k 560 × 560 624 1,047–1,050 2k 840 × 840 1,148 2,071–2,074 4k 1260 × 1260 2,071 4,119–4,122 8k 1792 × 1792 4,096 8,215–8,219 Concurrency 1, 4 and 8 used 8, 12 and 24 measured requests per context, respectively.
Concurrent vision and decode Two streams ran concurrently, with four workers and twelve requests each. The small stream used unique 560 × 560 images, a 624-token text target and max_tokens=256. The heavy-vision stream used unique 1792 × 1792 images, a 400-token text target and max_tokens=64. Measured prompt lengths were 1,048–1,051 and 4,520–4,523 tokens, respectively.
Repeated images Suite 3 reused one 1792 × 1792 image with a different question per request. It used a 400-token text target and max_tokens=64; measured prompts held 4,518–4,522 tokens. Concurrency 4 and 8 used 12 and 24 measured requests.
Measurement method The in-cluster load generator ran each configuration once, sequentially, on the same node. Two warm-up requests preceded every Suite 1 and Suite 3 cell and were excluded from latency summaries. The 45 result files hold 36 Suite 1 cells, three mixed-load runs and six repeated-image cells.
All 708 measured requests succeeded with zero errors, 236 per configuration, plus 28 warm-up requests each. Time per output token (TPOT) measures per-request generation time per token; ITL measures gaps between streamed tokens. Bold values mark lower latency or higher throughput within each matched workload and concurrency.
Results Suite 1: Multimodal context scaling Over TCP with unequal GPU budgets (1, 2 and 3 GPUs), EPD cut ITL p99 by 15.1×–21.8× against aggregated serving at 4k and 8k, concurrency 8 (231.453 to 15.352 ms; 296.710 to 13.607 ms).
EPD has no universal latency win: 1-GPU aggregated serving kept lower TTFT p50 in every 1k cell, lower TTFT p95 in every 2k cell, and lower TTFT p50 at 8k, concurrency 8 (3,963.085 versus 4,182.324 ms), while 8k, concurrency 4 lowered EPD median TTFT but worsened TTFT p95.

title: Encode, Prefill and Decode Benchmark

content:
Encode, Prefill and Decode An encode/prefill/decode (EPD) deployment separates visual encoding from language generation across three roles: multimodal requests traverse Encode → Prefill → Decode (Encode allocates no KV cache and loads no language weights), while text-only requests skip Encode. See Model Deployment Configuration for base role fields and admission rules.
Contents Configuration Supported serving configurations Encoder-cache connectors Operations Results Configuration yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeployment metadata: name: qwen-vl-epd namespace: team-a spec: model: name: Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct engine: name: vLLM # enum: vLLM, SGLang image: gpustack/runner:cuda13.0-vllm0.30.0 # must meet the admitted matrix version floor router: name: llm-d-router # required to pair Encode, Prefill and Decode roles: - name: encode kind: Encode replicas: 1 acceleratorType: gpustack--nvidia-h100-80gb-hbm3-linux-amd64 resources: accelerator: "1" # defaults to 1 on an accelerated AcceleratorType - name: prefill kind: Prefill replicas: 1 acceleratorType: gpustack--nvidia-h100-80gb-hbm3-linux-amd64 resources: accelerator: "1" - name: decode kind: Decode replicas: 1 acceleratorType: gpustack--nvidia-h100-80gb-hbm3-linux-amd64 resources: accelerator: "1" The operator injects the encoder-cache and KV-transfer connectors and attaches the decode routing sidecar where needed. On vLLM Encode, the operator defaults --mm-encoder-only, --enforce-eager and --no-enable-prefix-caching; Prefill and Decode keep CUDA graphs enabled. See EPD Walkthrough for deployment steps and multimodal checks.
Admission constraints Admission enforces every rule below except the image version floor:
Role triad: An Encode role requires one Prefill role, one Decode role, at most one role per kind, and no Server role. Router required: Set spec.router; omitting it fails admission. No shared KV pool: spec.kvCache is refused because Encode keeps no KV cache. Managed roles only: roles[].command is refused on all three roles. Uniform platform: All three roles must resolve to the same accelerator manufacturer from their AcceleratorType; mixed or unknown platforms are refused. Single-Pod encoder: Encode requires size: 1 and refuses elastic expert parallelism (Elastic EP) and external data parallelism (External DP). Image version floor: Pick an image meeting the matching row in Supported serving configurations ; admission does not read image tags. Supported serving configurations Admission accepts only these combinations:
Router Engine Platform Encoder transfer Minimum version llm-d-router vLLM nvidia ECCPUConnector over NIXL 0.30.0 llm-d-router vLLM amd (ROCm) ECCPUConnector over NIXL 0.30.0 llm-d-router vLLM ascend ECExampleConnector over shared volume 0.30.0rc1 vllm-router vLLM nvidia ECCPUConnector over NIXL 0.30.0 vllm-router vLLM amd (ROCm) ECCPUConnector over NIXL 0.30.0 llm-d-router SGLang nvidia encoder-urls 0.5.10 llm-d-router SGLang amd (ROCm) encoder-urls 0.5.10 llm-d-router SGLang ascend encoder-urls 0.5.10 sgl-router SGLang nvidia encoder-urls 0.5.10 sgl-router SGLang amd (ROCm) encoder-urls 0.5.10 sgl-router SGLang ascend encoder-urls 0.5.10 sglang-gateway SGLang nvidia encoder-urls 0.5.10 sglang-gateway SGLang amd (ROCm) encoder-urls 0.5.10 sglang-gateway SGLang ascend encoder-urls 0.5.10 Version and configuration limits Apply the image floor to spec.engine.image or roles[].image. Unlike text-only prefill/decode (PD), llm-d-router uses its built-in token estimator for EPD, so do not add --enable-scale-out (Router token counting ). See Router compatibility for explicit parallelism flag rules.
NVIDIA and AMD vLLM Runs ECCPUConnector over NIXL behind llm-d-router or vllm-router with no shared volume. See NIXL embedding transfer for buffer and port rules.
vLLM on Ascend Uses ECExampleConnector over a shared volume because Ascend lacks a NIXL host-copy path. vLLM-Ascend 0.30.0rc1 is the floor for clean --mm-encoder-only startup and per-rank NPU cache pinning under tensor parallelism (TP). Published 910B tag: cann9.1-910b-vllm0.30.0; set roles[].image for other Ascend variants.
SGLang SGLang uses address-based encoding without an encoder-cache connector. Encode runs --encoder-only; Prefill runs --language-only and dials --encoder-urls (the Encode Service), listening on registration port 8997 (reserved by admission on Prefill) with widened startup probes.
Send traffic only to status.endpoint (the router Service). The plain deployment Service (<name>) hits Prefill directly without a router bootstrap_room, returning HTTP 400 (Invalid bootstrap_room) on SGLang 0.5.18.
Unsupported configurations Candidate Status ECMooncakeConnector Refused: requires static prefiller addresses and unsupported by decode sidecar ECMemcacheConnector Not configured by operator ECCPUConnector on Ascend Refused: no NPU-to-host NIXL copy path or NIXL package vllm-router on Ascend Refused: vLLM-Ascend requires llm-d-router’s nixlv2 decode sidecar Encoder-cache connectors Shared volume transfer ECExampleConnector passes embeddings through a shared ReadWriteMany PVC attached via roles[].additionalVolumes on both Encode and Prefill with matching claimName, mountPath and subPath. Keep the Encode mount writable (readOnly: false).
The connector has no file locking or expiry, and storage latency adds transfer delay. The operator omits VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER because vLLM-Ascend V2 has no multimodal encoder path.
NIXL embedding transfer ECCPUConnector transfers embeddings between Pods over NIXL. The operator defaults VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 on both roles for vLLM < 0.34.0 (omitted at >= 0.34.0, where the variable was removed upstream) and renders an untuned 1 GiB host buffer (ec_cpu_bytes) in --ec-transfer-config.
Encode sets VLLM_EC_SIDE_CHANNEL_HOST to status.podIP and defaults VLLM_EC_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT=5601 (overridable in roles[].env, including 0 for an ephemeral port). Admission checks HTTP port conflicts on Encode (ports or --port) against the effective side-channel port (skipping the check when 0); ECExampleConnector reserves no side-channel port.
Operator-owned keys Admission refuses operator-owned encoder keys in any spelling the engine accepts (see Operator-owned keys ):
vLLM: --ec-transfer-config, plus VLLM_EC_SIDE_CHANNEL_HOST under ECCPUConnector (VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER and VLLM_EC_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT are defaulted, not owned). SGLang: --encoder-only, --language-only, --encoder-urls and --encoder-bootstrap-port. Four vLLM Encode flags are defaulted (user extraArgs wins): --enforce-eager, --no-enable-prefix-caching, --max-num-batched-tokens and --mm-encoder-only. --enforce-eager avoids empty language-model graph capture on V1 GPUModelRunner (ECExampleConnector) and is never defaulted on Prefill, Decode or Server; do not copy it onto language roles.
Operations Role placement preferences Deployments with an Encode role add soft hostname anti-spread preferences (matching modeldeployment.gpustack.ai/role-kind within the deployment); tight clusters still schedule across nodes:
Replica Co-location target Weight Prefill Decode 100 Decode Prefill 100 Encode Prefill 50 Prefill Encode 50 Prefill and Decode exchange KV cache on every request and get higher weight than Encode → Prefill embeddings. Deployments without Encode render no affinity.
Request routing across roles Send client traffic to status.endpoint. Encode Pods are excluded from the deployment Service, status.endpoint and KV-event discovery:
llm-d-router + vLLM: Selects an encoder for media requests; the decode sidecar coordinates transfer. vllm-router + vLLM: Drives Encode, Prefill and Decode directly via --epd-config. SGLang: Prefill calls Encode directly; the router adds no Encode stage. See Encode stage routing for full router behavior.
Replica drain and retirement Encode exports no in-flight request gauges, so retirement uses a fixed window: 30 s withdrawal, 240 s drain (Draining) and 30 s settle before Pod deletion. Transfers still in flight when the window ends fail at the client.
Deployment upgrades Upgrading the operator does not roll existing Server or PD deployments without an Encode role. Role kinds are frozen after creation; create a new ModelDeployment to adopt EPD.
Results An 8 × NVIDIA H100 80 GB HBM3 capture compared 1-GPU aggregated serving, 2-GPU PD and 3-GPU EPD over TCP and ConnectX-7 InfiniBand RDMA. Under small uniform prompts, 1-GPU aggregated serving kept the lowest first-token latency and highest per-GPU efficiency, while EPD isolated heavy vision encoding and cut long-prompt ITL tails. See Encode, Prefill and Decode Benchmark .

Engine Compatibility Verify engine, Mooncake and transport compatibility before choosing container images. Engines below the listed minimums are unsupported. Upgrade before diagnosing failures on an older engine release.
Contents Minimum versions Engine version resolution Transport compatibility Remote weight loading Limitations Minimum versions The matrix covers aggregated serving, prefill/decode (PD) and encode/prefill/decode (EPD) configurations.
Engine Configuration Minimum Mooncake client Store members vLLM alone 0.29.0; behind llm-d-router, --enable-scale-out is also required on 0.30.0+ 0.3.13.post1, on the cuda12.9 and the cuda13.0 tag — vLLM prefill/decode, direct transfer over tcp 0.29.0; behind llm-d-router, --enable-scale-out is also required on 0.30.0+ 0.3.13.post1 — vLLM with a Mooncake store, alone or as a pair 0.29.0; behind llm-d-router, --enable-scale-out is also required on 0.30.0+ 0.3.13.post1 the 0.3.13 line; the default store image is one vLLM-Ascend alone 0.23.0; behind llm-d-router, --enable-scale-out is also required on 0.30.0rc1+ 0.3.11.post1, the NPU build — vLLM-Ascend prefill/decode, direct transfer 0.23.0, behind llm-d-router; --enable-scale-out is also required on 0.30.0rc1+ 0.3.11.post1, the NPU build — SGLang alone 0.5.18, run as the halves of a pair 0.3.12.post1 — SGLang prefill/decode, direct transfer over tcp 0.5.18 0.3.12.post1 — SGLang with a Mooncake store 0.5.18, run as a pair 0.3.12.post1 the 0.3.12 line, such as kvcacheai/mooncake:0.3.12.post1 vLLM encode/prefill/decode, direct transfer over NIXL (ECCPUConnector) 0.30.0, behind llm-d-router or vllm-router: NVIDIA CUDA or AMD ROCm compiles its own — vLLM-Ascend encode/prefill/decode, direct transfer (ECExampleConnector) 0.30.0rc1, behind llm-d-router 0.3.11.post1, the NPU build — SGLang encode/prefill/decode, transfer by address (encoder-urls) 0.5.10, behind sgl-router, llm-d-router, or deprecated sglang-gateway 0.3.12.post1 — Engine image requirements Render flag: Non-Encode vLLM deployments behind llm-d-router need --enable-scale-out starting at vLLM 0.30.0 or vLLM-Ascend 0.30.0rc1 (Router token counting ). Earlier 0.29.0/0.23.0 floors predate that dependency. Mooncake client and store: Each runner image embeds its Mooncake client (ROCm images compile their own). Match KVCacheBackend members to the client’s minor line (Version compatibility ). Direct transport defaults: Listed runs moved KV over tcp, or ascend on vLLM-Ascend (which does not support direct tcp; see Role links and connectors ). Encoder floor: Pick an image meeting the supported serving configurations floor (0.30.0 for NVIDIA/AMD ECCPUConnector, 0.30.0rc1 for Ascend ECExampleConnector, 0.5.10 for SGLang); admission does not enforce it. Group-forward probe: Verified on vLLM 0.25.1/0.29.0 (cmpl- + request_id) and SGLang 0.5.18/0.5.21 (meta_info.id = rid). On other releases, the probe still runs: Verified admits a member, Unknown keeps prior eligibility, and only a failed health check withdraws it (Endpoint status ). Engine version resolution Managed roles (roles[].command empty) resolve an engine version from spec.roles[].engineVersion or fall back to spec.engine.version. Admission backfills empty version fields automatically from standard gpustack/runner image tags on both creation and update.
Custom or digest-only images: Set spec.engine.version or roles[].engineVersion explicitly. Admission fails closed when a managed role uses an unparseable image without a version, including when a role overrides roles[].image with a different unparseable image while leaving roles[].engineVersion empty. Runner tag agreement: If you update a gpustack/runner image while leaving a stale explicit version, admission refuses the update. Update or clear the version field alongside the image. Milestone comparison: Gates compare (major, minor, patch) tuples, so pre-release tags such as 0.30.0rc1 or 0.34.0rc0 satisfy their release line (0.30.0 or 0.34.0). Empty stored version baseline: In controller rendering, an empty stored version falls back to the < 0.30.0 baseline without re-parsing container image tags. Version gates Version gate Engine Before At/after 0.30.0 vLLM-Ascend PD renders MooncakeConnectorV1 (prefill tp_size >= decode tp_size) PD renders MooncakeConnectorV2 Pull mode (max(tp_p, tp_d) % min(tp_p, tp_d) == 0); mixed V1/V2 pairs refused 0.31.0 vLLM, vLLM-Ascend vllm-router kv_aware policy refused at admission vllm-router kv_aware admitted; emits KV events and sha256_cbor hash alignment 0.34.0 vLLM ECCPUConnector defaults VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 and VLLM_EC_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT=5601 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER omitted; VLLM_EC_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT=5601 remains defaulted (overridable, including 0) Transport compatibility The shared-store path uses KVCacheBackend.spec.transport.protocol. The direct PD path selects Mooncake, NIXL or HIXL through spec.kvTransfer.backend (Direct KV transports ). Admission refuses deployments whose store and direct paths request incompatible fabrics. A cell reads Admitted when admission does not refuse the combination.
Transport (API/Mooncake) Engine Store path TCP / tcp vLLM Works, default images; beside a direct path it keeps its store connections open and did not run out of ports where measured TCP / tcp SGLang Works, with a store image on its client’s line ; beside a direct path, it runs out of ports unless model-deployment-tcp-tw-reuse is on TCP / tcp vLLM-Ascend Not supported: refused at admission; store client accepts CANN only RDMA / rdma vLLM Admitted RDMA / rdma SGLang Admitted RDMA / rdma vLLM-Ascend Not supported: refused at admission, as for TCP EFA / efa vLLM Own image: requires an EFA build of Mooncake in the engine; default store image EFA / efa SGLang Not supported: no EFA build serves SGLang EFA / efa vLLM-Ascend Not supported: refused at admission, as for TCP CANN / ascend vLLM Not supported: CUDA client has no Ascend transport CANN / ascend SGLang Admitted CANN / ascend vLLM-Ascend Admitted; members need an image carrying CANN ROCM / hip vLLM, SGLang Admitted ROCM / hip vLLM-Ascend Not supported: refused at admission, as for TCP MUSA, MACA / musa, maca vLLM, SGLang, vLLM-Ascend Admitted Direct-path observations apply only to the named configurations:
Mooncake TCP: Verified on default vLLM and SGLang images. SGLang can exhaust ephemeral ports unless model-deployment-tcp-tw-reuse is enabled. Mooncake RDMA: Verified with vLLM on InfiniBand H100 SXM5 in Prefill and Decode Benchmark and Encode, Prefill and Decode Benchmark . EFA: Requires an EFA engine build (default store image includes EFA). vLLM-Ascend direct: Verified on cann9.1-910b-vllm0.23.0 behind llm-d-router. Stores on Ascend require CANN members (image carrying CANN ). Remote weight loading --load-format model-transfer loads verified tensors from a prepared remote source while keeping each engine’s parameter mapping and sharding. vLLM and vLLM-Ascend use the vLLM general load-format plugin; SGLang uses .pth CLI and LoadFormat hooks. See Remote Weight Delivery for configuration.
Engine Adapter entry Qualification state vLLM NativeModelTransferLoader, --load-format model-transfer on CUDA H100 loading and inference observed for full-resident and paged 80B sources and full-resident 235B broadcast; production qualification remains open vLLM-Ascend NativeModelTransferLoader through vLLM general plugin with vllm_ascend (requires CANN 9.2+ image with Python hixl, e.g. cann9.2-910b-vllm0.30.0) Loading and inference measured on two Ascend 910B2 nodes for Qwen3-8B, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Qwen3-235B-A22B-W8A8; managed HIXL admitted by default; production qualification remains open SGLang NativeSGLangModelTransferLoader, --load-format model-transfer via .pth CLI and LoadFormat hooks (requires CANN 9.2+ image on Ascend for Python hixl) H100 80B loading and inference observed; Ascend covers CLI, LoadFormat, probe and session-open, with full loading qualification open A CUDA capture does not qualify Ascend or ROCm. Under delivery policy Require, an unqualified engine and pool combination blocks instead of falling back.
Ascend (HIXL) See Ascend benchmark for same-node and cross-node load times. CANN 9.2 adds Python hixl (/usr/local/Ascend/cann-9.2.0/python/site-packages/hixl) beside libcann_hixl.so; CANN 9.0 images lack Python hixl, so load_runtime() fails closed with RuntimeUnavailableError.
Limitations SGLang store RAM: SGLang with a store enables --enable-hierarchical-cache (or --disaggregation-decode-retraction-backup cpu_tensor on Decode) and allocates pinned host RAM. Size node RAM above the engine heap plus that pool (KV Cache Pools and Bindings ). SGLang PD TCP port exhaustion: SGLang Prefill opens a new TCP connection per transfer to Decode and each store member. Ephemeral sockets left in TIME-WAIT exhaust container ports, after which requests fail (503 No available prefill workers without a store) until engine Pods restart. Mitigation (model-deployment-tcp-tw-reuse): Prevented exhaustion across 1,905 sequential requests on SGLang 0.5.18 with a store (~19,500 TIME-WAIT sockets). First add allowedUnsafeSysctls: ["net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse"] to KubeletConfiguration on every eligible node (otherwise Prefill Pods fail with SysctlForbidden), then patch the Setting: bashCopy kubectl -n gpustack-system patch setting model-deployment-tcp-tw-reuse \ --type merge -p '{"spec":{"value":"true"}}' Port range: Widening ip_local_port_range only delays exhaustion. vLLM comparison: vLLM reuses transfer connections and held at most 9 TIME-WAIT sockets without a store and at most 16 with a TCP store. External DP Benchmark On one eight-GPU H100 SXM5 node, wide tensor parallelism (TP) delivered 2.27×–6.99× higher output throughput than External DP over TCP across all twelve matched cells. External DP had lower median first-token latency at concurrency 64 on both shapes, while both eight-GPU configurations completed 1,088/1,088 measured requests with zero errors.
Both ran deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat, a mixture of experts (MoE) model. Wide TP kept all eight GPUs inside one NVLink Pod; External DP ran four two-GPU Pods with NVLink for local TP and TCP for the cross-Pod expert collective. External DP defines the serving contract.
The initial suites describe cross-Pod TCP. The separate InfiniBand RDMA comparison records the matched follow-up.
Contents Summary Environment Results InfiniBand RDMA comparison Limitations Summary Choose wide TP on single-node NVLink when throughput and token-generation latency dominate. Choose External DP when per-rank HTTP ingress or concurrency-64 first-token latency fits the workload (especially with InfiniBand RDMA, where it also led concurrency-64 output). Benefits Registered four healthy endpoints and balanced traffic evenly (285 + 284 × 3). Lowered concurrency-64 TTFT p50 by 2.58× at 1024/256 and 1.23× at 4096/128. Completed 1,088/1,088 measured requests in both configurations with zero errors. Trade-offs Over TCP, wide TP delivered 2.27×–6.99× higher output throughput in all twelve cells. Cross-Pod EP used TCP versus single-Pod NVLink for wide TP. At 4096/128, concurrency 64 over TCP, External DP suffered severe TTFT p95 and ITL p99 tails. Environment Property Captured value Cluster Kubernetes v1.35.7; one CPU node and one GPU node Accelerators 8 × NVIDIA H100 80 GB HBM3 SXM5 on one GPU node Interconnect NVLink within each Pod; TCP over eth0 between Pods GPUStack Operator v0.9.1 Captured InstanceType bench-gpu, selecting the H100 accelerator group Runner gpustack/runner:cuda13.0-vllm0.30.0; startup logs report vLLM 0.30.0 Router gpustack/llm-router:v0.3.1, round_robin Model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat, revision 85864749cd611b4353ce1decdb286193298f64c7 Model delivery ModelArtifact deepseek-v2-lite-chat; node delivery, served as /models Shared limits --max-model-len 8192, --max-num-seqs 16, --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 Wide parallelism TP = 8; EP disabled External parallelism TP = 2, DP = 4, EP world size = 8 External port setting VLLM_PORT=19500 Configuration Each configuration ran one ModelDeployment on gpu-node-0.
Configuration Roles Pods GPUs per Pod Router Wide TP 1 Server 1 8 None; direct engine HTTP External DP 1 Server group 4 2 vllm-router, round_robin Wide TP set --tensor-parallel-size 8 without --enable-expert-parallel. External DP set data parallelism (DP) = 4, local TP = 2 and expert parallelism (EP) enabled (--all2all-backend allgather_reducescatter), with one API server and local attention KV cache per rank and no cross-rank KV transfer.
NVLink carried intra-Pod traffic only. Each Pod had private IPC and /dev/shm, hostIPC disabled and no remote direct memory access (RDMA) interface, so cross-Pod EP communication used TCP sockets over eth0.
Port allocation Every External DP rank set VLLM_PORT=19500, and the run initialized on port 19502 (an observed choice, not a fixed offset). See Port allocation for vLLM port probing and the bootstrap-port race, and the walkthrough manifest .
Workload Target prompt/output shapes were 1024/256 and 4096/128 at concurrency 1, 4, 8, 16, 32 and 64 (32, 32, 32, 64, 128 and 256 measured requests per shape, plus four excluded warm-ups per cell and one calibration request per configuration). Prompts carried unique markers, and early stopping varied output-token totals.
Measurement method The in-cluster streaming generator ran each configuration once, sequentially, with warmed weights (2,176 measured requests across 24 result files). Output throughput divides actual generated tokens by cell wall time.
Time to first token (TTFT), time per output token (TPOT) and inter-token latency (ITL) use captured millisecond precision. Bold values mark lower latency or higher throughput within each matched pair without claiming statistical significance.

InfiniBand RDMA comparison A follow-up on the ConnectX-7 InfiniBand node from Prefill and Decode Benchmark kept DP = 4, TP = 2 per Pod, one API server per rank and round_robin routing. All twelve cells completed 1,088/1,088 requests with zero errors.
Transport verification Update external-dp.yaml from the TCP walkthrough (the diff shows current interface allocation; the capture used manual device exposure):
diffCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeployment metadata: name: external-dp-arm2-external-dp namespace: gpustack-bench spec: roles: - name: server kind: Server size: 4 resources: accelerator: "2" + interface: "2" NCCL logged Using network IB and via NET/IB/.../GDRDMA, confirming InfiniBand for the cross-Pod expert collective while intra-Pod TP stayed on NVLink. Keep VLLM_PORT=19500 on every rank; InfiniBand does not remove the bootstrap-port race .
Transport performance In this separate InfiniBand follow-up (where wide TP was not rerun), RDMA External DP cut concurrency-64 TTFT p50 by 6.26× (1024/256) and 8.47× (4096/128) over TCP, raised output 3.85× and 7.01×, and cut 4096/128 tails (TTFT p95 17,594.349 → 1,477.799 ms; ITL p99 1,953.899 → 182.693 ms).
Exceptions remain: wide TP kept higher output at concurrencies 1–32 (10 of 12 cells) and lower TPOT p50 and ITL p99 in all 12 cells, and RDMA regressed ITL p99 versus TCP at 1024/256, concurrency 8 (26.162 to 64.911 ms).

Engine completion counts matched 285 + 284 + 284 + 284 = 1,137 (1,088 measured, 48 warm-ups, one calibration), proving traffic reached every rank.
RDMA trade-offs Choose RDMA External DP when high-concurrency ingress (concurrency 64) and first-token latency outweigh smoother token generation. Choose wide TP on single-node NVLink for concurrencies 1–32 throughput and the lowest TPOT p50 and ITL p99 across every concurrency (including 55.619 versus 182.693 ms at 4096/128, concurrency 64). No repeated trials isolate the 1024/256, concurrency-8 RDMA ITL p99 regression (64.911 versus 26.162 ms TCP). Cross-node behavior, other models and other backends remain unmeasured.
Limitations One run per configuration (32–256 requests per cell) provides no repeated-run confidence intervals. Batching limits were per engine: four rank API servers differ from one wide API server. Parallelism, transport and routing changed together; no single overhead term was isolated. Neither capture measures cross-Pod NVLink, and separate runs do not isolate transport from run-to-run variation. All ranks shared one GPU node; cross-node placement, other DP widths and online resizing were not measured. Only one MoE model and two prompt shapes ran; dense-model behavior cannot be inferred. Unique prompt markers and early stopping varied prompt and generated-token totals slightly. Direct nonstreaming rank probes and a released-device snapshot were omitted from the TCP capture. See also — External DP (fixed-group contract) · External DP Walkthrough (manifest and endpoint checks) · Model Deployment Routing (router policies and discovery) · Elastic EP Benchmark (live collective expansion)
