title: External DP Benchmark

content:
External DP External data parallelism (External DP) runs one fixed group where every rank exposes its own HTTP endpoint behind a managed router. Because no rank is an HTTP leader, admission requires spec.router and rejects any External role without one (RouterRequired). See External DP Walkthrough for captured vLLM commands and output.
Contents Configuration Port allocation Endpoint selection Admission constraints Limitations Results Configuration A four-rank vLLM External DP group uses one Server role with size: 4 and TP = 2 per member behind vllm-router:
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeployment metadata: name: deepseek-external-dp namespace: team-a spec: model: name: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat engine: name: vLLM image: gpustack/runner:cuda13.0-vllm0.30.0 router: name: vllm-router # required; balances requests across all rank endpoints extraArgs: - --policy - round_robin roles: - name: server kind: Server replicas: 1 size: 4 # four member Pods in one fate-sharing DP group acceleratorType: gpustack--nvidia-h100-80gb-hbm3-linux-amd64 resources: accelerator: "2" # matches local --tensor-parallel-size per member extraArgs: - --tensor-parallel-size - "2" - --data-parallel-size - "4" - --data-parallel-rank - $(GPUSTACK_MEMBER_INDEX) # zero-based rank injected by operator - --data-parallel-address - $(GPUSTACK_REPLICA_LEADER_ADDRESS) # leader DNS name injected by operator - --enable-expert-parallel - --all2all-backend - allgather_reducescatter env: - name: VLLM_PORT value: "19500" # keeps candidate ports below ephemeral range To request two remote direct memory access (RDMA) endpoints per member, add interface: "2" under resources; verify active transport separately (RDMA Operations ).
Mode comparison Splitting a mixture of experts (MoE) model across data parallelism (DP) ranks gives each rank a narrow tensor parallelism (TP) slice inside one shared DP × TP expert parallelism (EP) collective, with independent per-rank HTTP schedulers. vLLM runs one engine process per rank; SGLang runs one distributed launch across size member Pods (SGLang rank configuration ).
Configuration Collective HTTP ingress Resize contract Monolithic TP One engine group, one master Master only Replaces replicas Elastic EP Ray Internal LB, one instance Master only Online elastic.dataParallelWidth scale-up vLLM External DP Fixed ranks (--data-parallel-rank) Every rank, Router-balanced Fixed; world-size edits recreate SGLang External DP Distributed launch over size members Every member, Router-balanced Fixed; replica edits recreate groups Choose External DP for fixed MoE groups needing per-rank HTTP ingress or lower high-concurrency median TTFT. Choose Elastic EP when the collective must grow online while keeping surviving Pods. SGLang rank configuration SGLang runs one distributed launch spanning size member Pods with one attention-DP group per member. With SGLANG_RUST_SERVER=1, each member serves HTTP on its base port behind sgl-router, while the FFN tensor-parallel group spans all members:
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeployment metadata: name: qwen3-sglang-external-dp namespace: team-a spec: model: name: Qwen/Qwen3-8B engine: name: SGLang image: gpustack/runner:cuda13.0-sglang0.5.22 router: name: sgl-router # required; balances across member endpoints roles: - name: server kind: Server replicas: 1 size: 2 # two member Pods in one fate-sharing group acceleratorType: gpustack--nvidia-h100-80gb-hbm3-linux-amd64 resources: accelerator: "1" # one GPU per member; FFN TP spans both extraArgs: - --tp-size - "2" - --attn-dp-size - "2" - --nnodes - "2" - --node-rank - $(GPUSTACK_MEMBER_INDEX) # zero-based member index injected by operator - --dist-init-addr - $(GPUSTACK_REPLICA_LEADER_ADDRESS):29500 # must differ from HTTP port env: - name: SGLANG_RUST_SERVER value: "1" Rendezvous port: Keep --dist-init-addr port (29500 above) distinct from the HTTP port (8000 default). Modern flag: Use --attn-dp-size (or --attention-data-parallel-size); deprecated --dp-size + --enable-dp-attention does not trigger External classification. Fault behavior: A member fault stalls survivor in-flight requests until the collective aborts; capacity equals one group, and withdrawal is group-atomic until every member re-qualifies. SGLang mode requirements An SGLang role derives External only when all four conditions hold:
Condition Purpose --attn-dp-size (or --attention-data-parallel-size) >= 2 Declares multiple attention groups --nnodes >= 2 Places groups across multiple member Pods SGLANG_RUST_SERVER set to a true value in env Exposes an HTTP listener on every member roles[].kind is Server Prefill and Decode stay routed through their own stages Single-Pod attention-DP or the Python frontend remains Internal (leader-served).
Load balancing modes There is no External DP spec field. The operator inspects roles[].extraArgs and roles[].env and reports status.roles[].parallelism.loadBalance (External, Hybrid, Internal, MultiPort or Unknown) beside declared degrees (dataParallel, dataParallelLocal, expertParallel):
Argument (vLLM spelling) Vote --data-parallel-external-lb External --data-parallel-rank External --data-parallel-hybrid-lb Hybrid --data-parallel-multi-port-external-lb MultiPort (refused on managed roles) Without an explicit flag, degree-based derivation runs only when --data-parallel-start-rank is set and --headless is absent (--data-parallel-size-local < --data-parallel-size yields External at local size 1 or Hybrid; equal yields Internal; --nnodes > 1 without local size yields Unknown). Hybrid normalizes to External at local size 1 and Internal when local equals global DP. Conflicting flags yield Unknown and fail admission.
Per-rank Pod identity For a Server role with size: N, the operator injects GPUSTACK_MEMBER_INDEX (zero-based rank) and GPUSTACK_REPLICA_LEADER_ADDRESS (leader DNS on headless Service <deployment>-<role>-r<replica>). Pass them via Kubernetes $(...) expansion in extraArgs; the operator never infers parallel flags from size or GPU count.
With vLLM, --data-parallel-rank implies these defaults without extra flags:
Omitted argument Engine default --data-parallel-external-lb Implied by --data-parallel-rank (external load balancing (External LB)) --data-parallel-size-local 1 One local DP rank per member under External LB --api-server-count 1 One API server per rank --data-parallel-backend mp Default DP backend (mp selects execution, not load balancing) --distributed-executor-backend mp Local TP stays inside one Pod --data-parallel-rpc-port Default RPC port across all ranks Port allocation Set 1024 <= VLLM_PORT < 32768 (such as 19500) on every vLLM rank, keeping candidate ports below the Linux ephemeral range (32768–60999) and clear of 8000, 29500 and 29550. Check net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range if customized.
Rank port negotiation vLLM v0.30.0 probes five free ports (get_open_ports_list), closes the probe sockets and shares the leader’s candidate list during the MoE handshake. Fixed multiprocessing External DP keeps _coord_store_port = 0, so stateless_init_dp_group retries EADDRINUSE up to five times locally without broadcasting the retry port to peers.
Port conflicts Conflict Behavior Symmetric during allocation All ranks skip an occupied base (for example 19500 → 19501–19505) and stay aligned Asymmetric after probing Only leader m0 hits EADDRINUSE and advances ports while m1–m3 stall on the old port In the captured failure, an outbound connection took leader ephemeral port 36558; m0 moved to 36557 while peers hung on 36558. With VLLM_PORT=19500, the group converged on 19502 (an observed port, not a fixed offset; see walkthrough manifest ).
Endpoint selection Unlike Internal multi-member roles (which restrict HTTP selectors to member-index=0), an External role drops the leader term on both its role Service and Router selectors while keeping the endpoint-eligible label requirement. Endpoint mode is read from running member arguments, so mid-flight edits keep serving existing ranks.
Check status.roles[].endpoints.eligible (qualified replica groups, 1 in the four-rank run) and endpoints.serving (Router-confirmed HTTP endpoints, 4 in the four-rank run). Confirm per-worker balance in the Router registry and metrics (Endpoint status ).
Rank health checks A member’s /health checks only that member, not the collective. Qualification therefore runs a group-forward probe (a real generation request) against every member across the collective. A member that answers /health while its collective is broken does not qualify.
Admission constraints Admission rejects these managed-role configurations:
MultiPort (--data-parallel-multi-port-external-lb) or unparseable Unknown load balance. External role without spec.router (RouterRequired; take-over roles[].command is unchecked). Encode paired with External or hybrid load balancing (Hybrid LB). Elastic EP (elastic.dataParallelWidth) combined with External or Hybrid LB. Limitations Scale-down grace: Disaggregated handoff grace adds 60 s before member drain gauges are read; Draining during those 60 s is expected. SGLang scope: Single-role dense text deployments only (Rust server rejects multimodal models). --load-balance-method is not rendered because the Router owns balancing. Fixed group size: Editing roles[].size replaces whole replicas (Rollout behavior ). Use Elastic EP for in-place width growth. Results On 8 × H100 SXM5 serving DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat (vLLM 0.30.0, TP = 2 over NVLink, DP = 4, EP = 8 over TCP eth0 versus single-Pod wide TP = 8 on NVLink), all four endpoints balanced evenly (285 + 284 × 3 = 1,137 total requests) with 1,088/1,088 measured requests and zero errors.
Over TCP at concurrency 64, External DP lowered time to first token (TTFT) p50 against single-Pod wide TP = 8, while wide TP kept 2.27×–6.99× higher output throughput across all 12 cells:
Prompt/output target Wide TP (ms) DP4 TP2 (ms) Median reduction 1024/256 4,798.411 1,863.100 2.58× 4096/128 3,814.139 3,094.017 1.23× With ConnectX-7 InfiniBand RDMA (resources.interface: "2"), External DP cut median TTFT 6.26×–8.47× and raised output 3.85×–7.01× over TCP, overtaking wide TP output at concurrency 64 (InfiniBand RDMA comparison ). Cross-node placement is unmeasured.
SGLang runtime record (SGLang 0.5.22, sglang-gateway from gpustack/llm-router:v0.3.1, two groups × two members): all eight content checks passed across member listeners, and scale-down honored the 60 s handoff grace (workers withdrew at 482 s and 310 s).
Without --dp-aware, the gateway registered at most one worker per group (Traffic targets ), and the surviving group did not republish Eligible within the 900 s budget.

title: External DP

content:
Prefill and Decode Benchmark On one H100 SXM5 node, prefill/decode (PD) isolated token generation from long-prompt processing. At concurrency 16, inter-token latency (ITL) p99 fell by 25.6×–27.8× for the two long-prompt shapes. The cost was higher time to first token (TTFT) through one Prefill replica and TCP KV transfer. Aggregated serving kept higher output throughput in 15 of 16 fixed-shape cells.
The initial suites and conclusions describe cross-Pod TCP. The separate InfiniBand RDMA comparison records the matched follow-up.
Contents Summary Environment Suite 1: Fixed token lengths Suite 2: Mixed load Verification InfiniBand RDMA comparison Limitations Summary Both configurations used six serving GPUs, llm-d-router and the same Qwen3-32B weights. Aggregated serving ran three Server replicas with tensor parallelism (TP) = 2. PD ran one Prefill replica and two Decode replicas, each with TP = 2. All 16 Suite 1 cells and both Suite 2 streams completed with zero errors in each configuration.
Choose PD when smooth token generation under long-prompt concurrency outweighs first-token delay and KV transfer cost. Choose aggregated when throughput or first-token delay matters more. It led throughput in 15 of 16 fixed-shape cells on this TCP setup. The mixed-load steady stream is a counterexample. It already had low ITL with aggregated serving and showed no p99 improvement with PD. The TCP results alone do not establish the same trade-off over remote direct memory access (RDMA).
Benefits At 4096/128, concurrency 16, ITL p99 fell from 458.058 ms to 17.895 ms, a 25.6× reduction. At 8192/128, concurrency 16, ITL p99 fell from 509.188 ms to 18.315 ms, a 27.8× reduction. At 256/1024, concurrency 16, output throughput rose from 753.604 to 1,078.624 tok/s, a 43.1% gain. Separating prompt processing protected Decode token gaps under heavy long-prompt concurrency.
Repeat the 256/1024 run before you rely on its throughput gain. That aggregated cell includes a TTFT outlier of 30,043.341 ms. Its TTFT p50 and p95 were 113.217 and 177.494 ms, and p99 equaled the outlier. The outlier extended aggregated wall time to 86.913 seconds, versus 60.735 seconds for PD. Its cause is unresolved, so the gain is not yet attributable to role separation.
Trade-offs The single Prefill replica queued long prompts while TCP moved their KV tensors. At 4096/128, concurrency 16, TTFT p50 rose from 1,231.691 ms to 8,065.377 ms. At 8192/128, it rose from 2,072.452 ms to 17,514.203 ms.
Aggregated serving had higher output throughput in 15 of 16 fixed-shape cells. At 8192/128, concurrency 16, it reached 322.852 tok/s against 98.154 tok/s for PD. In Suite 2, aggregated serving also had lower TTFT and higher throughput on both streams.
Environment Item Captured value Cluster Kubernetes v1.35.7; one CPU node and one GPU node Hardware 8 × NVIDIA H100 80 GB HBM3 SXM5 on one node; physical NVLink bandwidth 900 GB/s GPUStack Operator v0.9.1 Runner gpustack/runner:cuda13.0-vllm0.30.01 Model Qwen/Qwen3-32B, BF16 (16-bit brain floating-point) weights Model delivery ModelArtifact qwen3-32b, mounted at /models through node delivery Captured InstanceType bench-gpu, selecting the H100 accelerator group Aggregated 3 Server replicas × 2 GPUs, TP = 2 per replica PD 1 Prefill replica + 2 Decode replicas, 2 GPUs and TP = 2 per replica KV transport MooncakeConnector over TCP; no RDMA resources allocated Engine limits --max-model-len 16384, --max-num-seqs 64, --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 The configurations ran one after the other on the same node. Two GPUs were outside each serving allocation.
Each serving Pod exposed only its two assigned GPUs and had a private /dev/shm and IPC namespace. hostIPC was disabled, and no RDMA interface was attached. NVLink carried the intra-Pod TP traffic. All cross-Pod communication used TCP sockets over eth0, including Mooncake KV transfer between roles.
Suite 1: Fixed token lengths Each shape names target input tokens / requested output tokens. Each cell excluded four warm-up requests. Concurrency 1, 4 and 8 used 32 measured requests; concurrency 16 used 64. Every cell completed all requests with zero errors.
PD changed the ITL tail only where long prompts met high concurrency. At 4096/128, concurrency 16, ITL p99 fell from 458.058 ms to 17.895 ms. In the same cell, TTFT p50 rose from 1,231.691 ms to 8,065.377 ms, and output fell from 490.425 to 194.074 tok/s.
On 512/256 and 256/1024, both configurations kept ITL p99 between 16.751 and 18.334 ms, so PD gave no tail gain. PD raised median TTFT in seven of those eight cells; the sole exception was 512/256 at concurrency 8 (192.224 versus 210.641 ms), where TTFT p95 still worsened from 229.082 to 598.643 ms. 256/1024 at concurrency 16 is the only cell where PD led output throughput, and its aggregated run holds an unresolved outlier; see Benefits .
Latency columns keep the captured millisecond precision. Time per output token (TPOT) measures per-request generation time per token. ITL measures gaps between streamed tokens. Bold values mark the lower latency or higher throughput within each matched pair.

tokens. The burst stream ran at the same time with 40 requests of 4,096–8,192 target input tokens and 64 output tokens. It used concurrency 4 and a two-second burst interval. Both streams finished with zero errors.
Each stream’s throughput uses the whole mixed-load duration, including burst waits and the final interval. It is not that stream’s saturated throughput.

The maximum steady-stream token gap still fell from 486.353 ms to 20.850 ms, a 23.3× reduction.
The burst stream’s ITL p99 was 18.078 versus 17.826 ms. Its maximum fell from 486.248 to 20.663 ms, a 23.5× reduction. Maximum gaps and p99 describe different parts of the distribution.
Per-request TPOT p99 fell from 18.708 to 13.863 ms on the steady stream and from 21.420 to 14.171 ms on the burst stream. TPOT averages each request, while ITL measures individual token gaps.
Verification Role request counts Initial and final access-log counts confirm that requests reached every expected role. The two captures agree. The counts include warm-up, calibration and auxiliary requests, so they are not measured-suite totals or a one-to-one request trace.

The aggregated count capture also contains a collection-script diagnostic and supplies no reliable Router count. Engine counts establish role execution; client JSON establishes completion and errors.
All successful PD Suite 1 and mixed-load JSON records use the final Pod snapshot listed above.
KV transfer throughput Mooncake producer logs contain 67 APIServer metric windows, with throughput from 82.827 to 1,516.976 MB/s. One window reports 1,390.73 MB/s for 48.0 MB transferred in 34.514 ms.
If that rate applies to each TP rank independently, two ranks give approximately 2.78 GB/s. The log labels do not identify each rank, and no synchronized rank counters verify that aggregate estimate.
Every captured metric window reported zero failed transfers and zero failed receives.
InfiniBand RDMA comparison A separate follow-up used 8 × H100 SXM5 and 8 × ConnectX-7 InfiniBand adapters on one GPU node. The adapter inventory was mlx5_0–mlx5_7, and all roles stayed on gpu-node-0. The allocation stayed at one Prefill and two Decode replicas, with two GPUs and TP = 2 per replica. The 16 fixed-shape cells completed 640/640 requests with zero errors.
Configuration Add interface requests to pd-deployment.yaml from the TCP walkthrough :

The interface requests selected RDMA for cross-Pod Mooncake KV transfer.
Mooncake TP workers logged protocol rdma, KV-cache registration and RDMA-ready acknowledgements. The captured Decode workers enumerated mlx5_6 and mlx5_7, with LIDs 21816 and 21819. This runtime evidence establishes the InfiniBand KV path. HTTP routing and bootstrap control traffic stay separate.
The final access capture counted 809 Prefill completions and 407 + 402 Decode completions. These include warm-up and calibration, so they exceed the 744 measured client requests.
Fixed token lengths The baseline and follow-up used the same target shapes and measured request counts.
In this separate follow-up with larger-than-default KV blocks, RDMA PD observed 4.10× lower median TTFT and 2.45× higher throughput than TCP PD at 4096/128, concurrency 16 (2.80× and 2.41× at 8192/128), while keeping Decode ITL isolated. Choose RDMA PD over TCP PD for long-prompt isolation, though aggregated serving still led both cells behind one Prefill replica and separate runs with larger KV blocks do not isolate transport alone.

They do not measure multiple GPU nodes, additional Prefill replicas or other model sizes. Intra-Pod TP uses NVLink; cross-role KV transfer uses TCP or InfiniBand according to the capture. Neither capture measures KV transfer over NVLink.
The mixed burst used a range of prompt lengths, with different observed lengths between configurations. It is not a matched-prompt replay. The fixed-shape samples also have small token-count variations.
Requested output lengths are caps, and some requests ended earlier. Throughput uses actual output token counts. Zero client errors establish completion for these samples, not a general availability guarantee.

title: Prefill and Decode Benchmark

content:
Prefill and Decode A prefill/decode (PD) deployment runs Prefill and Decode roles in separate Pods. The operator admits all replicas as one set and links them through a managed router and a direct KV transfer path. See Prefill and decode for base role fields.
Contents Configuration Router configuration Direct KV transports Hardware requirements Role placement and services Configuration A direct PD pair needs spec.router and no spec.kvCache:
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeployment metadata: name: qwen-pd namespace: team-a spec: model: name: Qwen/Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct engine: name: vLLM # enum: vLLM, SGLang image: <a runner image your cluster can pull> # required router: name: llm-d-router # required to pair Prefill and Decode roles: - name: prefill kind: Prefill replicas: 2 acceleratorType: gpustack--nvidia-h20-linux-amd64 resources: accelerator: 2 - name: decode kind: Decode replicas: 2 acceleratorType: gpustack--nvidia-h20-linux-amd64 resources: accelerator: 2 One Kueue group per replica: Each replica forms its own Workload of size roles[].size (four single-Pod groups above), held together by an AdmissionCheck until all groups reserve quota. Replica blast radius: Preemption, eviction or rollout of one replica leaves sibling replicas and the peer role serving. Replacement starts only after the departed Pod disappears from the API server. Why replacement waits for an empty slot — Kueue keeps its finalizer on a departed serving Pod until that replica’s Workload is deleted. Creating a replacement while the old Pod is still listed makes the group exceed its declared size, and Kueue deletes the newcomer.
To share prefixes across deployments as well, add spec.kvCache on first apply (the block is frozen after creation):
diffCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeployment metadata: name: qwen-pd namespace: team-a spec: + kvCache: + poolRef: + name: team-a-dram # KVCachePoolBinding in this namespace Router configuration spec.router pairs the roles; spec.kvCache does not. A PD deployment without spec.router is admitted, but each role receives only its shared-store discriminator and no request splits across roles.
Admission matches spec.router.name to spec.engine.name and rejects cross pairings:
Router Engines Rendered configuration Routing policy llm-d-router vLLM, SGLang Endpoint picker behind a proxy with a mounted config file Fixed scoring profile vllm-router vLLM Single process configured by CLI flags cache_aware, or --policy (supports kv_aware at >= 0.31.0) sgl-router SGLang Single process configured by CLI flags with EndpointSlice discovery SGLang native policies and KV events sglang-gateway (deprecated, frozen at gateway-v0.3.1) SGLang Single process configured by CLI flags cache_aware, or --policy Router replicas: spec.router.replicas defaults to 1. Running > 1 trades prefix-cache hit rate for availability (upstream reports unsynchronized radix trees and a 10%–20% hit-rate drop). Owned router flags: Admission refuses operator-derived flags in spec.router.extraArgs. On llm-d-router: --endpoint-selector, --endpoint-target-ports, --config-file, --secure-serving, --grpc-health-port, and --metrics-endpoint-auth. On vllm-router, sgl-router, and sglang-gateway: bind addresses/ports, service-discovery flags, disaggregation flags, vllm-router’s --kv-connector, and sgl-router’s --model-id, --chat-routing, --no-tokenizer, and --dp-aware. Fixed east-west flags: llm-d-router fixes --secure-serving=false (loopback gRPC inside the Pod) and --metrics-endpoint-auth=false (in-cluster scrape). Enforce caller TLS and auth at the north-south cluster gateway. Router fields spec.router.requestTimeoutSeconds: Sets router reply timeout (> 0; 0 is refused). If omitted, upstream defaults diverge: 1 day on llm-d-router versus 30 minutes on vllm-router, sgl-router, and sglang-gateway. spec.router.disaggregationThresholdTokens: Supported on llm-d-router only (refused on other routers). Sets uncached prompt tokens needed to split a request; 0 disables splitting. Access logs: The llm-d-router proxy writes one JSON access record per request to stdout (status, flags, duration, chosen endpoint, method, path, request ID, bytes). Other routers follow their own logging flags. Router token counting Non-Encode vLLM deployments behind llm-d-router require --enable-scale-out on every role. The router counts prompt tokens via POST /v1/chat/completions/render, which vLLM exposes only under --enable-scale-out (floor: vLLM 0.30.0, vLLM-Ascend 0.30.0rc1). Admission does not check for the flag, and the operator does not inject it.
Declared roles Token counting Flag needed Rendered flag Encode, Prefill, Decode Router built-in estimator; no HTTP call No None Prefill, Decode Engine /v1/chat/completions/render call Yes None Single Server role Engine /v1/chat/completions/render call Yes None Without --enable-scale-out, disaggregation fails silently. Render calls return 404, the router sends every request to Decode alone, clients receive 200, and Prefill receives zero completions (Verification ).
Add the flag to both roles of a vLLM PD deployment:
diffCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeployment metadata: name: qwen-pd namespace: team-a spec: roles: - name: prefill kind: Prefill + extraArgs: + - --enable-scale-out - name: decode kind: Decode + extraArgs: + - --enable-scale-out Do not add --enable-scale-out to images below the documented floor; older vLLM builds exit on the unknown flag.
Router compatibility Pick an engine image meeting Engine Compatibility . Other router paths:
Router path --enable-scale-out status Configuration path llm-d-router + vLLM / vLLM-Ascend Required on >= 0.30.0 (non-Encode) Publishes KV events (kv@pod@<model>) on Server and Prefill vllm-router + vLLM / vLLM-Ascend Not established Uses router PD mode and selectors; kv_aware (>= 0.31.0) enables KV events; encode/prefill/decode (EPD) renders --epd-config sgl-router + SGLang Not applicable Uses EndpointSlice selectors, SGLang native disaggregation flags, and native KV events (kv-events) on Server and Prefill; EPD uses --encoder-urls sglang-gateway + SGLang (deprecated) Not applicable Frozen at gateway-v0.3.1; uses --pd-disaggregation and SGLang native disaggregation flags llm-d-router + SGLang Not applicable; token path unmeasured Uses approx-prefix-cache-producer (no KV events) and SGLang native disaggregation flags Direct KV transports spec.kvTransfer.backend selects Mooncake, NIXL or HIXL. If omitted, it defaults to Mooncake on non-Ascend pools and HIXL on Ascend pools.
diffCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeployment metadata: name: qwen-pd namespace: team-a spec: + kvTransfer: + backend: NIXL Backend refusals: Admission rejects HIXL off Ascend (or CPU-only), NIXL on Ascend, and mixed Ascend/non-Ascend PD pairs (see Admission refusals ). Fabric derivation: Mooncake selects ascend on Ascend, efa when both roles set resources.interface > 0 under EFA, hip on AMD ROCm, rdma when both roles set resources.interface > 0, and tcp otherwise. NIXL selects LIBFABRIC when aws-efa-enabled is true or a bound pool uses EFA, and UCX otherwise. Rollout: Changing transfer settings rolls both roles; transfers can fail until both halves converge. Verify image support in Engine Compatibility . Role links and connectors Leader routing: Multi-Pod PD replicas route HTTP to member 0 (member-index=0). Combined pool + direct KV: On vLLM pairs with spec.kvCache, Prefill wraps the direct connector first in MultiConnector beside the store connector; Decode runs the direct connector alone while keeping pool dtype and block-size alignment. Ascend connector generation: On vLLM-Ascend, effective engine version >= 0.30.0 renders MooncakeConnectorV2 (Pull mode) and relaxes TP validation to max(prefill_tp, decode_tp) % min(prefill_tp, decode_tp) == 0. Versions < 0.30.0 and legacy versionless ModelDeployments keep MooncakeConnectorV1 (prefill_tp >= decode_tp). Admission refuses mixed V1/V2 pairs where one role is < 0.30.0 and the other is >= 0.30.0. Sidecar and handshakes: Under llm-d-router, Decode runs a routing-proxy sidecar using --kv-connector=nixlv2 (vLLM NIXL or Ascend), mooncake (vLLM Mooncake), or sglang (SGLang). Ascend vLLM pairs also render behind vllm-router with --kv-connector=nixl. SGLang uses its native disaggregation flags. Parallelism declarations The operator reads each role’s parallel degrees from roles[].extraArgs (managed role) or roles[].command (take-over role), plus literal VLLM_DP_SIZE in env. Undeclared degrees default to 1/1. On SGLang, prefer --attn-dp-size over legacy --enable-dp-attention; both are parsed.
resources.accelerator requests GPUs for scheduling; it never generates --tensor-parallel-size, --pipeline-parallel-size or --data-parallel-size. Pass engine parallelism flags explicitly in extraArgs.
Flags hidden in an image entrypoint, config file, sh -c wrapper, --additional-config JSON or ConfigMap/Secret envFrom are invisible to the operator. A symmetrically hidden pair silently reads a mismatched KV layout; an asymmetric pair fails startup when Decode exceeds Prefill.
Hardware requirements Ascend driver mount On Ascend PD pairs, both roles mount host /usr/local/Ascend/driver read-only so hccn_tool can resolve NPU Device RoCE addresses. Non-transfer Ascend deployments omit this mount. If a node lacks the host driver path, Pod volume setup fails naming /usr/local/Ascend/driver; install the host Ascend driver on that node first.
Ascend A5 topologies On Ascend A5 (AcceleratorType status.detail.family "950", Ascend950PR and Ascend950DT), the operator selects on-die UnifiedBus (UB) / Unified Remote Memory Access (URMA) versus Linux Host RDMA (Host RoCE) from the engine and roles[].resources.interface. Ascend A2 and A3 keep legacy rendering.
UB, UBG and UBoE (interface: 0): Omit resources.interface on fabric.kind=ub nodes (RDMA Operations ). Pass ASCEND_GLOBAL_RESOURCE_CONFIG in roles[].env for UBG (ub_rtp:device) or UBoE (uboe:device). Host RoCE (interface > 0): Set resources.interface > 0 on both Prefill and Decode (or KVCache Server) for vLLM roles with converged "950". The operator requests device.gpustack.ai/rdma.shared (1) or device.gpustack.ai/rdma (> 1), mounts /etc/hixlep read-only and sets ascend_local_comm_res_path. Provision host endpoint files first (Ascend prerequisites ). Constraints: Asymmetric PD interfaces fail admission. Encode and SGLang never receive /etc/hixlep on KV paths (SGLang A5 PD rejects interface > 0 unless a bound KVCache pool uses RDMA). Static-UB take-over via roles[].command requires instance-host-path-volume-allowed: "true". yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeployment metadata: name: qwen-a5-roce namespace: team-a spec: model: name: Qwen/Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct engine: name: vLLM # Host RoCE /etc/hixlep applies to vLLM only image: <vllm-ascend runner image> kvCache: poolRef: name: ascend-shared-kv # homogeneous CANN KVCachePoolBinding kvTransfer: backend: HIXL router: name: llm-d-router roles: - name: prefill kind: Prefill replicas: 1 acceleratorType: atlas-950 # converged status.detail.family: "950" resources: accelerator: 1 interface: 1 # required on both Prefill and Decode for Host RoCE - name: decode kind: Decode replicas: 1 acceleratorType: atlas-950 resources: accelerator: 1 interface: 1 # grants device.gpustack.ai/rdma.shared An explicit /etc/hixlep entry in additionalVolumes replaces the operator mount while keeping the connector path. Operator-managed /etc/hixlep works with instance-host-path-volume-allowed set to false.
AWS EFA For AWS EFA, set an EFA-enabled runner in spec.engine.image or roles[].image, and an EFA-enabled model-transfer image in Helm modelTransfer.images.nvidia for remote weight loading. Default images exclude the EFA provider.
Role placement and services Different hardware per role Each role’s Workload submits to the queue named by its acceleratorType status.entrance, so Prefill and Decode can target different pools or queues while the AdmissionCheck still admits the deployment atomically (see Replica admission groups and Worker-managed resources ).
Different manufacturers use separate pool queues (credits.gpustack.ai/<manufacturer>). Mixed Ascend/non-Ascend PD pairs fail admission; mixed non-Ascend pairs are admitted but unmeasured.
Role endpoints Each role publishes a ClusterIP Service named <deployment>-<role> beside the deployment-wide Service, used by the router and direct role debugging.
When spec.router is set, the operator manages <deployment>-router (Deployment, ConfigMap, Service, ServiceAccount, Role, RoleBinding) and prunes them if spec.router is removed. status.endpoint publishes http://<deployment>-router.<namespace>.svc:<port> once a router replica is ready.
See also — Model Deployment Configuration (role fields, owned keys and admission refusals) · Model Deployment Routing (replica selection and endpoint eligibility) · Engine Compatibility (supported versions and transports) · Prefill and Decode Benchmark (equal-GPU comparison against aggregated serving)
Next → Model Deployment Routing
title: Prefill and Decode

content:
Model Deployment Routing A managed router selects among qualified serving endpoints using its configured routing policy. Endpoint selection, per-router defaults, SGLang DP registration and qualification checks govern which replicas receive traffic.
Contents Traffic targets Default routing policies Policy overrides Endpoint status Troubleshooting Traffic targets The serving mode decides which Pods are HTTP candidates; the router policy chooses only among those candidates.
Serving mode HTTP candidates Internal Server group Member 0 of each replica Qualified External Server group Every qualified member (one data parallelism (DP) rank per member) Prefill or Decode group Member 0 of each replica, even when size > 1 Elastic EP collective Master endpoint only Encode group Excluded from answering candidates and deployment Service Admission enforces strict engine-router pairing: vllm-router accepts vLLM (including Ascend) only, sgl-router and deprecated sglang-gateway accept SGLang only, and llm-d-router accepts both:
Mode llm-d-router vllm-router sgl-router sglang-gateway (deprecated) Multi-replica Server Fixed scoring profile (precise-prefix-cache-producer on vLLM/Ascend; approx-prefix-cache-producer on SGLang) cache_aware default; --policy kv_aware (>= 0.31.0) or round_robin EndpointSlice discovery + native SGLang KV events (kv-events) Frozen at gateway-v0.3.1; cache_aware default or --policy PD pair Token-counted PD split, connector docs, and decode sidecar Native PD mode; optional kv_aware (>= 0.31.0) Inferred from --prefill-selector + --decode-selector + KV events Native --pd-disaggregation (never combined with --dp-aware) EPD encode profile + decode sidecar transfer Operator-owned --epd-config, no sidecar Native pair; Prefill dials --encoder-urls Native pair; Prefill dials --encoder-urls Elastic EP Engine internal load balancing; single endpoint Same Same Same External DP Admitted, no --policy flag; prefer engine router Per-rank endpoints with --policy round_robin Per-member endpoints with --dp-aware (including PD) Per-member endpoints with --dp-aware (undivided only) Where even spread matters (multi-replica Server or External DP), choose vllm-router for vLLM or sgl-router for SGLang because llm-d-router has no policy switch (Fixed scoring profile ). Prefer sgl-router over deprecated sglang-gateway (frozen at gateway-v0.3.1) for new SGLang deployments.
External selectors: Qualified External Server roles omit member-index=0 while keeping the endpoint-eligible selector; the headless Service always publishes all members for peer communication. Shared serving port: Managed roles expose one HTTP port (8000 default; all routed roles must match). Admission rejects vLLM MultiPort. See External DP Walkthrough . sgl-router discovery and RBAC: sgl-router watches Kubernetes EndpointSlice objects rather than Pods. The operator stamps modeldeployment.gpustack.ai/role-kind=<kind> on per-role Services (<deployment>-<role>) and grants discovery.k8s.io/endpointslices (get, list, watch) in the router Role. Custom least-privilege operator worker bindings must include discovery.k8s.io/endpointslices (get, list, watch). sgl-router tokenizer default: The operator emits --no-tokenizer by default so sgl-router starts offline in air-gapped clusters without calling Hugging Face Hub. It omits --no-tokenizer automatically when spec.router.extraArgs supplies --tokenizer-path, --bucket-config, or sets --policy to cache_aware (power_of_two and session_aware keep --no-tokenizer). llm-d-router SGLang limitation: On llm-d-router@v1.0.0, SGLang stays on approx-prefix-cache-producer with no KV events because upstream precise-prefix-cache-producer requires vLLM’s /v1/chat/completions/render endpoint. Use sgl-router for SGLang KV events. SGLang --dp-aware routing: The operator renders --dp-aware on sgl-router for SGLang External DP and multi-DP PD (--attn-dp-size >= 2 or --dp-size >= 2 on Prefill or Decode) to select DP ranks per worker, and on sglang-gateway (undivided External DP only) to register one worker per attention-DP rank. Excluded replica groups Protected groups are gated by Pod labels, never by dropping selector terms. Both the Router and the role Service enforce the same rule:
Group class Selector rule Managed protected group (multi-member ordinary, External DP, PD) Requires endpoint-eligible: "true" from first enable; only qualified groups receive the label Unsupported custom route or engine outside capability matrix Keeps leader restriction with no qualification claim Ordinary single-member Server Leader restriction, no eligibility label required Managed and custom roles When roles in one deployment carry mixed requirements, the operator labels eligible discovery members with modeldeployment.gpustack.ai/router-candidate to form a deployment-wide union. That label marks membership only; actual routing intersects it with native role and member filters.
Encode stage routing Send all client requests to status.endpoint. Encode Pods stay excluded from the deployment Service and KV-event discovery:
Router Engine Encoder routing llm-d-router vLLM encode profile picks an encoder for media requests; decode sidecar (--ec-connector=ec-nixl or ec-example) coordinates transfer vllm-router vLLM Operator renders --epd-config (owned, refused in extraArgs); router drives Encode → Prefill (NIXL) → Decode without a sidecar llm-d-router SGLang Router splits every request to Prefill/Decode (no --ec-connector); Prefill dials Encode via --encoder-urls sgl-router SGLang Router routes Prefill/Decode via EndpointSlice selectors; Prefill dials Encode via --encoder-urls sglang-gateway SGLang Deprecated frozen gateway routes Prefill/Decode natively; Prefill dials Encode via --encoder-urls Under llm-d-router + vLLM, the encode profile omits queue, KV-cache and prefix scorers, sends media requests through Encode first, and routes text-only requests straight to Prefill and Decode. See Supported serving configurations for the accepted combinations.
Default routing policies vllm-router and sglang-gateway default to cache_aware (logging policy: CacheAware { cache_threshold: 0.3, ... }), sgl-router defaults to power_of_two under --chat-routing=reorg, and llm-d-router uses its fixed scoring profile:
Router Default Replica selection vllm-router cache_aware Longest matching prefix above --cache-threshold (0.3), else smallest tree; switches to least-loaded when load gap exceeds --balance-abs-threshold (64) and --balance-rel-threshold (1.5×) sgl-router power_of_two Picks the less-loaded of two sampled workers under --chat-routing=reorg (override with --policy cache_aware or --policy session_aware) sglang-gateway cache_aware Same algorithm and three defaults llm-d-router Fixed profile Highest sum of prefix match (weight 3, omitted on Decode), queue depth (2) and KV utilization (2) Prefix affinity Under cache_aware, serial requests sharing a long prefix land on one replica while peers stay idle. This is expected prefix reuse, not a fault; traffic spills over only when the load gap exceeds the thresholds above.
Measured on two single-GPU Server replicas with serial 500-character shared-prefix chat requests (zero errors; concurrent spread unmeasured):
Router Engine Requests per replica vllm-router vLLM 354 and 0 sglang-gateway SGLang 406 and 0 llm-d-router vLLM 187 and 170 llm-d-router SGLang 375 and 0 Policy overrides Add --policy round_robin to spec.router.extraArgs on vllm-router or sglang-gateway to spread requests evenly across replicas:
diffCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeployment metadata: name: round-robin-serving namespace: team-a spec: router: name: vllm-router # or sglang-gateway + extraArgs: + - --policy + - round_robin --policy is accepted by admission (Router configuration ); the router logs Starting router ... | policy: RoundRobin. On the same two-replica test at creation, 120 requests split 60 / 60 on both routers with zero errors.
Editing router.extraArgs replaces only the router Deployment without rolling worker Pods (Router rollout effects ), except when toggling kv_aware on vllm-router, which rolls only the affected worker roles. The new router starts with an empty prefix table. vllm-router, sgl-router, and sglang-gateway run behind the Envoy inference allowlist sidecar with a :9091 observer (sgl-router also proxies /metrics on :9090).
Admission validates kv_aware version requirements on vllm-router but does not validate other --policy values; an unknown value stops the router at startup:
Router Accepted --policy values vllm-router random, round_robin, cache_aware, kv_aware (vLLM >= 0.31.0), power_of_two, consistent_hash, rendezvous_hash sgl-router power_of_two (default), cache_aware (omits --no-tokenizer), session_aware (under --chat-routing=reorg, --decode-policy accepts power_of_two only and --filter accepts overloaded only) sglang-gateway (deprecated) random, round_robin, cache_aware, power_of_two, prefix_hash, manual vllm-router kv_aware (>= 0.31.0): --policy on Server, or --policy / --prefill-policy on PD Prefill, set to kv_aware enables --kv-events-config (topic: "kv@pod@<model>"), --prefix-caching-hash-algo sha256_cbor, VLLM_KV_EVENTS_USE_INT_BLOCK_HASHES=0, and ZMQ event/replay ports on Server/Prefill (Decode never subscribes to KV events). Shared KVCachePool domains must use matching hash algorithms for cross-deployment prefix hits. Fixed scoring profile llm-d-router cannot switch policies through extraArgs because the operator owns --config-file and exposes no scorer weight fields.
Endpoint status status.roles[].endpoints.eligible counts operator-qualified endpoints (null before first observation, 0 when empty), while status.roles[].endpoints.serving.state reports the direct per-Router union (Confirmed with serving.value, NotConverged, Unknown or NotConfigured).
Protected groups must pass all five criteria to hold modeldeployment.gpustack.ai/endpoint-eligible: "true":
Criterion Requirement Failure effect MemberSetComplete Every declared member Pod exists Revokes endpoint-eligible; Unknown keeps prior state MembersReady Every member passes readiness (/health or /gpustack/v1/ready) Revokes endpoint-eligible immediately GroupForward Collective forward generation probe succeeds Revokes endpoint-eligible; Unknown keeps prior state NoPlannedRetirement No active retirement holds the ordinal Revokes endpoint-eligible during withdrawal and drain NoPendingReplacement No replacement is queued for the ordinal Revokes endpoint-eligible immediately status.roles[].groups[] publishes member UID generation, state (Eligible, Withdrawn, AwaitingMembers, AwaitingReady, AwaitingProbe, AwaitingObservation, Unsupported, Unknown) and serving confirmation. An already-Eligible group with unchanged ready members stays Eligible during a transient Router scrape loss while serving.state turns Unknown.
The operator queries every Router Pod directly under three timeouts (all Router replicas must agree for Confirmed):
Bound Value Scope Fetch deadline 2 s Single Router Pod read Collection budget 14 s One collection across all Router Pods Freshness policy 15 s Validity of a collected view before falling back to Unknown Per-worker routing metrics The ModelDeployment /metrics subresource aggregates role and router counters without per-replica labels. Scrape each router’s own /metrics for per-worker attribution (worker carries the worker URL/Pod address):
Router Series Meaning vllm-router vllm_router_processed_requests_total{worker} Requests sent to each worker vllm-router vllm_router_policy_decisions_total{policy,worker} Policy picks per worker vllm-router vllm_router_pd_prefill_requests_total{worker}, vllm_router_pd_decode_requests_total{worker} PD requests per Prefill and Decode worker sgl-router sgl_router_workers, sgl_router_worker_inflight_requests Active worker count and in-flight requests per worker sgl-router sgl_router_requests_total, sgl_router_responses_total, sgl_router_worker_requests_total{outcome} Total requests, responses, and per-worker outcomes sglang-gateway smg_worker_requests_active{worker} Active in-flight requests per worker sglang-gateway smg_worker_selection_total{worker_type,policy} Picks by policy and regular/prefill/decode type llm-d-router llm_d_epp_per_endpoint_queue_size{model_server_endpoint} Queued requests per endpoint llm-d-router llm_d_epp_disagg_decision_total{decision_type} prefill-decode versus decode-only split counts Neither sglang-gateway nor llm-d-router exposes cumulative per-worker request totals; compare each engine Pod’s time to first token (TTFT) histogram _count instead. On sglang-gateway after scale-down, retired workers remain in smg_worker_health with value -1 while smg_discovery_deregistrations_total{reason="pod_deleted"} increments; count series equal to 1.
Troubleshooting Inspect router readiness, endpoint eligibility and per-group status on the ModelDeployment:
bashCopy kubectl -n <namespace> get modeldeployment <name> -o json \ | jq '{phase: .status.phase, endpoint: .status.endpoint, conditions: [.status.conditions[] | select(.type | IN("RouterReady","RoleKindsReady","EndpointEligibility"))], roles: [.status.roles[] | {name, ready, desired, endpoints, groups}]}' Symptom Signal Owner & action status.endpoint is empty RouterReady=False (RenderFailed, NoReadyReplicas) or Unknown (NotDeployed) Fix refused spec.router flags on the ModelDeployment or inspect <deployment>-router Pod logs and events. Pod Running (0/1 Ready) groups[].state: AwaitingReady or RoleKindsReady=False Wait for weight load (startupTimeoutSeconds, default 1800 s), or check worker Pod logs, /gpustack/v1/ready and roles[].pause. Pod 1/1 Ready without endpoint-eligible groups[].state: AwaitingMembers, AwaitingProbe or Withdrawn Read groups[].reason on the ModelDeployment for missing peer Pods, failed forward probe, status.retirement or roles[].pause: true. endpoints.eligible is null EndpointEligibility=Unknown (NotObserved) Wait for qualification pass or inspect operator worker logs if status stalls. Qualified group gets no traffic AwaitingObservation or serving.state: Unknown / NotConverged Inspect <deployment>-router Pods and :9091/observer/endpoints (:9090 on llm-d-router) so all Router replicas report fresh views within 15 s. See also — Prefill and Decode (spec.router pairing and refused flags) · Encode, Prefill and Decode (EPD disaggregation and connectors) · Model Deployment Configuration (readiness probes and rollout behavior) · Online Runtime Control (router hash decoupling and role pause)
Next → Model Deployment Scaling — scale serving replicas and observe graceful retirement.
title: Model Deployment Routing

content:
Online Runtime Control A ModelDeployment tunes engine parameters live, pauses roles and resizes Elastic EP collectives without restarting worker Pods or changing --load-format. See Online Runtime Control Walkthrough for end-to-end vLLM and SGLang examples.
Contents Configuration Supported parameters Runtime safeguards Pause and retirement Operations Limitations Troubleshooting Configuration Declare static boot ceilings in roles[].extraArgs, live-tunable values in roles[].runtimeControl.parameters and role traffic state in roles[].pause:
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeployment metadata: name: qwen-tuned namespace: team-a spec: model: name: Qwen/Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct engine: name: vLLM image: gpustack/runner:cuda13.0-vllm0.32.0 router: name: vllm-router roles: - name: main kind: Server replicas: 2 pause: false # optional; excluded from pod-spec-hash acceleratorType: gpustack--nvidia-h20-linux-amd64 resources: accelerator: 1 extraArgs: # static boot ceilings; edits roll worker Pods - --max-num-seqs=64 - --max-num-batched-tokens=8192 runtimeControl: # excluded from pod-spec-hash; reconciled live over HTTP parameters: scheduling.maxActiveRequests: "32" scheduling.maxBatchedTokens: "4096" scheduling.longPrefillTokenThreshold: "2048" scheduling.cacheAwareWindow: "128" scheduling.cacheAwareThreshold: "0.5" Owned environment: Never set GPUSTACK_ENGINE_SENTINEL_ENABLE, GPUSTACK_ENGINE_SENTINEL_REQUIRE_ACK or GPUSTACK_ENGINE_SENTINEL_ENGINE in roles[].env. Host staging: Managed accelerated non-Encode roles mount read-only gpustack-engine-sentinel at /var/lib/gpustack/operator/lib/engine-sentinel. Supported parameters Admission validates runtimeControl.parameters against engine support, manufacturer, topology prerequisites and declared extraArgs boot ceilings. All values are strings; decimal keys accept Kubernetes decimal quantities and reject binary suffixes.
Parameter Type Valid range Engine support Boot ceiling scheduling.maxActiveRequests Integer >= 1 vLLM (NVIDIA, Ascend), SGLang <= --max-num-seqs (vLLM) or --max-running-requests (SGLang) when declared scheduling.maxBatchedTokens Integer >= 1 vLLM (NVIDIA, Ascend), SGLang <= --max-num-batched-tokens (vLLM) or --chunked-prefill-size (SGLang) when declared scheduling.longPrefillTokenThreshold Integer >= 0 vLLM (NVIDIA, Ascend) <= effective maxBatchedTokens when declared scheduling.prefillMaxRequests Integer >= 1 SGLang <= effective maxActiveRequests when declared scheduling.scheduleConservativeness Decimal [0.1, 2.0] SGLang None scheduling.prefillDecodeInterval Integer >= 0 (0 disables deferral) SGLang None scheduling.cacheAwareWindow Integer >= 0 vLLM (NVIDIA, Ascend) None scheduling.cacheAwareThreshold Decimal [0.0, 1.0] vLLM (NVIDIA, Ascend) None scheduling.ppMaxMicroBatchSize Integer >= 1 (<= effectiveMaxActiveRequests / ppSize) SGLang Requires --pp-size or --pipeline-parallel-size > 1 scheduling.maxInflightKVLoads Integer >= 1 vLLM (NVIDIA, Ascend) Requires active KV connector (kvCache, kvTransfer, routed pair, or --kv-transfer-config) scheduling.maxAsyncKVLoadsPerStep Integer >= 1 vLLM (NVIDIA, Ascend) Requires active KV connector (kvCache, kvTransfer, routed pair, or --kv-transfer-config) speculative.acceptThresholdSingle Decimal [0.0, 1.0] SGLang None speculative.acceptThresholdAcc Decimal [0.0, 1.0] SGLang None speculative.draftBudgetFraction Decimal (0.0, 1.0] (strictly > 0.0, up to 1.0) SGLang None elastic.dataParallelWidth Integer [2, 64] vLLM (NVIDIA, Ascend) <= --elastic-ep-max-dp-size when declared; immutable presence, non-decreasing, replicas: 1, size: 1 In vLLM, scheduling.maxActiveRequests updates scheduler.max_num_active_reqs (not max_num_running_reqs); in SGLang, it updates a live admission gate. Removing keys or clearing runtimeControl restores engine boot defaults before reporting Synced or NotConfigured.
Role pause spec.roles[].pause works on every role, including CPU-only, Encode, SGLang Ray and unmanaged roles[].command roles. Setting pause: true revokes endpoint-eligible, waits for router withdrawal, drains in-flight requests and (on sentinel roles) enables the ASGI 503 pause gate on inference routes and /gpustack/v1/ready. Setting pause: false clears pause mode, replays parameters, re-acknowledges /gpustack/v1/ack and restores eligibility.
Elastic EP integration elastic.dataParallelWidth enables elastic expert parallelism (Elastic EP) inside runtimeControl.parameters (Elastic EP ). Presence is frozen in pod-spec-hash; numeric increases (2–64) serialize against pause and replay non-elastic parameters onto the master after expansion.
Reserved LoRA adapters spec.model.loraAdapters (name, artifactRef, subPath, pinned) reserves a deployment-level LoRA contract; admission currently rejects non-empty values pending ModelArtifact LoRA support.
Router rollout effects Worker pod-spec-hash reads only spec.router presence, spec.router.name and, on vllm-router, whether --policy=kv_aware or --prefill-policy=kv_aware is active for each producing role.
Editing replicas, image, imagePullPolicy, imagePullSecrets, requestTimeoutSeconds, disaggregationThresholdTokens, or unrelated extraArgs updates the router Deployment without rolling worker Pods. Toggling vllm-router kv_aware rolls the affected producing roles so --kv-events-config and CBOR block-hash settings converge; pre-existing render-version <= 5 Pods roll at most once if a router field changes before replacement.
Runtime safeguards Engine sentinel injection Managed accelerated non-Encode roles inject gpustack-engine-sentinel automatically (CPU-only, Encode, unmanaged roles[].command and SGLang Ray roles are skipped):
Zero intrusion: Loads via PYTHONPATH (sitecustomize.py) without altering VLLM_PLUGINS, container argv or developer modes. ASGI coverage: Hooks vLLM, SGLang and uvicorn.Config fallback (vllm-omni, sglang-omni). PreStop drain: Runs python3 -m gpustack_engine_sentinel.drain on Pod deletion. Router API allowlist All four managed routers enforce a shared Envoy method/path allowlist on port 8000 (including vllm-omni and sglang-omni multimodal endpoints) and return 403 on non-inference routes:
Envoy sidecar: vllm-router, sgl-router and sglang-gateway front loopback 127.0.0.1:8001 with Envoy on 0.0.0.0:8000 and expose /observer/endpoints on :9091; sgl-router also exposes a dedicated :9090 Envoy metrics listener forwarding GET /metrics to 127.0.0.1:8001. Forbidden flags: Admission rejects --enable-igw, --admin-port, --admin-host, --control-plane-port, --control-plane-host, --enable-admin-api and --enable-control-plane in spec.router.extraArgs. Router-first gate: Reconcile holds GPUSTACK_ENGINE_SENTINEL_ENABLE=1 (WaitingForRouterIsolation) until the router Deployment converges on the allowlist revision. Startup readiness and drain Each sentinel-injected engine generates a per-boot boot_id UUID and returns 503 on GET /gpustack/v1/ready until replay and POST /gpustack/v1/ack succeed:
Liveness and startup: Poll GET /gpustack/v1/live (200 while alive including paused; 503 on failure). Incarnation-bound drain: Binds pre-pause draining to (podUID, bootID) across restarts. Sharded ledger: Per-role ConfigMap (runtime-control-<deploymentUID>-<roleHash>) fences 5 s POST timeouts (AmbiguousOperation) for readback recovery. Scaling during pause ModelDeploymentScaler coexists with pause and runtimeControl because scaler-binding fences only replicas. While desired or observed pause is true, the scaler holds writes with Blocked=True (RolePaused).
Pause and retirement Role pause, replica retirement and Pod deletion drain follow separate lifecycles:
Mode Trigger Capacity and quota Signal and recovery Paused roles[].pause: true Keeps Pods, weights and Kueue Workload quota RuntimeControlSynced=True, paused: true, /ready=503, /live=200, scaler RolePaused; set pause: false to resume Retiring replicas decrease, surplus shed or dropped role Holds Pods and Workload until drained, then deletes both status.retirement.state steps to Deleting; re-declaring the ordinal before Deleting cancels (RetirementAdopted) Pod drain Rollout, eviction or post-retirement delete Holds devices up to terminationGracePeriodSeconds (G, default 30 s) preStop drains in-flight work before SIGTERM Retirement budgets At most one retirement runs per deployment (status.retirement); unscheduled or unadmitted replicas delete immediately without running the protocol:
Retirement step Budget Behavior Withdrawing 30 s Revokes endpoint-eligible and awaits Router withdrawal (requires spec.router) Draining 240 s Waits 60 s on disaggregated (PD / External DP) replicas, then requires two idle pods/exec /metrics reads Settling 30 s Deletes UID-preconditioned Pods and Workload (300 s total operation cap) Exceeding any budget before Deleting sets state: Aborted and keeps the Pods and quota. Inspect active or stalled retirement:
bashCopy kubectl -n <namespace> get modeldeployment <name> -o json \ | jq '{retirement: .status.retirement, roles: [.status.roles[] | {name, ready, desired, runtimeControl}]}' Drain window and grace On Pod deletion, preStop serves normally for 0–5 s so late-routed traffic lands, polls in-flight gauges (vllm:num_requests_running + vllm:num_requests_waiting, or SGLang running, queue, bootstrap and transfer gauges) from 5 s to G - 5 (G in 15–3600 s), and exits on two idle reads so SIGTERM arrives by G - 3.
Set roles[].terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 45 on SGLang Prefill and Decode roles because SGLang’s split-role scheduler waits ~15 s after SIGTERM even when idle. Take-over roles[].command roles receive no preStop hook.
Operations Step 1: Set startup limits Apply a ModelDeployment with static ceilings in roles[].extraArgs and wait for any managed router to converge:
bashCopy kubectl apply -f model-deployment.yaml Step 2: Tune or pause roles Patch runtimeControl.parameters or pause without recreating worker Pods:
bashCopy kubectl -n team-a patch modeldeployment qwen-tuned --type=json \ -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/roles/0/runtimeControl/parameters/scheduling.maxActiveRequests","value":"24"}]' kubectl -n team-a patch modeldeployment qwen-tuned --type=json \ -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/roles/0/pause","value":true}]' Step 3: Verify runtime settings Inspect RuntimeControlSynced, status.roles[].runtimeControl and scaler Blocked conditions:
bashCopy kubectl -n team-a get modeldeployment qwen-tuned -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions[?(@.type=="RuntimeControlSynced")]}{"\n"}{.status.roles[*].runtimeControl}{"\n"}' kubectl -n team-a get modeldeploymentscaler -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{"\t"}{.status.conditions[?(@.type=="Blocked")]}{"\n"}{end}' Condition Reason Meaning True Synced All answering Pods match desired runtimeControl and pause True NotConfigured No role sets runtimeControl or pause and prior state is restored Unknown WaitingForRouterIsolation Router Deployment has not converged on Envoy allowlist Unknown Draining Eligible endpoints are draining before pause Unknown Reconciling Replay, pause toggle or /gpustack/v1/ack in progress Unknown EndpointUnreachable One or more answering Pods unreachable False UnsupportedEngineVersion Engine rejected fields in unsupportedFields False DrainFailed Pre-pause incarnation drain failed False AmbiguousOperation Mutating POST timed out; readback did not settle False ReconcileFailed Engine returned a validation or apply error Limitations Deferred power states: GPU sleep / weight offload and KV eviction states are not applied live. Static parameters: TP, PP, context parallelism, quantization, --gpu-memory-utilization, --kv-cache-dtype, --load-format ipc_cache and Elastic EP scale-down require restart or recreation. Excluded shapes: Unmanaged (roles[].command), Encode, CPU-only and SGLang Ray roles reject runtimeControl; pause works on all roles. Gateway auth: Put caller auth at the external gateway; engine --api-key blocks sentinel probes. Troubleshooting Symptom Owner Action WaitingForRouterIsolation persists <deployment>-router Deployment Inspect router Pods and events for Envoy sidecar or image failures. UnsupportedEngineVersion reported ModelDeployment / engine image Read status.roles[*].runtimeControl.unsupportedFields and remove unsupported keys or upgrade the engine image. AmbiguousOperation reported Worker Pod Inspect worker Pod logs and /gpustack/v1/runtime_config state before retrying. Pod stays unready after restart Worker Pod / operator worker Check /gpustack/v1/ready response and operator worker logs for replay or /ack errors. RolePaused blocks scaler ModelDeployment Set spec.roles[*].pause: false and wait for RuntimeControlSynced=True. Retirement Aborted at 30 s ModelDeployment Add spec.router for active scale-down (unrouted Service withdrawal cannot be proved), or scale down before admission. Disaggregated retirement stays Draining ModelDeployment / member Pods Wait out the normal 60 s handoff grace, inspect status.retirement.reason and /metrics, or raise replicas before Deleting (RetirementAdopted). Admission rejects loraAdapters ModelDeployment Omit spec.model.loraAdapters until ModelArtifact LoRA support ships. See also — Online Runtime Control Walkthrough (end-to-end vLLM and SGLang examples) · Model Deployment Configuration (role fields, readiness and rollout hash) · Model Deployment Routing (router policies and endpoint eligibility) · Model Deployment Scaling (ModelDeploymentScaler behavior) · Elastic EP (collective resize serialization)
Next → Model Deployment Routing — inspect router policies and traffic targets.
title: Online Runtime Control

content:
Model Deployment Scaling Benchmark Two hardware suites evaluate ModelDeploymentScaler. Suite 1 ran five disaggregated configurations on one eight-H100 node. Suite 2 evaluated offline capacity priors, 18 serial capacity-arm rounds, 360-second algorithm sensitivity, embedded InferenceX priors and multi-node disaggregation across four single-H200 nodes.
ModelDeploymentScaler observed load shifts, resolved offline priors and updated replicas promptly. End-to-end scale-out latency still depends on weight loading, engine startup, graph compilation (~76 s on H200 vLLM) and accelerator queueing outside the scaler’s control.
Contents Summary Environment Configuration Suite 1: Scaling comparison Suite 2: Capacity priors Verification Limitations Summary A prefill/decode (PD) pair splits prompt processing from token generation; an encode/prefill/decode (EPD) deployment adds an image encoder. Suite 1 compared Proportional, TokenThroughput and Predictive on H100; Suite 2 evaluated Server capacity priors and multi-node PD/EPD on H200. Model Deployment Scaling defines the algorithms, priors and guards.
Choose catalog-backed Predictive for sustained traffic ramps where startup latency (~76 s) otherwise outlasts reactive scale-out; pair horizonSeconds with maxStepReplicas because ramp slopes amplify rawRecommendedReplicas. Choose TokenThroughput with 0.75 catalog headroom for steady workloads where unmargined saturation capacities stay under-triggered. Failures and caveats remain: Suite 1 SGLang PD hit Mooncake TCP port exhaustion (4,421 errors); the standalone lifecycle check lost 7/13,073 requests during scale-out; Suite 2 TokenThroughput failed 11/1,272 requests in 360 s sustain; and multi-node H200 vLLM PD prefill scale-out hit transient Router 503s during worker registration.
All 18 H200 single-Server rounds, the embedded openai/gpt-oss-120b check, and H200 vLLM PD Proportional and EPD Predictive completed with zero failed requests.
Benefits In Suite 2 on H200 from an equal 1-replica baseline, 0.75 catalog headroom triggered TokenThroughput (1 → 2 at c = 24) where unmargined saturation (17135.159 tok/s) stalled, and the embedded openai/gpt-oss-120b (fp4) prior matched sustain throughput within 1.2% (4862.388 versus 4804.08 tok/s). Pairing the catalog with Predictive offset ~76 s vLLM startup, cutting 45 s sustain TTFT p50 from 343.842 to 189.511 ms (maxReplicas: 2) and 90 s sustain TTFT p50 from 145.939–190.555 to 120.59 ms (maxReplicas: 4, 3886.136 output tok/s, zero errors). In Suite 1 on H100, predictive PD cut ramp TTFT p50 (467.906 versus 2540.853 ms) and raised output (2109.251 versus 1117.481 tok/s), though low manual targets scaled it during baseline. Trade-offs In Suite 1, 90 s cooldown sat below the 300 s downward stabilization window, leaving final snapshots at two replicas. In Suite 2’s 45 s sustain rounds, TokenThroughput catalog spent 317.04 median readyReplicaSeconds (+33.7% over manual’s 237.094 s) without lowering sustain TTFT p50 because ~76 s startup consumed most of the window. Predictive amplifies initial ramp slopes (rawRecommendedReplicas 4–75), so production configs pair horizonSeconds (180–300 s) with behavior.scaleUp.maxStepReplicas; see Step 3: Choose an algorithm . Environment Item Suite 1 (H100) Suite 2 (H200) Cluster Kubernetes v1.35.7; one CPU node and one GPU node Kubernetes v1.35.7; one CPU node (4 vCPU, 16 GB) and four GPU nodes Hardware 8 × NVIDIA H100 80 GB SXM GPUs; 128 vCPUs, 1600 GB RAM 4 × NVIDIA H200 140 GB SXM GPUs (1 GPU, 16 vCPUs, 200 GB RAM per node) Text models Qwen/Qwen3-8B (b968826d9c46dd6066d109eabc6255188de91218) Qwen/Qwen3-8B (bf16) and openai/gpt-oss-120b (fp4, d782fd43...) Multimodal model Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct (cc594898...) Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct (0c351dd0...) Model delivery Prefetched node cache, mounted at /models Prefetched node cache, mounted at /models vLLM image gpustack/runner:cuda13.0-vllm0.30.0 gpustack/runner:cuda13.0-vllm0.30.0 SGLang image gpustack/runner:cuda12.9-sglang0.5.18 gpustack/runner:cuda12.9-sglang0.5.18 Router / Service llm-d-router with cluster-internal Service endpoints Target-owned Service for Server; llm-d-router / sglang-router for PD/EPD Load driver In-cluster default/bench-driver; case129-probe for lifecycle In-cluster default/bench-driver on the dedicated CPU node GPU allocation bench-gpu InstanceType; 1 GPU per replica, TP = 1 gpustack--nvidia-h200-linux-amd64; 1 GPU per replica, TP = 1 Traffic went directly from the in-cluster driver to cluster-internal Service endpoints with no kubectl port-forward. vLLM roles set VLLM_HTTP_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE=3600.
Configuration Suite 1 roles started at 1 replica with bounds 1..2, Active mode and a 10 s sampling interval.
Configuration Model Algorithm Capacity settings vllm-pd-proportional Qwen3-8B Proportional RunningRequests, target 3 per role, tolerance 0.1 vllm-pd-token-throughput Qwen3-8B TokenThroughput Prefill 1200 tok/s; decode 300 tok/s per replica vllm-pd-predictive Qwen3-8B Predictive Same fallback targets; forecast capacity 2000 tok/s per role sglang-pd-token-throughput Qwen3-8B TokenThroughput Prefill 1200 tok/s; decode 300 tok/s per replica vllm-epd-predictive Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct Predictive Same fallback and forecast capacities; encode coupled to prefill Predictive runs set horizonSeconds: 30, minPoints: 2, qLevel: "0.5" and qTrend: "0.3". Token-based runs kept default 180 s stable / 60 s panic windows, panic threshold 2, and latency targets 500 ms / 50 ms. All preferred a prefill/decode ratio of 1 (EPD also preferred encode/prefill 1, reaching 1 encode, 2 prefill, 2 decode).
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeploymentScaler metadata: name: autoscale-vllm-pd spec: targetRef: name: autoscaling-vllm-pd mode: Active # commits the recommendation to the target sampling: intervalSeconds: 10 # sampling cadence roles: - name: prefill minReplicas: 1 maxReplicas: 2 - name: decode minReplicas: 1 maxReplicas: 2 ratios: - numeratorRole: prefill denominatorRole: decode target: "1" # preferred ratio, not a fixed band algorithm: type: Proportional proportional: metric: RunningRequests # requests per ready replica tolerance: "0.1" # deadband around the target roleTargets: - name: prefill target: "3" # requests per ready replica - name: decode target: "3" # requests per ready replica # TokenThroughput replaced proportional: # type: TokenThroughput # tokenThroughput: # prefillTargetTokensPerSecond: "1200" # decodeTargetTokensPerSecond: "300" # Predictive kept those token targets and added a forecast: # type: Predictive # predictive: # tokenThroughput: # prefillTargetTokensPerSecond: "1200" # decodeTargetTokensPerSecond: "300" # horizonSeconds: 30 # minPoints: 2 # qLevel: "0.5" # qTrend: "0.3" # prefillTokenCapacityPerReplica: "2000" # decodeTokenCapacityPerReplica: "2000" See Scaling Walkthrough for the target ModelDeployment manifest.
Benchmark run order Two waves shared an eight-GPU ceiling (maximum reserved capacity per sequence, not continuous use):
Wave First sequence Second sequence GPU ceiling 1 vLLM PD: Proportional, reset, then Predictive; up to 4 GPUs SGLang PD: TokenThroughput, release, then a separate vLLM PD TokenThroughput deployment; up to 4 GPUs 4 + 4 = 8 2 vLLM EPD Predictive; up to 6 GPUs Single-role live lifecycle check; up to 2 GPUs 6 + 2 = 8 Admission checks ran separately before Wave 1. Between configurations on a shared deployment, the runner deleted the scaler, waited for binding release and restored one replica per role.
Workload Text runs streamed 1,024-input / up-to-256-output-token requests; multimodal runs sent fixed request counts with unique 560-pixel images (shared_image: false), 1,024 text tokens and up to 256 output tokens.
Phase Duration (s) Concurrency Multimodal requests Baseline 45 2 9 Ramp 75 24 180 Sustain 75 24 180 Cooldown 90 2 18 Time to first token (TTFT) and inter-token latency (ITL) percentiles use successful requests; output throughput divides successful output tokens by recorded phase wall time.
Suite 1: Scaling comparison On H100 vLLM PD (zero errors across all three algorithms), Predictive held ramp TTFT p50 to 467.906 ms versus 2,325.222 ms (TokenThroughput) and 2,540.853 ms (Proportional), with 2,109.251 tok/s ramp output versus 1,230.879 and 1,117.481 tok/s.
Confounder: manual token targets sat below baseline load, so TokenThroughput (raw = 2) and Predictive (raw = 7) scaled at B2 before ramp (Predictive entered R1 with 2 Ready replicas), which does not isolate forecasting alone.

Its error-heavy phases do not measure healthy capacity, and no rerun with model-deployment-tcp-tw-reuse was captured.
Suite 2: Capacity priors Suite 2 ran across four single-GPU H200 nodes plus a dedicated CPU driver node, testing offline priors on single-Pod Server deployments before re-running the five disaggregated configurations across multiple nodes.
Single-replica sweep One Qwen/Qwen3-8B (bf16, vllm, 1 × H200, TP = 1) Server replica ran six 60-second concurrency levels (1,024/256 tokens, zero errors) to build the offline ConfigMap catalog.
Every point met P95 TTFT <= 2000 ms and ITL <= 33 ms (ExplicitSaturation). Catalog.Resolve picked 17135.159 tok/s at c = 32 as the seed and applied headroom: "0.75" to derive 12851.37 tok/s, crossing measured throughput between c = 16 (11477.608 tok/s) and c = 24 (14527.811 tok/s).
