Encode, Prefill and Decode Walkthrough Deploy Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct across dedicated Encode, Prefill, and Decode roles behind llm-d-router, inspect rendered NIXL encoder-cache flags, and verify multimodal completion across all three stages.
Contents Summary Deployment Verification Cleanup Limitations Troubleshooting Summary Encode/prefill/decode (EPD) disaggregation isolates multimodal vision encoding onto Encode Pods so large image bursts do not stall token generation. Text-only requests traverse Prefill → Decode, while multimodal requests route through Encode → Prefill → Decode (Encode, Prefill and Decode ):
Object Scope Creator Purpose ModelArtifact namespace user Resolves Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct weights ModelPrefetch namespace user Warms qwen2-5-vl-7b-instruct onto the H100 node AcceleratorType cluster operator H100 pool requested by all three roles ModelDeployment namespace user Runs 1 Encode, 1 Prefill, and 1 Decode replica behind llm-d-router Router Deployment and Service namespace operator Single HTTP endpoint routing multimodal and text requests In the H100 benchmark (3 GPUs for EPD vs 2 for PD and 1 for aggregated serving), EPD improved concurrency-8 4k/8k inter-token latency (ITL) p99 by 15.1×–21.8× and repeated-image time to first token (TTFT) p50 by 5.9×, while small-prompt TTFT often favored aggregated serving; see Encode, Prefill and Decode Benchmark .
Environment Item Value Cluster Kubernetes v1.35.7; 1 CPU node and 1 GPU node (gpu-node-0) GPUs 8 × NVIDIA H100 80 GB HBM3 SXM5 (3 GPUs allocated: 1 per role) Pool Captured on custom InstanceType bench-gpu; reusable manifest uses gpustack--nvidia-h100-80gb-hbm3-linux-amd64 Model Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct from ModelArtifact qwen2-5-vl-7b-instruct mounted at /var/lib/gpustack/model Runtime vLLM gpustack/runner:cuda13.0-vllm0.30.0 with llm-d-router Deployment Step 1: Start three-role serving Create and prefetch ModelArtifact qwen2-5-vl-7b-instruct in gpustack-bench using Model Prefetch , then save epd-deployment.yaml:
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeployment metadata: name: epd-arm3-epd namespace: gpustack-bench spec: model: name: qwen2-5-vl-7b-instruct artifactRef: name: qwen2-5-vl-7b-instruct engine: name: vLLM image: gpustack/runner:cuda13.0-vllm0.30.0 router: name: llm-d-router roles: - name: encode kind: Encode replicas: 1 size: 1 acceleratorType: gpustack--nvidia-h100-80gb-hbm3-linux-amd64 image: gpustack/runner:cuda13.0-vllm0.30.0 imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent resources: accelerator: "1" extraArgs: - --max-model-len - "16384" - --gpu-memory-utilization - "0.85" - name: prefill kind: Prefill replicas: 1 size: 1 acceleratorType: gpustack--nvidia-h100-80gb-hbm3-linux-amd64 image: gpustack/runner:cuda13.0-vllm0.30.0 imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent resources: accelerator: "1" extraArgs: - --tensor-parallel-size - "1" - --max-model-len - "16384" - --gpu-memory-utilization - "0.85" - name: decode kind: Decode replicas: 1 size: 1 acceleratorType: gpustack--nvidia-h100-80gb-hbm3-linux-amd64 image: gpustack/runner:cuda13.0-vllm0.30.0 imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent resources: accelerator: "1" extraArgs: - --tensor-parallel-size - "1" - --max-model-len - "16384" - --gpu-memory-utilization - "0.85" Apply epd-deployment.yaml and wait for ROLES=1R1E1P1D and PHASE=Ready:
bashCopy kubectl apply -f epd-deployment.yaml kubectl get modeldeployment epd-arm3-epd -n gpustack-bench \ -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,ENGINE:.spec.engine.name,ROLES:.status.roleSummary,PHASE:.status.phase kubectl get pods -n gpustack-bench -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=epd-arm3-epd Captured output:
textCopy NAME ENGINE ROLES PHASE epd-arm3-epd vLLM 1R1E1P1D Ready NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE epd-arm3-epd-decode-h62cw 2/2 Running 0 95s epd-arm3-epd-encode-9jz5c 1/1 Running 0 94s epd-arm3-epd-prefill-26ls5 1/1 Running 0 95s epd-arm3-epd-router-6cc94d94b8-glnvt 2/2 Running 0 93s The Decode Pod runs 2/2 containers (main engine plus native routing-proxy sidecar). If admission rejects the manifest or PHASE stays Starting, see Troubleshooting .
Step 2: Inspect role configuration Project the operator-synthesized connector flags, ports, and sidecar arguments across all three engine roles (do not pass these owned flags in extraArgs; see Encoder-cache connectors ):
bashCopy kubectl get pods -n gpustack-bench -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=epd-arm3-epd -o json | jq '[.items[] | select(.metadata.labels["app.kubernetes.io/component"] != "router") | { role: .metadata.labels["app.kubernetes.io/component"], pod: .metadata.name, command: .spec.containers[0].command, ports: [.spec.containers[0].ports[]?.containerPort], proxyArgs: (.spec.initContainers // [] | map(select(.name=="routing-proxy"))[0].args) }]' Captured output (condensed per role):
jsonCopy [ { "role": "encode", "pod": "epd-arm3-epd-encode-9jz5c", "command": [ "vllm", "serve", "/var/lib/gpustack/model", "--ec-transfer-config", "{\"ec_connector\":\"ECCPUConnector\",\"ec_role\":\"ec_producer\",\"ec_connector_extra_config\":{\"ec_enable_nixl\":true,\"ec_cpu_bytes\":1073741824}}", "--enforce-eager", "--no-enable-prefix-caching", "--max-num-batched-tokens", "114688", "--mm-encoder-only", "--served-model-name", "qwen2-5-vl-7b-instruct", "--max-model-len", "16384", "--gpu-memory-utilization", "0.85", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000" ], "ports": [8000, 5601], "proxyArgs": null }, { "role": "prefill", "pod": "epd-arm3-epd-prefill-26ls5", "command": [ "vllm", "serve", "/var/lib/gpustack/model", "--kv-transfer-config", "{\"kv_connector\":\"MooncakeConnector\",\"kv_role\":\"kv_producer\",\"kv_connector_extra_config\":{\"mooncake_protocol\":\"tcp\"}}", "--ec-transfer-config", "{\"ec_connector\":\"ECCPUConnector\",\"ec_role\":\"ec_consumer\",\"ec_connector_extra_config\":{\"ec_enable_nixl\":true,\"ec_cpu_bytes\":1073741824}}", "--kv-events-config", "{\"enable_kv_cache_events\":true,\"publisher\":\"zmq\",\"endpoint\":\"tcp://*:5557\",\"replay_endpoint\":\"tcp://*:5558\",\"buffer_steps\":10000,\"hwm\":100000,\"max_queue_size\":100000,\"topic\":\"kv@\"}", "--served-model-name", "qwen2-5-vl-7b-instruct", "--tensor-parallel-size", "1", "--max-model-len", "16384", "--gpu-memory-utilization", "0.85", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000" ], "ports": [8000], "proxyArgs": null }, { "role": "decode", "pod": "epd-arm3-epd-decode-h62cw", "command": [ "vllm", "serve", "/var/lib/gpustack/model", "--kv-transfer-config", "{\"kv_connector\":\"MooncakeConnector\",\"kv_role\":\"kv_consumer\",\"kv_connector_extra_config\":{\"mooncake_protocol\":\"tcp\"}}", "--served-model-name", "qwen2-5-vl-7b-instruct", "--tensor-parallel-size", "1", "--max-model-len", "16384", "--gpu-memory-utilization", "0.85", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8200" ], "ports": [8200], "proxyArgs": [ "--port=8000", "--model-server-port=8200", "--kv-connector=mooncake", "--mooncake-bootstrap-port=8998", "--secure-proxy=false", "--ec-connector=ec-nixl" ] } ] Confirm three rendered invariants:
Encode runs --mm-encoder-only (keeping LLM weights unloaded), defaults --enforce-eager and --no-enable-prefix-caching (Operator-owned keys ), defaults NIXL side-channel port 5601 (VLLM_EC_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT=5601, overridable including 0), and defaults VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 on vLLM < 0.34.0 (omitted at >= 0.34.0). Prefill pairs ECCPUConnector (ec_consumer) with MooncakeConnector (kv_producer) while keeping CUDA graphs enabled. Decode serves behind routing-proxy on :8000 (--ec-connector=ec-nixl → engine :8200). Verification Step 3: Send a multimodal request Read status.endpoint and send a multimodal chat completion containing both an image_url (base64 PNG) and a text prompt for "model": "qwen2-5-vl-7b-instruct":
bashCopy kubectl get modeldeployment epd-arm3-epd -n gpustack-bench -o jsonpath='{.status.endpoint}{"\n"}' Captured output:
textCopy http://epd-arm3-epd-router.gpustack-bench.svc:8000 Build a small multimodal chat-completion payload containing a 56×56 RGB PNG image_url part beside a text prompt, then send it to the router from inside the cluster:
bashCopy cat <<'EOF' > request.json { "model": "qwen2-5-vl-7b-instruct", "max_tokens": 32, "messages": [ { "role": "user", "content": [ {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this image briefly."}, { "type": "image_url", "image_url": { "url": "data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAADgAAAA4CAIAAAAn5KxJAAAARElEQVR42u3OQQkAAAgEsItmNKMZzYcphMECLNXzQkRFRUVFRUVFRUVFRUVFRUVFRUVFRUVFRUVFRUVFRUVFRUVFRc8CbIRhD2BnZn0AAAAASUVORK5CYII=" } } ] } ] } EOF kubectl run curl-probe -n gpustack-bench --rm -i --restart=Never --image=curlimages/curl -- \ curl -fsS -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data-binary @- \ http://epd-arm3-epd-router.gpustack-bench.svc:8000/v1/chat/completions < request.json Across 236 measured requests with zero errors (plus 28 warm-ups; 280 router access-log lines), container access logs confirm activity at every stage:
Stage Container Captured log count Encode epd-arm3-epd-encode-9jz5c/main POST /v1/chat/completions (264 lines) Prefill epd-arm3-epd-prefill-26ls5/main POST /v1/chat/completions (264 lines) Decode epd-arm3-epd-decode-h62cw/main POST /v1/chat/completions (264 lines) Decode sidecar epd-arm3-epd-decode-h62cw/routing-proxy Multimodal items received (264 lines) If Encode receives requests while Prefill receives zero, check vLLM PD token-counting flags in Troubleshooting .
Step 4: Check admission and placement Confirm that Kueue reserved all three role Workloads together:
bashCopy kubectl get workloads -n gpustack-bench All four Pods ran on gpu-node-0, with private IPC, private /dev/shm, and no RDMA interface; all cross-Pod NIXL encoder-cache and Mooncake KV transfers used TCP over eth0.
Across multi-node clusters, rendered soft Pod affinity weights prefer co-locating roles that exchange the largest payloads without blocking scheduling (Role placement preferences ):
Replica Preferred peer Weight Encode Prefill 50 Prefill Decode 100 Prefill Encode 50 Decode Prefill 100 Cleanup Delete epd-arm3-epd and wait until all owned Pods and Services terminate:
bashCopy kubectl delete modeldeployment epd-arm3-epd -n gpustack-bench kubectl get pods,services -n gpustack-bench -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=epd-arm3-epd Limitations Role kinds (Encode, Prefill, Decode, Server) are frozen after creation. Measurements cover single-node TCP transfer. Retiring an Encode replica drains for a fixed ~300 s window because encoders expose no in-flight request counter; transfers still active when that window expires fail at the client. Troubleshooting Symptom Signal Resolution Apply rejected on role structure Webhook refusal on ModelDeployment Encode requires both Prefill and Decode (one role per kind, no Server, no spec.kvCache, and no role command; see Admission constraints ). Apply rejected on engine, router, or platform Webhook refusal on ModelDeployment All three roles must share one accelerator platform and match Supported serving configurations (vllm-router is rejected on Ascend). Encoder container exits on unknown flag Container startup failure Upgrade the runner image to meet the floor (vLLM >= 0.30.0, vllm-ascend >= 0.30.0rc1, SGLang >= 0.5.10; see Engine Compatibility ). Requests bypass Prefill Router routes directly to Decode Check vLLM token-counting support and --enable-scale-out rules (Router token counting ). Ascend encoder fails storage setup ECExampleConnector missing shared path Mount a shared ReadWriteMany PVC on both Encode (read-write) and Prefill with identical claimName, mountPath, and subPath. Apply rejected on port 5601 or 8997 Side-channel or bootstrap port collision ECCPUConnector defaults VLLM_EC_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT=5601 (override in roles[].env, including 0, or move HTTP off 5601), and SGLang Prefill in EPD owns 8997. Encode replica stays in Draining ~300 s Bounded encoder drain timer Expected behavior; wait for the ~300 s drain window to finish. RoleKindsReady=False Zero Ready replicas in one role kind Read the failing kind from ModelDeployment status and inspect its Pod events and container logs. See also — Encode, Prefill and Decode (role contract and supported configurations) · Encode, Prefill and Decode Benchmark (H100 latency and throughput) · Prefill and Decode Walkthrough (two-role disaggregation)

External DP Walkthrough Deploy four fixed vLLM data parallelism (DP) ranks behind vllm-router, verify direct completions on every rank, and confirm that the router distributes traffic across all four endpoints. For SGLang (sglang-gateway) contracts and results, see External DP .
Contents Summary Step 1: Deploy rank group Verification Cleanup Limitations Troubleshooting Summary External load balancing (External LB) exposes an independent HTTP server on every DP rank inside one fixed expert parallelism (EP) collective (replicas: 1, size: 4, 2 GPUs per member = 8 GPUs, TP = 2, DP = 4, EP world size = 8). Unlike Elastic EP , the collective size is fixed at startup:
Object Scope Creator Purpose ModelArtifact namespace user Resolves deepseek-v2-lite-chat weights via node model delivery AcceleratorType cluster operator Whole-GPU H100 pool requested by all four members ModelDeployment namespace user Four-member External LB collective fronted by vllm-router At concurrency 64 on H100 SXM5, four-rank External DP cut time to first token (TTFT) p50 by 2.58× on 1024/256 (1,863.100 ms vs 4,798.411 ms) and 1.23× on 4096/128 (3,094.017 ms vs 3,814.139 ms), while wide TP = 8 retained 2.27×–6.99× higher output throughput; see External DP Benchmark .
Environment Item Value Cluster Kubernetes v1.35.7; 1 CPU node and 1 GPU node (gpu-node-0) with 8 free H100 80 GB HBM3 SXM5 GPUs Operator GPUStack Operator v0.9.1 Runner and router gpustack/runner:cuda13.0-vllm0.30.0; vllm-router (gpustack/llm-router:v0.3.1, --policy round_robin) Model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat (ModelArtifact deepseek-v2-lite-chat) Pool Captured on custom InstanceType bench-gpu; reusable manifest uses gpustack--nvidia-h100-80gb-hbm3-linux-amd64 GPU budget 4 members × 2 GPUs = 8 GPUs Each member Pod exposed two GPUs with private IPC, private /dev/shm, and no remote direct memory access (RDMA) interface. Intra-Pod TP = 2 used NVLink, while cross-Pod EP communication (allgather_reducescatter) ran over TCP on eth0.
Enable node model delivery and warm deepseek-v2-lite-chat in namespace gpustack-bench via Model Prefetch before applying Step 1.
Step 1: Deploy rank group Save external-dp.yaml:
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeployment metadata: name: external-dp-arm2-external-dp namespace: gpustack-bench spec: model: name: deepseek-v2-lite-chat artifactRef: name: deepseek-v2-lite-chat engine: name: vLLM image: gpustack/runner:cuda13.0-vllm0.30.0 router: name: vllm-router image: gpustack/llm-router:v0.3.1 extraArgs: - --policy - round_robin roles: - name: server kind: Server replicas: 1 size: 4 acceleratorType: gpustack--nvidia-h100-80gb-hbm3-linux-amd64 image: gpustack/runner:cuda13.0-vllm0.30.0 imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent resources: accelerator: "2" extraArgs: - --tensor-parallel-size - "2" - --data-parallel-size - "4" - --data-parallel-rank - $(GPUSTACK_MEMBER_INDEX) - --data-parallel-address - $(GPUSTACK_REPLICA_LEADER_ADDRESS) - --enable-expert-parallel - --max-model-len - "8192" - --max-num-seqs - "16" - --gpu-memory-utilization - "0.90" - --all2all-backend - allgather_reducescatter env: - name: VLLM_PORT value: "19500" - name: OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER value: none - name: OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER value: none The operator injects GPUSTACK_MEMBER_INDEX (0..3) and GPUSTACK_REPLICA_LEADER_ADDRESS into every member Pod; passing --data-parallel-rank activates vLLM’s External LB mode.
Port allocation On hosts using Linux ephemeral ports 32768–60999, set 1024 <= VLLM_PORT < 32768 (such as 19500, clear of 8000, 29500, and 29550) on every rank so vLLM’s handshake ports never collide with outbound ephemeral sockets (19500 initialized cleanly at 19502 in this capture; see Port allocation ).
Validate and apply external-dp.yaml:
bashCopy kubectl apply --dry-run=server -f external-dp.yaml kubectl apply -f external-dp.yaml kubectl -n gpustack-bench get modeldeployment external-dp-arm2-external-dp kubectl -n gpustack-bench get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=external-dp-arm2-external-dp -o wide Captured output (genericized node name, ROLES=1R1S, PHASE=Ready):
textCopy NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE NODE external-dp-arm2-external-dp-router-6f7ccf57b8-vq4fr 1/1 Running 0 2m17s gpu-node-0 external-dp-arm2-external-dp-server-r0-m0 1/1 Running 0 2m19s gpu-node-0 external-dp-arm2-external-dp-server-r0-m1 1/1 Running 0 2m19s gpu-node-0 external-dp-arm2-external-dp-server-r0-m2 1/1 Running 0 2m19s gpu-node-0 external-dp-arm2-external-dp-server-r0-m3 1/1 Running 0 2m19s gpu-node-0 Verification Step 2: Verify rank endpoints Verify that the operator detected loadBalance: "External" and confirmed all four HTTP endpoints on replica group r0:
bashCopy kubectl -n gpustack-bench get modeldeployment external-dp-arm2-external-dp -o json > external-dp-cr.json jq '.status.roles[0] | {parallelism, endpoints}' external-dp-cr.json Captured output:
jsonCopy { "parallelism": { "declared": { "dataParallel": 4, "tensorParallel": 2 }, "loadBalance": "External", "modes": { "expertParallel": true }, "source": { "complete": true, "kind": "ExtraArgs" } }, "endpoints": { "eligible": 1, "serving": { "state": "Confirmed", "value": 4 } } } endpoints.eligible (1) counts the admitted replica group r0, while endpoints.serving.value (4) confirms all four per-rank HTTP servers under http://external-dp-arm2-external-dp-router.gpustack-bench.svc:8000. If serving.value is 1, check --data-parallel-rank in extraArgs.
Step 3: Send requests per rank Verify each rank directly before testing router distribution. Forward each member (RANK=0..3) in separate terminals:
bashCopy RANK=0 RANK_POD=$(kubectl -n gpustack-bench get pods \ -l "app.kubernetes.io/instance=external-dp-arm2-external-dp,app.kubernetes.io/component=server,modeldeployment.gpustack.ai/member-index=$RANK" \ -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') kubectl -n gpustack-bench port-forward "pod/$RANK_POD" "$((18000 + RANK)):8000" Send non-streaming and streaming completions to every forwarded rank:
bashCopy for port in 18000 18001 18002 18003; do curl --fail-with-body --max-time 60 "http://127.0.0.1:$port/v1/completions" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"deepseek-v2-lite-chat","prompt":"The sky is","max_tokens":8,"temperature":0}' \ -o "rank-$port.json" jq '{text: .choices[0].text, finish_reason: .choices[0].finish_reason, completion_tokens: .usage.completion_tokens}' "rank-$port.json" curl --fail-with-body --no-buffer --max-time 60 "http://127.0.0.1:$port/v1/completions" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"deepseek-v2-lite-chat","prompt":"A GPU is","max_tokens":8,"temperature":0,"stream":true,"stream_options":{"include_usage":true}}' \ -o "rank-$port-stream.txt" done Confirm positive completion_tokens, non-empty text, and a trailing data: [DONE] on all four ports.
Step 4: Check router distribution Forward the router’s HTTP (:8000) and Prometheus (:9090) ports:
bashCopy ROUTER_POD=$(kubectl -n gpustack-bench get pods \ -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=external-dp-arm2-external-dp -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(any(.spec.containers[]; .name == "router")) | .metadata.name') kubectl -n gpustack-bench port-forward "pod/$ROUTER_POD" 18080:8000 19090:9090 Verify four healthy workers in /observer/endpoints (note: port :8000 blocks /observer/endpoints on newer Envoy-fronted router images; use pod-internal :9091 if :8000 returns 403), then send eight requests and compare per-worker counters:
bashCopy curl --fail-with-body http://127.0.0.1:19090/metrics > router-before.prom for request in 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8; do curl --fail-with-body --max-time 60 http://127.0.0.1:18080/v1/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"deepseek-v2-lite-chat","prompt":"The sky is","max_tokens":8,"temperature":0}' \ -o "router-$request.json" done curl --fail-with-body http://127.0.0.1:19090/metrics > router-after.prom grep -H '^vllm_router_processed_requests_total' router-before.prom router-after.prom Confirm that vllm_router_processed_requests_total increments on all four server-r0-m0..m3 workers. Across 1,088/1,088 measured requests with zero errors (plus 48 warm-ups and 1 calibration request = 1,137 total), router counters matched engine access logs on every rank (285 on m0 and 284 each on m1–m3); see Routing verification .
Cleanup If startup or routing stalls, inspect member logs and headless Service discovery before deleting:
bashCopy kubectl -n gpustack-bench logs \ -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=external-dp-arm2-external-dp,app.kubernetes.io/component=server \ -c main --prefix --tail=200 Stop all port-forward processes, delete the deployment, and confirm all eight GPUs release:
bashCopy kubectl -n gpustack-bench delete modeldeployment external-dp-arm2-external-dp --wait=true kubectl -n gpustack-bench get pods,services,deployments,workloads \ -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=external-dp-arm2-external-dp kubectl get devices -o json Limitations Measurements cover single-node cross-Pod TCP. Fixed External DP groups do not resize in place; edits to size roll the entire four-Pod replica (Admission constraints ). Troubleshooting Symptom Signal Resolution Member Pods stay Pending Kueue Workload unreserved Check kubectl -n gpustack-bench get workloads,events and AcceleratorType capacity; size: 4 × 2 GPUs requires 8 free GPUs. Ranks fail collective startup or hit EADDRINUSE Engine startup log error on m0..m3 Pin 1024 <= VLLM_PORT < 32768 (such as 19500) on all members and confirm --data-parallel-size 4, --data-parallel-rank $(GPUSTACK_MEMBER_INDEX), and --data-parallel-address $(GPUSTACK_REPLICA_LEADER_ADDRESS). Direct rank requests succeed, router returns 503 status.roles[].endpoints unconfirmed Inspect EndpointEligibility on ModelDeployment and router logs for endpoint qualification failures. Router sends traffic only to m0 Metrics increment on one worker only Confirm status.roles[0].parallelism.loadBalance reads External (--data-parallel-rank must be present in extraArgs). Leftover resources remain after delete Pods or Services still listed Inspect metadata.ownerReferences before deleting any residual objects manually. See also — External DP (vLLM and SGLang contracts) · External DP Benchmark (H100 latency and throughput vs wide TP) · Model Deployment Routing (router discovery and policies) · Elastic EP Walkthrough (in-place collective growth)
Next → Model Deployment Scaling Walkthrough — observe and activate replica autoscaling.

content:
Multi-Host Serving Walkthrough Span a single serving instance across multiple physical GPU hosts when a model’s memory footprint exceeds one node, using gang admission and operator-injected leader coordinates.
Contents Summary Step 1: Deploy distributed model Verification Step 4: Scale replica groups Cleanup Limitations Troubleshooting Summary Setting spec.roles[].size above 1 groups size fate-sharing member Pods into each serving replica under Kueue gang scheduling. Member m0 runs the Ray head and receives all Service HTTP traffic, while subordinate members (m1..mN) join m0 using injected discovery variables:
Object Scope Creator Purpose ModelArtifact namespace user Resolves deepseek-v2-lite-chat weights warmed onto both GPU hosts AcceleratorType cluster operator Discovered whole-GPU H100 pool requested by every member ModelDeployment namespace user Two-node (size: 2, 16-GPU) Ray serving group This 16-GPU layout (tensor parallelism (TP) = 8 within each node, pipeline parallelism (PP) = 2 across two nodes) is an illustrative configuration example. Complete Cluster preparation , GPU pool selection , and Model Prefetch in namespace gpustack-elastic with minReady: 2 across both GPU hosts so both m0 and m1 mount warm local weights.
Environment Item Value Nodes Two physical GPU hosts (8 GPUs each, 16 GPUs total) Fabric High-speed inter-node network (InfiniBand, RoCE, or AWS EFA) AcceleratorType gpustack--nvidia-h100-80gb-hbm3-linux-amd64 Namespace and model gpustack-elastic with ModelArtifact deepseek-v2-lite-chat Step 1: Deploy distributed model Because the operator does not synthesize multi-node Ray startup commands, multi-host roles use the take-over tier (roles[].command, which sets status.roles[].unmanaged: true; see Engine overrides ). Save multi-host.yaml:
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeployment metadata: name: deepseek-multi-host namespace: gpustack-elastic spec: model: name: deepseek-v2-lite-chat artifactRef: name: deepseek-v2-lite-chat engine: name: vLLM image: gpustack/runner:cuda13.0-vllm0.29.0 roles: - name: server kind: Server replicas: 1 size: 2 acceleratorType: gpustack--nvidia-h100-80gb-hbm3-linux-amd64 image: gpustack/runner:cuda13.0-vllm0.29.0 resources: accelerator: "8" command: - /bin/bash - -c - | set -euo pipefail if [ "${GPUSTACK_MEMBER_INDEX}" -eq 0 ]; then ray start --head --port=6379 --disable-usage-stats exec vllm serve /var/lib/gpustack/model --served-model-name deepseek-v2-lite-chat \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --pipeline-parallel-size "${GPUSTACK_REPLICA_SIZE}" \ --distributed-executor-backend ray else exec ray start --address="${GPUSTACK_REPLICA_LEADER_ADDRESS}:6379" --block fi Apply multi-host.yaml:
bashCopy kubectl apply -f multi-host.yaml kubectl -n gpustack-elastic get modeldeployment deepseek-multi-host Verification Step 2: Verify gang admission Confirm that Kueue admitted both members (deepseek-multi-host-server-r0-m0 and r0-m1) together and inspect the injected GPUSTACK_* coordinates on m1:
bashCopy kubectl -n gpustack-elastic get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=deepseek-multi-host -o wide kubectl -n gpustack-elastic exec deepseek-multi-host-server-r0-m1 -- env | grep '^GPUSTACK_' | sort Example output (illustrative):
textCopy GPUSTACK_MEMBER_INDEX=1 GPUSTACK_REPLICA_LEADER_ADDRESS=deepseek-multi-host-server-r0-m0.deepseek-multi-host-server-r0 GPUSTACK_REPLICA_SIZE=2 Verify that Service/deepseek-multi-host-server selects only leader m0 (member-index: "0"):
bashCopy kubectl -n gpustack-elastic get svc deepseek-multi-host-server -o jsonpath='{.spec.selector}{"\n"}' If either member stays Pending, inspect QuotaReserved and Workload conditions in Troubleshooting .
Step 3: Verify distributed inference Once m0 is serving on :8000 (take-over roles omit operator health probes unless configured in your entrypoint), send a completion request to Service/deepseek-multi-host-server:
bashCopy kubectl -n gpustack-elastic run test-client --rm -i --restart=Never \ --image=curlimages/curl -- \ curl -fsS http://deepseek-multi-host-server:8000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "deepseek-v2-lite-chat", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello distributed inference!"}], "max_tokens": 16 }' | jq '{model, finish_reason: .choices[0].finish_reason, tokens: .usage.completion_tokens}' Confirm "model": "deepseek-v2-lite-chat" and positive tokens. If curl fails to connect, inspect m0 and m1 container logs to confirm m1 joined the Ray head on :6379.
Step 4: Scale replica groups Increase replicas to add a second independent 16-GPU two-node group (requiring 32 GPUs total):
diffCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeployment metadata: name: deepseek-multi-host namespace: gpustack-elastic spec: roles: - name: server - replicas: 1 + replicas: 2 size: 2 Editing size, resources, or acceleratorType replaces whole replica groups one slot per pass rather than resizing Ray in place: the operator deletes an old replica and its Workload before admitting its replacement, so a replicas: 1 deployment experiences downtime during replacement (Rollout behavior ). Keep --tensor-parallel-size aligned with per-member resources.accelerator.
Cleanup Delete deepseek-multi-host and verify all 16 GPUs return full remaining credits:
bashCopy kubectl -n gpustack-elastic delete modeldeployment deepseek-multi-host kubectl -n gpustack-elastic get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=deepseek-multi-host kubectl get devices -o json | jq '[.items[].status.groups[].accelerators[] | {mode, remaining, allocatedSlices: (.allocatedSlices // 0)}]' Limitations All-or-nothing gang scheduling: all size members must reserve pool capacity together, or the entire replica waits Pending. Leader-only HTTP ingress: under internal load balancing (Internal LB), only m0 serves HTTP traffic. Full-replica replacement on size edits: changing size tears down and recreates each replica group rather than expanding live. Troubleshooting Symptom Signal Resolution ModelDeployment stuck in Starting, missing Workload QuotaReserved=False/PodGroupIncomplete Read QuotaReserved on ModelDeployment and inspect missing or rejected member Pods. Entire replica tears down and rebuilds ReplicasUpToDate=False/ReplacementInProgress One member Pod was evicted, drained, or deleted; because members share fate, the operator rebuilds the whole size-member replica. Check node and Kueue events. Replica stays Pending for quota QuotaReserved=False/Pending ClusterQueue lacks size × accelerator free GPUs across distinct hosts; free capacity or reduce replicas / size. m1 cannot join m0 Ray head Connection errors in m1 logs Verify headless Service DNS resolution for GPUSTACK_REPLICA_LEADER_ADDRESS and allow port 6379 plus Ray/NCCL ephemeral ports in NetworkPolicy. vLLM exits on invalid parallel world size Startup error in m0 logs Ensure --tensor-parallel-size equals per-member resources.accelerator (8) and --pipeline-parallel-size equals GPUSTACK_REPLICA_SIZE (2). See also — Configuration (multi-member roles and override tiers) · Prefill and Decode Walkthrough (disaggregated serving) · Elastic EP Walkthrough (in-place collective expansion) · External DP Walkthrough (fixed per-rank serving)
Next → Model Deployment — review serving contracts, routers, and benchmarks.

content:
Prefill and Decode Walkthrough Deploy a disaggregated serving topology with dedicated Prefill and Decode roles behind a managed llm-d-router, inspect joint Kueue admission, and verify completion requests through the router’s single endpoint.
Contents Summary Deployment Verification Cleanup Limitations Troubleshooting Summary Prefill/decode (PD) disaggregation separates compute-bound prompt prefill from memory-bandwidth-bound token decode. A managed router fronts both roles under one cluster HTTP endpoint, coordinates Mooncake KV cache transfer between roles, and waits for Kueue to admit the full role set atomically:
Object Scope Creator Purpose ModelArtifact namespace user Resolves and pins Qwen/Qwen3-32B weights ModelPrefetch namespace user Warms qwen3-32b onto the H100 node before serving AcceleratorType cluster operator H100 pool requested by both roles ModelDeployment namespace user Declares 1 Prefill and 2 Decode replicas behind llm-d-router Router Deployment and Service namespace operator Single HTTP entrypoint routing requests across roles On one 8-GPU H100 SXM5 node (6 GPUs per configuration), PD cut concurrency-16 long-prompt inter-token latency (ITL) p99 by 25.6×–27.8× (and cut mixed steady-stream max ITL by 23.3× with no p99 gain) at the cost of higher time to first token (TTFT) and lower total throughput in 15 of 16 cells; see Prefill and Decode Benchmark .
Environment Item Value Cluster Kubernetes v1.35.7; 1 CPU node and 1 GPU node (gpu-node-0) GPUs 8 × NVIDIA H100 80 GB HBM3 SXM5 (6 GPUs allocated to serving) Pool Captured on custom InstanceType bench-gpu; reusable manifest uses gpustack--nvidia-h100-80gb-hbm3-linux-amd64 Model Qwen/Qwen3-32B via ModelArtifact qwen3-32b (node model delivery) Engine and router vLLM gpustack/runner:cuda13.0-vllm0.30.0 with llm-d-router KV transfer Mooncake over TCP (mooncake_protocol: "tcp") Each engine Pod saw only its two assigned GPUs with private IPC, private /dev/shm, and no remote direct memory access (RDMA) interface. Intra-Pod tensor parallelism (TP) (*TP* = 2) used NVLink, while cross-Pod Mooncake KV transfer ran over TCP on eth0.
Deployment Step 1: Start disaggregated serving Enable node model delivery and run Model Prefetch in namespace gpustack-bench for ModelArtifact qwen3-32b (Qwen/Qwen3-32B at revision 9216db5781bf21249d130ec9da846c4624c16137). Wait until ModelPrefetch reports Available=True.
Save pd-deployment.yaml (1 Prefill × 2 GPUs + 2 Decode × 2 GPUs = 6 GPUs):
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeployment metadata: name: pd-arm2-pd namespace: gpustack-bench spec: model: name: Qwen/Qwen3-32B artifactRef: name: qwen3-32b engine: name: vLLM image: gpustack/runner:cuda13.0-vllm0.30.0 router: name: llm-d-router roles: - name: prefill kind: Prefill replicas: 1 size: 1 acceleratorType: gpustack--nvidia-h100-80gb-hbm3-linux-amd64 image: gpustack/runner:cuda13.0-vllm0.30.0 imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent resources: accelerator: "2" extraArgs: - --tensor-parallel-size - "2" - --max-model-len - "16384" - --max-num-seqs - "64" - --gpu-memory-utilization - "0.90" - --enable-scale-out - name: decode kind: Decode replicas: 2 size: 1 acceleratorType: gpustack--nvidia-h100-80gb-hbm3-linux-amd64 image: gpustack/runner:cuda13.0-vllm0.30.0 imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent resources: accelerator: "2" extraArgs: - --tensor-parallel-size - "2" - --max-model-len - "16384" - --max-num-seqs - "64" - --gpu-memory-utilization - "0.90" - --enable-scale-out Apply pd-deployment.yaml and confirm the deployment reaches Ready (1R1P2D):
bashCopy kubectl apply -f pd-deployment.yaml kubectl get modeldeployment pd-arm2-pd -n gpustack-bench \ -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,ENGINE:.spec.engine.name,ROLES:.status.roleSummary,PHASE:.status.phase kubectl get pods -n gpustack-bench -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=pd-arm2-pd \ -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,READY:.status.containerStatuses[*].ready,STATUS:.status.phase,NODE:.spec.nodeName Captured output:
textCopy NAME ENGINE ROLES PHASE pd-arm2-pd vLLM 1R1P2D Ready NAME READY STATUS NODE pd-arm2-pd-decode-2xglg 2/2 Running gpu-node-0 pd-arm2-pd-decode-r2zt4 2/2 Running gpu-node-0 pd-arm2-pd-prefill-xmjvs 1/1 Running gpu-node-0 pd-arm2-pd-router-6b9fcd6b75-5ngnj 2/2 Running gpu-node-0 Because this deployment has no Encode role, both roles set --enable-scale-out for router token counting (Router token counting ). If PHASE stays Starting, inspect deployment conditions and match the reason in Troubleshooting .
Step 2: Select the transfer backend Without resources.interface, the operator defaults spec.kvTransfer.backend to Mooncake over tcp. Inspect the rendered transfer flags across Prefill and Decode:
bashCopy kubectl -n gpustack-bench get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=pd-arm2-pd -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.metadata.labels["app.kubernetes.io/component"] != "router") | {pod: .metadata.name, role: .metadata.labels["app.kubernetes.io/component"], command: .spec.containers[0].command, proxyArgs: (.spec.initContainers // [] | map(select(.name=="routing-proxy"))[0].args)}' Captured output:
textCopy Prefill main: --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_connector_extra_config":{"mooncake_protocol":"tcp"}}' --kv-events-config enables the publisher on ports 5557 and 5558 --port 8000 Decode main: --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer","kv_connector_extra_config":{"mooncake_protocol":"tcp"}}' --port 8200 Decode routing-proxy init container: --port=8000 --model-server-port=8200 --kv-connector=mooncake --mooncake-bootstrap-port=8998 --secure-proxy=false To switch KV transfer to RDMA, request resources.interface on both roles (RDMA Walkthrough ) and verify InfiniBand transport in engine logs (InfiniBand RDMA comparison ). If you also attach a shared KV store via spec.kvCache.poolRef, declare it at creation because spec.kvCache is immutable (Deployment identity fields ).
Verification Step 3: Verify the router Confirm status.endpoint is populated and send a chat completion naming Qwen/Qwen3-32B:
bashCopy ENDPOINT=$(kubectl -n gpustack-bench get modeldeployment pd-arm2-pd -o jsonpath='{.status.endpoint}') echo "$ENDPOINT" kubectl -n gpustack-bench run test-client --rm -i --restart=Never \ --image=curlimages/curl -- \ curl -fsS "$ENDPOINT/v1/chat/completions" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-32B", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Explain prefill and decode disaggregation."}], "max_tokens": 16 }' Captured output:
textCopy http://pd-arm2-pd-router.gpustack-bench.svc:8000 Captured output (burst probe: 16 requests at concurrency 8, 8,192 input tokens, 64 output tokens):
jsonCopy {"requests":16,"concurrency":8,"input_tokens":8192,"output_tokens":64,"ok":16,"empty":0,"bad":0} If status.endpoint is empty or requests return 503, check RouterReady and EndpointEligibility conditions on ModelDeployment/pd-arm2-pd.
Step 4: Inspect joint admission Verify that Kueue admitted one Workload per engine replica (1 Prefill + 2 Decode = 3 Workloads):
bashCopy kubectl -n gpustack-bench get workloads Captured output:
textCopy NAME QUEUE RESERVED IN ADMITTED gpustack-fnv64-ab5121bc91ece976 gpustack-fnv64-889bba71d87d29e2 bench-gpu True gpustack-fnv64-ab5122bc91eceb29 gpustack-fnv64-889bba71d87d29e2 bench-gpu True gpustack-fnv64-d6b4e8ae20539d37 gpustack-fnv64-889bba71d87d29e2 bench-gpu True You can edit replicas independently on Prefill or Decode without rolling surviving replicas; see Rollout behavior .
Cleanup Delete pd-arm2-pd and confirm owned Pods, Services, and GPU allocations clear:
bashCopy kubectl -n gpustack-bench delete modeldeployment pd-arm2-pd kubectl -n gpustack-bench get pods,services -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=pd-arm2-pd Captured output (post-deletion Devices summary on gpu-node-0):
textCopy node: gpu-node-0 accelerator: NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 count: 8 remaining per accelerator: 1600000 Deleting ModelDeployment leaves prefetched weights in NodeModelStore untouched.
Limitations Measurements cover single-node TCP transfer; cross-node placement and RDMA, EFA, CANN, or ROCm transports require separate validation. See Prefill and Decode Benchmark for full concurrency sweeps and Router configuration for router lifecycle contracts. Troubleshooting Symptom Signal Resolution ModelDeployment stuck in Starting, missing Workloads QuotaReserved=False/PodGroupIncomplete Read the condition message on ModelDeployment and inspect unschedulable or rejected role Pods. Workloads stop requesting quota QuotaReserved=False/Parked Joint placement timed out and deactivated the Workloads; free pool capacity and reactivate the Workloads or recreate the ModelDeployment (re-applying identical YAML does not unpark). Partial preemption holds remaining GPUs QuotaReserved=False/PreemptedInPart Higher-priority work preempted part of the deployment; free pool quota so preempted replicas re-admit, or delete the ModelDeployment. status.endpoint stays empty with Router Pod present RouterReady=False/NoReadyReplicas Inspect Router Pod events and logs for image pull or readiness probe failures. No Router Deployment or Pod exists RouterReady=False/RenderFailed Read RouterReady on ModelDeployment and fix invalid fields under spec.router. KV transfer fails between Prefill and Decode Engine transfer errors in both role logs Verify matching Mooncake build versions in the runner image, valid resources.interface counts, and pod-to-pod network reachability. KVEventsPublishing=False/PublisherDisabled Expected when a publishing role’s --kv-events-config is missing on rendered Pods Informational condition reporting configuration rather than runtime failure; routed SGLang reports True/Publishing under sgl-router and True/NotApplicable under llm-d-router or sglang-gateway (Operator-owned keys ). RoleKindsReady=False Zero Ready replicas in Prefill or Decode Inspect Pod logs and events for the unready role named in the condition message. See also — Prefill and Decode (pairing and transfer contracts) · Prefill and Decode Benchmark (H100 SXM5 latency and throughput) · Model Deployment Routing (router policies and qualification)
Next → Encode, Prefill and Decode Walkthrough — disaggregate multimodal encode, prefill, and decode roles.
title: Prefill and Decode Walkthrough

content:
Online Runtime Control Walkthrough Tune live vLLM and SGLang serving parameters, pause and resume roles safely beside an active scaler, and verify restart replay and Elastic EP expansion without restarting worker Pods.
Contents Summary vLLM runtime changes SGLang runtime changes Verification Limitations Troubleshooting Summary ModelDeployment mounts gpustack-engine-sentinel read-only via PYTHONPATH on managed accelerated non-Encode roles without API-key Secrets. Managed routers enforce an Envoy inference allowlist on port 8000 and serve /observer/endpoints on pod-internal port 9091:
Capability Engine and router Verified behavior Envoy allowlist and router hash decoupling vLLM 0.32.0 + vllm-router, SGLang 0.5.22 + sglang-gateway 200 on /v1/chat/completions, 403 on control routes; editing requestTimeoutSeconds rolls only the router Live parameter tuning and auto-reset vLLM 0.32.0, SGLang 0.5.22 (including NGRAM speculative) Applies live via /gpustack/v1/runtime_config; removing keys restores boot_defaults with zero Pod restarts Version-gated unsupported parameters vLLM 0.32.0, SGLang 0.5.22 Reports UnsupportedEngineVersion (unsupportedFields); removing keys recovers Synced Role pause and scaler guard vLLM 0.32.0 + Active scaler, SGLang 0.5.22, 1P+1D llm-d-router /live=200, /ready=503, direct inference 503, scaler Blocked=True (RolePaused); resume restores 200 Same-UID restart latch and Elastic EP resize vLLM 0.32.0 (Qwen3-8B, DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat) Container restart rotates boot_id and replays parameters before readiness; Elastic EP grows 2 → 3 keeping master Pod UID Environment Item Value Cluster Kubernetes v1.35.7; 1 CPU node (cpu-d3) and 3 GPU nodes (gpu-h200-sxm, 1 GPU per node) Hardware 3 × NVIDIA H200 SXM 141 GB (gpustack--nvidia-h200-linux-amd64) Runners gpustack/runner:cuda13.0-vllm0.32.0, gpustack/runner:cuda13.0-sglang0.5.22 Models Qwen/Qwen3-8B (ModelArtifact qwen3-8b), deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat (deepseek-v2-lite-chat) Routers vllm-router, sglang-gateway, llm-d-router (gpustack/llm-router:v0.5.0) Enable node model delivery and complete Model Prefetch for qwen3-8b and deepseek-v2-lite-chat, then check cluster capacity:
bashCopy kubectl get nodes kubectl get acceleratortypes kubectl get nodemodelstores Captured output:
textCopy NAME STATUS ROLES AGE VERSION computeinstance-e01ah0pbdcbn4pngh5 Ready <none> 143m v1.35.7 computeinstance-e01dcjfh8cjnywrtf2 Ready <none> 143m v1.35.7 computeinstance-e01j5ns0wkmc376ygw Ready <none> 144m v1.35.7 computeinstance-e01nd7j1ezqp5jhwh3 Ready <none> 143m v1.35.7 NAME ENTRANCE ACCELERATOR(EX/SH/SL/PT) PHASE gpustack--nvidia-h200-linux-amd64 gpustack-fnv64-1bdcbb48b860c5ed 1/3 1/30 100/300 0/0 Active vLLM runtime changes Step 1: Deploy routed vLLM Save vllm-runtime-control.yaml and wait for qwen-vllm-rc to reach Ready:
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeployment metadata: name: qwen-vllm-rc namespace: default spec: model: name: Qwen/Qwen3-8B artifactRef: name: qwen3-8b engine: name: vLLM image: gpustack/runner:cuda13.0-vllm0.32.0 router: name: vllm-router requestTimeoutSeconds: 60 roles: - name: server kind: Server replicas: 1 size: 1 acceleratorType: gpustack--nvidia-h200-linux-amd64 resources: accelerator: "1" extraArgs: - --max-model-len=4096 - --max-num-seqs=64 - --max-num-batched-tokens=8192 - --gpu-memory-utilization=0.80 bashCopy kubectl apply -f vllm-runtime-control.yaml kubectl -n default wait --for=jsonpath='{.status.phase}'=Ready modeldeployment/qwen-vllm-rc --timeout=600s Record the initial worker Pod UID, patch spec.router.requestTimeoutSeconds to 90, and verify router hash decoupling:
bashCopy BEFORE_UID=$(kubectl -n default get pod -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=qwen-vllm-rc,app.kubernetes.io/component=server \ -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.uid}') kubectl -n default patch modeldeployment qwen-vllm-rc --type=merge \ -p '{"spec":{"router":{"requestTimeoutSeconds":90}}}' AFTER_UID=$(kubectl -n default get pod -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=qwen-vllm-rc,app.kubernetes.io/component=server \ -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.uid}') test "$BEFORE_UID" = "$AFTER_UID" && echo "worker UID unchanged" Expected behavior:
Zero runtime-control Secrets are created in default. Router port :8000 returns 200 on POST /v1/chat/completions and 403 on /gpustack/v1/ready, /gpustack/v1/runtime_config, /gpustack/v1/pause, /scale_elastic_ep, and /observer/endpoints, while pod-internal :9091/observer/endpoints returns 200. Updating requestTimeoutSeconds from 60 to 90 rolls only the router Deployment, keeping the worker Pod UID identical with restartCount: 0. Step 2: Tune and reset vLLM Patch spec.roles[0].runtimeControl.parameters live and inspect RuntimeControlSynced:
bashCopy kubectl -n default patch modeldeployment qwen-vllm-rc --type=json -p '[ {"op":"add","path":"/spec/roles/0/runtimeControl","value":{"parameters":{ "scheduling.maxActiveRequests":"24", "scheduling.maxBatchedTokens":"4096", "scheduling.longPrefillTokenThreshold":"1024" }}} ]' kubectl -n default get modeldeployment qwen-vllm-rc \ -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions[?(@.type=="RuntimeControlSynced")]}{"\n"}{.status.roles[0].runtimeControl}{"\n"}' Expected convergence, parameter reset, and version-gating behavior:
RuntimeControlSynced converges to True (Reason: Synced) with a non-empty appliedConfigDigest and zero worker restarts. Removing scheduling.longPrefillTokenThreshold resets only that parameter to its boot_defaults value while keeping maxActiveRequests=24 and maxBatchedTokens=4096 active under a new config digest. Setting version-gated keys absent from vllm0.32.0 (scheduling.cacheAwareWindow and scheduling.cacheAwareThreshold, or scheduling.maxInflightKVLoads and scheduling.maxAsyncKVLoadsPerStep on a 1P+1D decode role) reports RuntimeControlSynced=False (Reason: UnsupportedEngineVersion) with unsupportedFields populated and zero Pod restarts. Removing the unsupported keys restores Synced on the same worker Pod UID. Step 3: Pause scaled role With an Active ModelDeploymentScaler bound to qwen-vllm-rc, pause the server role:
bashCopy kubectl -n default patch modeldeployment qwen-vllm-rc --type=json \ -p '[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/roles/0/pause","value":true}]' kubectl -n default get modeldeploymentscaler \ -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{"\t"}{.status.conditions[?(@.type=="Blocked")]}{"\n"}{end}' Expected pause, resume, and drain behavior:
The operator removes modeldeployment.gpustack.ai/endpoint-eligible, drains active requests, and sets sentinel paused: true (Reason: Synced). Worker /gpustack/v1/live returns 200, while /gpustack/v1/ready and direct POST /v1/chat/completions return 503. The bound Active ModelDeploymentScaler sets Blocked=True (Reason: RolePaused) and suspends replica writes. On a 1P+1D deployment behind llm-d-router, pausing decode turns only decode /ready to 503 (prefill stays 200) and evicts only decode from /observer/endpoints (registry_revision 3 → 6). Setting pause: false and removing runtimeControl restores boot_defaults, removes the role ledger ConfigMap, sets RuntimeControlSynced=True (Reason: NotConfigured), and restores router 200 responses. Deleting the worker Pod executes python3 -m gpustack_engine_sentinel.drain with zero FailedPreStopHook events. SGLang runtime changes SGLang parameter tuning uses a separate SGLang 0.5.22 deployment (qwen-sglang-rc behind sglang-gateway), distinct from qwen-vllm-rc in Steps 1–3. Start from a Ready ModelDeployment configured with spec.engine.name: SGLang and a compatible spec.engine.image (substituting your deployment name if different), then patch all five scheduling parameters live:
bashCopy kubectl -n default patch modeldeployment qwen-sglang-rc --type=json -p '[ {"op":"add","path":"/spec/roles/0/runtimeControl","value":{"parameters":{ "scheduling.maxActiveRequests":"24", "scheduling.maxBatchedTokens":"2048", "scheduling.prefillMaxRequests":"12", "scheduling.scheduleConservativeness":"1.2", "scheduling.prefillDecodeInterval":"2" }}} ]' Captured output (/gpustack/v1/runtime_config readback from wt-sglang-server-7wwdr):
jsonCopy { "engine": "sglang", "boot_id": "ccf7515e-d667-49c5-ae79-ff88367160b3", "observed_generation": 2, "applied_config_digest": "sha256:2cb017f63c6377dc1c09d7bc8a9634b170067cde11fae3898a281e9dda41b25c", "ready": true, "paused": false, "boot_defaults": { "scheduling.maxActiveRequests": 64, "scheduling.maxBatchedTokens": 4096, "scheduling.prefillMaxRequests": null, "scheduling.scheduleConservativeness": 1.0, "scheduling.prefillDecodeInterval": 0 }, "values": { "scheduling.maxActiveRequests": 24, "scheduling.maxBatchedTokens": 2048, "scheduling.prefillMaxRequests": 12, "scheduling.scheduleConservativeness": 1.2, "scheduling.prefillDecodeInterval": 2 } } On a separate SGLang 0.5.22 deployment launched with --speculative-algorithm=NGRAM, speculative.acceptThresholdSingle: "0.85" and speculative.acceptThresholdAcc: "0.75" applied live with zero restarts, whereas speculative.draftBudgetFraction (DFlash/DSpark only) reported UnsupportedEngineVersion and recovered cleanly when removed.
Verification Verify ModelDeployment sentinel replay across container restarts and Elastic EP width changes:
Same-UID container restart latch replay: killing vLLM’s EngineCore process triggered an in-place container restart (restartCount: 0 → 1) on the same Pod UID. The restarted sentinel generated a fresh boot_id, held /gpustack/v1/ready fail-closed until the controller replayed maxActiveRequests=24 and maxBatchedTokens=4096 and sent /gpustack/v1/ack, and only then returned 200 on /gpustack/v1/ready. Folded Elastic EP expansion (DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat): widening runtimeControl.parameters["elastic.dataParallelWidth"] from "2" to "3" preserved the master Pod UID, converged ElasticResize=True (Reason: NoRefusal), advanced /gpustack/v1/runtime_config to ranks=3 and membership_epoch=2, and replayed scheduling.maxActiveRequests=16 across all three ranks. Limitations scheduling.ppMaxMicroBatchSize requires --pp-size > 1 with resources.accelerator >= 2 per member and was admission-tested only on this 1-GPU-per-node H200 cluster. Parameters absent from vllm0.32.0 (cacheAware*, maxInflightKVLoads, maxAsyncKVLoadsPerStep) and sglang0.5.22 NGRAM (draftBudgetFraction) were verified through the UnsupportedEngineVersion rejection and recovery path. Behavior on other engines or hardware follows Online Runtime Control . Troubleshooting Symptom Signal Resolution RuntimeControlSynced=False Reason: UnsupportedEngineVersion Inspect status.roles[].runtimeControl.unsupportedFields on ModelDeployment, then remove those keys or upgrade the runner image. Control routes return 403 on router :8000 Envoy inference allowlist active Expected security boundary; query /observer/endpoints on the router pod’s internal port (:9091 or :9090) rather than :8000. ModelDeploymentScaler stops scaling Blocked=True (Reason: RolePaused) Expected while any target role sets pause: true; set pause: false on ModelDeployment to resume autoscaling. Restarted container stays unready briefly /gpustack/v1/ready returns 503 after container restart Sentinel holds readiness fail-closed on a new boot_id until the worker replays runtimeControl.parameters and /gpustack/v1/ack; check worker connectivity if it does not clear. Router fails to render RouterReady=False/RenderFailed No Router Pod exists when rendering fails; inspect RouterReady on ModelDeployment and fix spec.router. See also — Online Runtime Control (parameter catalog and status reasons) · Elastic EP Walkthrough (eight-GPU H100 collective expansion)
Next → Multi-Host Serving Walkthrough — span a serving group across multiple GPU hosts.
title: Online Runtime Control Walkthrough

content:
Model Deployment Scaling Walkthrough Attach a ModelDeploymentScaler in Shadow mode to inspect replica recommendations, compare Proportional, TokenThroughput, Predictive, and catalog-prior algorithms, then switch to Active mode to observe scale-out and graceful replica retirement.
Contents Summary Environment Scaler deployment Step 3: Choose an algorithm Live scaling Verification Cleanup Troubleshooting Summary Start one vLLM prefill/decode (PD) target, verify recommendations safely in Shadow mode, select a scaling algorithm (including InferenceX catalog priors or encode/prefill/decode (EPD) role ratios), and switch to Active mode:
Object Scope Creator Purpose ModelArtifact namespace user Resolves Qwen/Qwen3-8B weights (qwen3-8b) AcceleratorType cluster operator Whole-GPU pool requested by each role replica ModelDeployment namespace user Disaggregated PD target whose replicas the scaler controls ModelDeploymentScaler namespace user Autoscaling policy evaluated in Shadow and enforced in Active Manifests below are reusable configuration examples; captured lifecycle results from the standalone H100 and H200 runs are labeled explicitly in Verification and Model Deployment Scaling Benchmark .
Environment Item Value GPUs 2 free GPUs initially, up to 4 GPUs at max scale (1 GPU per replica) AcceleratorType Reusable example uses gpustack--nvidia-h100-80gb-hbm3-linux-amd64 (substitute an Active pool from kubectl get acctype) Namespace gpustack-bench Model Qwen/Qwen3-8B via ModelArtifact qwen3-8b at revision b968826d9c46dd6066d109eabc6255188de91218 Tools kubectl, jq, and Python 3 with aiohttp (plus a repo checkout for bench_client.py) Prerequisites Complete Cluster preparation and warm qwen3-8b in gpustack-bench via Model Prefetch . Confirm no other ModelDeploymentScaler already binds the target deployment; see Model Deployment Scaling and GitOps sync .
Scaler deployment Step 1: Deploy scaling target Save scaling-target.yaml (replace acceleratorType if not running on H100):
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeployment metadata: name: autoscaling-vllm-pd namespace: gpustack-bench spec: model: name: Qwen/Qwen3-8B artifactRef: name: qwen3-8b engine: name: vLLM image: gpustack/runner:cuda13.0-vllm0.30.0 router: name: llm-d-router roles: - name: prefill kind: Prefill replicas: 1 size: 1 acceleratorType: gpustack--nvidia-h100-80gb-hbm3-linux-amd64 resources: accelerator: "1" extraArgs: - --tensor-parallel-size - "1" - --max-model-len - "16384" - --max-num-seqs - "64" - --gpu-memory-utilization - "0.90" - --enable-scale-out env: - name: VLLM_HTTP_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE value: "3600" - name: decode kind: Decode replicas: 1 size: 1 acceleratorType: gpustack--nvidia-h100-80gb-hbm3-linux-amd64 resources: accelerator: "1" extraArgs: - --tensor-parallel-size - "1" - --max-model-len - "16384" - --max-num-seqs - "64" - --gpu-memory-utilization - "0.90" - --enable-scale-out env: - name: VLLM_HTTP_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE value: "3600" Apply scaling-target.yaml and wait until PHASE=Ready (1R1P1D) before generating load:
bashCopy kubectl apply -f scaling-target.yaml kubectl -n gpustack-bench get modeldeployment autoscaling-vllm-pd -w --enable-scale-out enables router token counting (Router token counting ), and VLLM_HTTP_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE=3600 matches the benchmark configuration (it reduces, without eliminating, scale-out connection drops).
Step 2: Review Shadow recommendations Save scaling-policy.yaml in Shadow mode so the scaler computes recommendations without writing target replicas:
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeploymentScaler metadata: name: autoscale-vllm-pd namespace: gpustack-bench spec: targetRef: name: autoscaling-vllm-pd mode: Shadow sampling: intervalSeconds: 10 roles: - name: prefill minReplicas: 1 maxReplicas: 2 - name: decode minReplicas: 1 maxReplicas: 2 ratios: - numeratorRole: prefill denominatorRole: decode target: "1" # soft preference; add min/max only when hard ratio bounds are required algorithm: type: Proportional proportional: metric: RunningRequests tolerance: "0.1" roleTargets: - name: prefill target: "3" - name: decode target: "3" bashCopy kubectl apply -f scaling-policy.yaml kubectl -n gpustack-bench get mds autoscale-vllm-pd \ -o jsonpath='{range .status.conditions[*]}{.type}={.status} {.reason}{"\n"}{end}' kubectl -n gpustack-bench get modeldeployment autoscaling-vllm-pd -o json | jq '{replicas: [.spec.roles[] | {name, replicas}], binding: .metadata.annotations["modeldeployment.gpustack.ai/scaler-binding"]}' Confirm Bound=True, Active=False (Reason: ShadowMode), unchanged replicas: 1, and binding: null. Inspect status.roles[].rawRecommendedReplicas, constrainedReplicas, signalState, and reason together.
Create an in-cluster load driver Pod (default/bench-driver) if absent, and send a 45 s baseline load against the router Service:
bashCopy kubectl -n default run bench-driver --image=python:3.11-slim --restart=Never --command -- sleep infinity kubectl -n default wait pod/bench-driver --for=condition=Ready --timeout=300s kubectl -n default exec bench-driver -- python3 -m pip install aiohttp bashCopy BENCH_INCLUSTER=1 python3 .agents/skills/gpustack-operator-benchmark/scripts/bench_client.py load \ --endpoint http://autoscaling-vllm-pd-router.gpustack-bench.svc:8000 \ --model Qwen/Qwen3-8B --arm shadow --suite autoscaling --label baseline \ --input-tokens 1024 --output-tokens 256 --concurrency 2 --duration 45 \ --out /tmp/scaler-shadow.json --requests-out /tmp/scaler-shadow-requests.jsonl If bench_client.py reports local fallback, stop and fix default/bench-driver access because cluster-internal DNS will not resolve locally.
Step 3: Choose an algorithm When switching algorithms in scaling-policy.yaml, replace the entire spec.algorithm block (admission rejects sub-blocks that do not match algorithm.type):
Choice Target scenario Configuration guidance Predictive + capacityPrior Latency-sensitive serving and traffic ramps where replica startup (~76 s on H200) must start ahead of peak load Set horizonSeconds above startup time (180–300 s), keep headroom: "0.75", and cap step bursts via behavior.scaleUp.maxStepReplicas. TokenThroughput + capacityPrior Variable prompt lengths and prefix caching where GPU replica-seconds should track sustained token demand Use capacityPrior (headroom: "0.75") or set manual targets at 70–75% of single-replica saturation. Proportional Uniform request shapes using RunningRequests or QueueDepth without offline token sweeps Set roleTargets[].target to per-replica concurrency within TTFT targets (Proportional rejects capacityPrior). Token throughput diffCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeploymentScaler metadata: name: autoscale-vllm-pd namespace: gpustack-bench spec: algorithm: - type: Proportional - proportional: - metric: RunningRequests - tolerance: "0.1" - roleTargets: - - name: prefill - target: "3" - - name: decode - target: "3" + type: TokenThroughput + tokenThroughput: + prefillTargetTokensPerSecond: "1200" + decodeTargetTokensPerSecond: "300" Allow two successive metric samples before evaluating rate recommendations. Before testing sustained SGLang PD traffic over TCP, review the SGLang TCP limitation .
Predictive diffCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeploymentScaler metadata: name: autoscale-vllm-pd namespace: gpustack-bench spec: algorithm: - type: Proportional - proportional: - metric: RunningRequests - tolerance: "0.1" - roleTargets: - - name: prefill - target: "3" - - name: decode - target: "3" + type: Predictive + predictive: + horizonSeconds: 30 + minPoints: 2 + qLevel: "0.5" + qTrend: "0.3" + prefillTokenCapacityPerReplica: "2000" + decodeTokenCapacityPerReplica: "2000" + tokenThroughput: + prefillTargetTokensPerSecond: "1200" + decodeTargetTokensPerSecond: "300" Nested tokenThroughput targets act as fallback while the predictor collects minPoints; inspect status.predictors and role reasons to distinguish forecast planning from fallback (Scale-out timing ).
Catalog capacity estimates spec.algorithm.capacityPrior resolves omitted TokenThroughput or Predictive capacities from an embedded InferenceX ModelDeploymentScalerCapacityPriorCatalog (when catalogRef is omitted) or from a same-namespace ConfigMap (priors.yaml key by default; empty catalogRef: {} is rejected). See Catalog matching requirements and Capacity priors .
Because the embedded catalog omits Qwen/Qwen3-8B, create a reviewed ConfigMap/autoscaling-priors in gpustack-bench first (if multiple catalog quantizations match, pass --quantization or annotate the deployment with worker.gpustack.ai/precision):
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeploymentScaler metadata: name: autoscale-vllm-pd-prior namespace: gpustack-bench spec: targetRef: name: autoscaling-vllm-pd mode: Shadow roles: - name: prefill minReplicas: 1 maxReplicas: 2 - name: decode minReplicas: 3 maxReplicas: 6 ratios: - numeratorRole: decode denominatorRole: prefill min: "3" max: "3" algorithm: type: TokenThroughput tokenThroughput: ttftTargetMilliseconds: "2000" itlTargetMilliseconds: "50" capacityPrior: catalogRef: name: autoscaling-priors headroom: "0.75" For a single-role Server target (catalog-server), you can also combine an explicit fallback override with catalog-resolved forecast capacity:
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeployment metadata: name: catalog-server namespace: gpustack-bench spec: model: name: Qwen/Qwen3-8B artifactRef: name: qwen3-8b engine: name: vLLM image: gpustack/runner:cuda13.0-vllm0.30.0 roles: - name: server kind: Server replicas: 1 size: 1 acceleratorType: gpustack--nvidia-h100-80gb-hbm3-linux-amd64 resources: accelerator: "1" --- apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeploymentScaler metadata: name: autoscale-server namespace: gpustack-bench spec: targetRef: name: catalog-server roles: - name: server minReplicas: 1 maxReplicas: 2 algorithm: type: Predictive predictive: horizonSeconds: 30 minPoints: 2 tokenThroughput: serverTargetTokensPerSecond: "1200" # Explicit fallback override ttftTargetMilliseconds: "500" # required for Server catalog resolution itlTargetMilliseconds: "50" # required for Server catalog resolution capacityPrior: catalogRef: name: autoscaling-priors key: priors.yaml headroom: "0.75" Verify resolved priors and conditions:
bashCopy kubectl -n gpustack-bench get mds autoscale-server -o json | jq '{priors: .status.resolvedCapacityPriors, conditions: [.status.conditions[] | select(.type == "CapacityPriorsReady" or .type == "Blocked")]}' When a target matches an embedded catalog profile, omit both serverTargetTokensPerSecond and catalogRef:
diffCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeploymentScaler metadata: name: autoscale-server namespace: gpustack-bench spec: algorithm: type: Predictive predictive: tokenThroughput: - serverTargetTokensPerSecond: "1200" ttftTargetMilliseconds: "500" itlTargetMilliseconds: "50" capacityPrior: - catalogRef: - name: autoscaling-priors - key: priors.yaml headroom: "0.75" To switch back to manual capacities, remove capacityPrior and supply explicit capacity fields:
diffCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeploymentScaler metadata: name: autoscale-server namespace: gpustack-bench spec: algorithm: type: Predictive predictive: + serverTokenCapacityPerReplica: "2000" tokenThroughput: + serverTargetTokensPerSecond: "1200" - capacityPrior: - headroom: "0.75" CREATE rejects an unresolved catalog prior when the target already exists, whereas UPDATE admits with a warning so you can switch to Shadow, remove capacityPrior, or supply manual capacities while reconciliation sets CapacityPriorsReady=False and Blocked=True.
Encoder replica ratios For a multimodal EPD target (Encode, Prefill and Decode Walkthrough ), couple encode replica counts via ratios rather than an encode token-throughput target:
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeploymentScaler metadata: name: qwen-scaler namespace: gpustack-bench spec: targetRef: name: epd-arm3-epd roles: - name: encode minReplicas: 1 maxReplicas: 2 - name: prefill minReplicas: 1 maxReplicas: 2 - name: decode minReplicas: 1 maxReplicas: 2 algorithm: type: TokenThroughput tokenThroughput: prefillTargetTokensPerSecond: "2000" decodeTargetTokensPerSecond: "800" ratios: - numeratorRole: prefill denominatorRole: decode target: "1" - numeratorRole: encode denominatorRole: prefill target: "1" Live scaling Step 4: Activate scaling Change spec.mode to Active in scaling-policy.yaml, apply it, and confirm Bound=True and Active=True:
bashCopy kubectl apply -f scaling-policy.yaml kubectl -n gpustack-bench get mds autoscale-vllm-pd -o json | jq '{conditions: .status.conditions, binding: .status.binding, roles: .status.roles}' Do not hand-edit target spec.roles[].replicas while the scaler holds Active=True; the scaler owns those replica fields for its active binding term. Drive concurrency-24 load in one terminal and watch scale-out in another:
bashCopy BENCH_INCLUSTER=1 python3 .agents/skills/gpustack-operator-benchmark/scripts/bench_client.py load \ --endpoint http://autoscaling-vllm-pd-router.gpustack-bench.svc:8000 \ --model Qwen/Qwen3-8B --arm active --suite autoscaling --label ramp \ --input-tokens 1024 --output-tokens 256 --concurrency 24 --duration 75 \ --out /tmp/scaler-ramp.json --requests-out /tmp/scaler-ramp-requests.jsonl bashCopy kubectl -n gpustack-bench get modeldeployment autoscaling-vllm-pd -w kubectl -n gpustack-bench get mds autoscale-vllm-pd -o json | jq '{roles: .status.roles, commit: .status.lastCommit, pending: .status.pendingCohort, conditions: .status.conditions}' kubectl -n gpustack-bench get pods,workloads Verify that lastCommit advances, new Pods reach Ready, and router per-worker request counters increase on the added replicas. If pendingCohort stays non-null, inspect Kueue quota and Pod events before raising maxReplicas.
Step 5: Observe replica retirement Drop load to concurrency 2 for 600 s (exceeding the default 300 s scale-down stabilization window plus router withdrawal and drain budgets; setting 0 stores the 300 s default):
bashCopy BENCH_INCLUSTER=1 python3 .agents/skills/gpustack-operator-benchmark/scripts/bench_client.py load \ --endpoint http://autoscaling-vllm-pd-router.gpustack-bench.svc:8000 \ --model Qwen/Qwen3-8B --arm active --suite autoscaling --label cooldown \ --input-tokens 1024 --output-tokens 256 --concurrency 2 --duration 600 \ --out /tmp/scaler-cooldown.json --requests-out /tmp/scaler-cooldown-requests.jsonl Poll retirement and scale-down status during cooldown:
bashCopy kubectl -n gpustack-bench get modeldeployment autoscaling-vllm-pd -o json | jq '{roles: .status.roles, retirement: .status.retirement}' kubectl -n gpustack-bench get mds autoscale-vllm-pd -o json | jq '{roles: .status.roles, lastScaleDown: .status.lastScaleDown, conditions: .status.conditions}' Retiring replicas step through endpoint withdrawal (Disqualified), Draining, and Deleting (Pause and retirement ). Keep maxReplicas at or above current counts so planning does not block on BoundsConflict.
Verification Captured output from the standalone single-role Server lifecycle verification run:
textCopy PASS | the target's replica count rises under load | the count of the role server is 2 while the heavy phase runs PASS | the scaler records the vector it committed | the scaler committed server=2 on term 1 PASS | the replica count falls when the scaler is narrowed | the count of the role server is 1 after the scaler was narrowed PASS | the retirement that carried the count down is observed | the target carried the retirement states Disqualified,Draining That standalone Server run verified replica scale-out, new-replica traffic, and Disqualified → Draining retirement to 1 Ready survivor, while failing its zero-error gate due to request errors during scale-out (Retirement ).
Catalog prior resolution Catalog.Resolve converts an offline benchmark curve into a per-replica token capacity seed. Below is the shipped profile (Server, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-0528, fp8, sglang, amd-mi325x, gpusPerReplica: 8, tensorParallel: 8) from pkg/worker/scaling/priors/priors.yaml (illustrative tokens/s/MW assumes a ~0.0115 MW 8-GPU node; interactivity is 1000 / ITL P90):
Concurrency Per-replica tokens/s tokens/s/MW TTFT P90 (ms) ITL P90 (ms) tokens/s/user 4 1875.02 ~163k 665.4 16.95 59.0 8 3167.82 ~275k 1001.7 18.47 54.1 16 4988.96 ~434k 1119.7 20.82 48.0 32 6496.65 ~565k 1516.6 28.32 35.3 64 7630.2 ~663k 2636.2 44.44 22.5 Configure a scaler holding P90 TTFT <= 2000 ms and P90 ITL <= 33 ms (~30.3 tokens/s/user):
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeploymentScaler metadata: name: deepseek-scaler namespace: gpustack-bench spec: targetRef: name: deepseek-server roles: - name: server minReplicas: 1 maxReplicas: 4 algorithm: type: TokenThroughput tokenThroughput: latencyQuantile: "0.90" # default: 0.95 ttftTargetMilliseconds: "2000" itlTargetMilliseconds: "33" capacityPrior: headroom: "0.75" Resolution proceeds in four steps:
Matches the normalized (role, model, quantization, engine, hardware, topology) tuple automatically. Filters sweep points against the P90 targets: concurrencies 4–32 pass, while 64 breaches both (HigherLoadSLOFailure; if all points pass, capacity caps at 64 as ExplicitSaturation without extrapolation). Picks the highest-throughput feasible point (concurrency: 32 at 6496.65 tokens/s). Multiplies by headroom: 6496.65 × 0.75 = 4872.49 tokens/s per replica, so 15,000 tokens/s demand plans ceil(15000 / 4872.49) = 4 replicas. Capacity estimate comparison To compare frozen-manual, tuned-manual, and catalog configurations on a single-Server ModelDeployment (no router, kvCache, or kvTransfer, and offline evaluationTraceID disjoint from fitRunIDs), copy .agents/skills/gpustack-operator-benchmark/manifests/autoscaling-comparison.json, fill in REPLACE_WITH_* placeholders, and validate offline:
bashCopy bash .agents/skills/gpustack-operator-benchmark/cases/case-5-autoscaling.sh \ --capacity-comparison --config FILE --out DIR --validate-only python3 .agents/skills/gpustack-operator-benchmark/scripts/autoscaling_report.py \ ARM_DIR --out REPORT_JSON --validate-only makes zero cluster calls and exits 0 (valid) or 2 (input error); --execute runs at least three repeats per configuration and writes comparison.json (0 success, 1 round/cleanup failure, 2 validation error, 130 interrupt). See Capacity estimate comparison for the 18-round H200 benchmark results.
Cleanup Delete the ModelDeploymentScaler first so its finalizer clears the scaler-binding annotation, then delete the target ModelDeployment:
bashCopy kubectl -n gpustack-bench delete modeldeploymentscaler autoscale-vllm-pd --wait=true kubectl -n gpustack-bench get modeldeployment autoscaling-vllm-pd -o json | jq '.metadata.annotations["modeldeployment.gpustack.ai/scaler-binding"]' kubectl -n gpustack-bench delete modeldeployment autoscaling-vllm-pd --wait=true Troubleshooting Symptom Signal Resolution Target replicas stay at 1 Active=False (Reason: ShadowMode) Expected in Shadow mode; set spec.mode: Active on ModelDeploymentScaler when ready. Apply rejected with AlreadyBound Another scaler owns scaler-binding Edit the existing ModelDeploymentScaler, or delete it and wait for binding release first. Reason: InvalidBinding Corrupted scaler-binding annotation on target Remove or repair modeldeployment.gpustack.ai/scaler-binding on the target ModelDeployment. Reason: BoundsConflict or RatioConflict Live replica counts fall outside policy bands Widen minReplicas/maxReplicas or ratios on ModelDeploymentScaler to include current counts. MetricsReady=False/WaitingForMetrics Missing successive metric samples Wait at least two sampling intervals and verify Ready role Pods expose engine metrics. CapacityPriorsReady=False CapacityPriorUnresolved, InsufficientLoadCoverage, or IncompatibleMetric Check catalogRef, precision annotation/--quantization, single-Pod role eligibility, and latency targets, or switch to explicit manual capacities. Reason: ResourceExhausted Scale-out blocked by Kueue quota Inspect status.pendingCohort, Workloads, and ClusterQueue capacity. Reason: ScaleDownAborted Replica drain aborted Inspect status.lastScaleDown and target status.retirement; wait out the abort cooldown after fixing drain blockers. Reason: PacingBounded Cooldown or step cap still active Wait for stabilizationWindowSeconds and retirement grace timers to elapse. Router errors during scale-out Client 5xx or connection resets Capture router and engine logs; VLLM_HTTP_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE reduces but does not eliminate all scale-out resets. SGLang TCP KV transfer errors Engine port-exhaustion logs Enable model-deployment-tcp-tw-reuse after permitting net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse on kubelets. See also — Model Deployment Scaling (autoscaler contracts and capacity priors) · Model Deployment Scaling Benchmark (H100 and H200 measurements) · Online Runtime Control (role pause guard and retirement lifecycle)
