title: Model Deployment Scaling Walkthrough

content:
RDMA Networking Walkthrough Request and verify remote direct memory access (RDMA) endpoints alongside accelerators, align NICs and GPUs on the same non-uniform memory access (NUMA) socket through kubelet, and attach fabric interfaces to prefill/decode (PD) roles and KV cache backends.
Contents Summary Node configuration Workload configuration AWS EFA configuration Limitations Troubleshooting Summary Device Manager discovers NICs from /sys/class/net and InfiniBand verbs devices from /sys/class/infiniband, checks link health, and advertises shared (rdma.shared), exclusive (rdma), and single-root I/O virtualization (SR-IOV) resource keys. Nodes with at least one healthy endpoint carry feature.gpustack.ai/rdma.capable=true (RDMA Operations ).
Object Scope Creator Purpose Pod namespace user Standalone workload requesting RDMA endpoints alongside GPUs ModelDeployment namespace user Managed serving roles requesting fabric counts via roles[].resources.interface KVCacheBackend cluster administrator Shared Mooncake cache configured for RDMA or EFA transport Environment Item Value Cluster Kubernetes with GPUStack installed (illustrative configuration examples) Hardware Workload Nodes equipped with active RDMA-capable NICs (or AWS EFA adapters) Tools kubectl, jq, and node SSH access for Step 2 kubelet configuration Node configuration Step 1: Request RDMA endpoints Inspect discovered RDMA interfaces in Devices and verify positive allocatable rdma keys on your target Node:
bashCopy kubectl get devices <node> -o json | jq '[.spec.interfaces[] | (., (.virtualFunctions // [])[])] | map(select(.rdma or .link)) | map({name, pciBusId, rdmaDevice, link})' kubectl get node <node> -o json | jq '.status.allocatable | with_entries(select(.key | contains("gpustack.ai/rdma")))' Example output (illustrative):
jsonCopy { "device.gpustack.ai/rdma": "2", "device.gpustack.ai/rdma.shared": "200" } If allocatable counts are "0" or absent, inspect link states and any DevicesRDMASelectionPolicy in Troubleshooting .
Next, look up the pool’s LocalQueue in team-a (kubectl -n team-a get localqueues), substitute its gpustack-fnv64-<hash> name, and apply trainer-0.yaml:
yamlCopy apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: name: trainer-0 namespace: team-a labels: kueue.x-k8s.io/queue-name: gpustack-fnv64-<hash> # required for Kueue admission spec: restartPolicy: Never containers: - name: trainer image: ubuntu:24.04 command: - sleep - "3600" resources: limits: nvidia.com/gpu: "1" device.gpustack.ai/rdma.shared: "1" # prefer rdma.shared unless exclusive HCA ownership is needed bashCopy kubectl apply -f trainer-0.yaml kubectl -n team-a wait --for=condition=Ready pod/trainer-0 --timeout=120s kubectl -n team-a exec trainer-0 -- sh -c 'env | grep -E "^(GPUSTACK_RDMA_DEVICES|NCCL_IB_HCA)=" && ls /dev/infiniband' Example output (illustrative):
textCopy GPUSTACK_RDMA_DEVICES=mlx5_0 NCCL_IB_HCA==mlx5_0 rdma_cm uverbs0 Confirm GPUSTACK_RDMA_DEVICES is non-empty and /dev/infiniband/uverbs* exists; see Injected devices . GetPreferredAllocation spreads rdma.shared tokens across distinct eligible HCAs before repeating an HCA, so requesting more shared units than eligible HCAs yields one uverbs node per HCA.
Step 2: Configure kubelet alignment By default, kubelet allocates GPUs and NICs independently across sockets. Enforce NUMA co-location in /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml on each GPU node (Enabling NUMA alignment ):
diffCopy apiVersion: kubelet.config.k8s.io/v1beta1 kind: KubeletConfiguration +topologyManagerPolicy: restricted +topologyManagerScope: container Restart kubelet on the host and verify the active policy from the API server:
bashCopy systemctl restart kubelet kubectl get --raw /api/v1/nodes/<node>/proxy/configz | jq '.kubeletconfig | {topologyManagerPolicy, topologyManagerScope}' Example output (illustrative):
jsonCopy { "topologyManagerPolicy": "restricted", "topologyManagerScope": "container" } With restricted and container scope, single-socket requests bind GPUs and NICs on one NUMA node, and multi-socket requests pack into the fewest NUMA nodes. If a Pod fails placement with TopologyAffinityError, free co-located GPU/NIC pairs or verify both resources sit in the same container.
Workload configuration Step 3: Request interfaces per role In ModelDeployment, request fabric adapters through roles[].resources.interface rather than raw extended resource keys. Admission accepts interface only when an active RDMA or EFA transfer path uses it (such as a managed PD pair or an RDMA/EFA KVCacheBackend). Save and apply qwen-pd.yaml:
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeployment metadata: name: qwen-pd namespace: team-a spec: model: name: Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct engine: name: vLLM image: gpustack/runner:cuda13.0-vllm0.29.0 router: name: llm-d-router kvTransfer: backend: Mooncake roles: - name: prefill kind: Prefill replicas: 1 acceleratorType: gpustack--nvidia-a10g-linux-amd64 resources: accelerator: "2" interface: "2" # 1 -> rdma.shared: 1; >1 -> rdma: N distinct physical HCAs - name: decode kind: Decode replicas: 1 acceleratorType: gpustack--nvidia-a10g-linux-amd64 resources: accelerator: "2" interface: "2" bashCopy kubectl apply -f qwen-pd.yaml kubectl -n team-a get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=qwen-pd,app.kubernetes.io/component=prefill \ -o json | jq '.items[0].spec.containers[0].resources.limits' Example output (illustrative):
jsonCopy { "device.gpustack.ai/rdma": "2", "nvidia.com/gpu": "2" } If admission rejects the manifest with no effective RDMA or EFA transfer leg uses the requested interfaces, ensure both Prefill and Decode roles are managed (no custom command) with a router, or attach an RDMA KV cache pool from Step 4.
Step 4: Configure RDMA cache Switch mooncake-dram from Step 1 of Shared Cache from TCP to RDMA and allocate two fabric interfaces per member:
diffCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: KVCacheBackend metadata: name: mooncake-dram spec: type: Mooncake + transport: + protocol: RDMA connection: managed: leader: {} members: - nodeSelector: kubernetes.io/os: linux medium: DRAM capacityPerMember: 8Gi + fabricInterfaceCount: 2 Verify that the backend rolls its member DaemonSet and returns to Ready with expected capacity:
bashCopy kubectl get kvcb mooncake-dram If MembersMounted turns False, check that every node matched by nodeSelector advertises at least two healthy device.gpustack.ai/rdma endpoints (Member groups ).
AWS EFA configuration AWS Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) devices expose vpc.amazonaws.com/efa rather than standard verbs completion queues, so device.gpustack.ai/rdma* stays zero on EFA nodes. Set transport.protocol: EFA on KVCacheBackend:
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: KVCacheBackend metadata: name: mooncake-efa spec: type: Mooncake transport: protocol: EFA connection: managed: leader: {} members: - nodeSelector: node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: c6in.32xlarge medium: DRAM capacityPerMember: 64Gi fabricInterfaceCount: 2 For ModelDeployment roles on EFA, enable Setting/aws-efa-enabled in gpustack-system and supply runner images built with libfabric and EFA-enabled Mooncake:
bashCopy kubectl -n gpustack-system patch setting aws-efa-enabled --type merge -p '{"spec":{"value":"true"}}' kubectl -n gpustack-system get setting aws-efa-enabled -o jsonpath='{.spec.value}{"\n"}' Limitations Kueue does not meter device.gpustack.ai/rdma* or vpc.amazonaws.com/efa in ClusterQueue quotas, so Kueue can admit a Workload that then waits Pending until node fabric frees up (RDMA Operations ). Kubelet NUMA policy trade-offs (none, restricted, single-numa-node) are detailed in Enabling NUMA alignment and Result format . Troubleshooting Symptom Signal Resolution rdma keys report 0 allocatable Links Failed or filtered out by policy Inspect kubectl get devices <node> -o json and DevicesRDMASelectionPolicy (Selection policy ); fix cabling, subnet manager, or policy filters (never hand-edit Devices status). Workload admitted by Kueue, Pod stays Pending Insufficient free node device.gpustack.ai/rdma* Kueue does not meter network keys; check Node.status.allocatable and active Pod requests, then free endpoints or lower resources.interface. Pod fails placement with TopologyAffinityError Free GPUs and NICs sit on different NUMA sockets Confirm topologyManagerPolicy: restricted in /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml and keep GPU and RDMA requests in the same container. Fewer uverbs devices mounted than rdma.shared count Shared units exceed eligible HCA count Expected round-robin behavior; switch to device.gpustack.ai/rdma (interface > 1) when each unit requires its own physical HCA. Node loses feature.gpustack.ai/rdma.capable Every endpoint on the host is Failed or unbound Check host dmesg and NIC carrier state (NIC record inspection ); Device Manager restores the label automatically once a link recovers. AWS EFA Pod stays Pending Requested device.gpustack.ai/rdma* on EFA host Patch Setting/aws-efa-enabled to "true" for ModelDeployment, or set transport.protocol: EFA on KVCacheBackend. ModelDeployment rejected: no effective RDMA or EFA transfer leg uses the requested interfaces resources.interface set without an active fabric leg Pair managed Prefill and Decode roles behind a router, attach an RDMA/EFA KV cache pool, or remove resources.interface. See also — RDMA Operations (resource keys, selection policies, and EFA setup) · Accelerator Requests (combining accelerator and fabric requests) · Heterogeneous Devices Walkthrough (pool scheduling run)

content:
Hierarchical Placement Walkthrough Publish cloud-zone and rack topology hierarchies, constrain multi-Pod serving replicas to one failure domain, and observe how moving a node between racks differs from changing hierarchy levels.
Contents Summary Zone placement Rack placement Limitations Troubleshooting Summary Topology-aware scheduling (TAS) packs all size Pods of a replica inside one failure domain (such as an availability zone or physical rack). You first discover existing cloud zone labels via a read-only TopologySource, then switch to a versioned ConfigMap rack snapshot and move a node without draining queues:
Object Scope Creator Purpose TopologySource cluster administrator Declares ordered hierarchy levels and where node domain values come from ConfigMap namespace administrator Versioned rack inventory snapshot consumed in Steps 3–5 ModelDeployment namespace user Requests domain packing via roles[].topology.requiredLevel Environment Item Value Cluster Kubernetes with GPUStack installed (illustrative configuration examples) Nodes Worker Nodes carrying topology.kubernetes.io/region and zone in Steps 1–2; ConfigMap snapshot in Steps 3–5 AcceleratorType gpustack--nvidia-a10g-linux-amd64 (substitute an Active pool from kubectl get acctype) Model and engine Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct on vLLM gpustack/runner:cuda13.0-vllm0.29.0 Zone placement Step 1: Discover cloud zones Check existing Node topology labels and confirm no conflicting TopologySource already selects the worker nodes:
bashCopy kubectl get nodes --show-labels kubectl get topologysources kubectl get topologies.kueue.x-k8s.io Save and apply cloud-zones.yaml to build a two-level hierarchy from existing cloud provider labels:
yamlCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: TopologySource metadata: name: cloud-zones spec: nodeSelector: matchLabels: node-role.kubernetes.io/worker: "" levels: - topology.kubernetes.io/region - topology.kubernetes.io/zone nodeLabels: {} bashCopy kubectl apply -f cloud-zones.yaml kubectl get topologysource cloud-zones \ -o jsonpath='{range .status.conditions[*]}{.type}={.status} {.reason}{"\n"}{end}' kubectl get topologies.kueue.x-k8s.io Example output (illustrative):
textCopy Valid=True Valid Ready=True Ready NAME AGE gpustack-fnv64-... 12s The operator verifies that every zone belongs to one region, stamps topology.gpustack.ai/profile=fnv64-<hash> onto matched Nodes, and materializes the Kueue Topology resource. If Ready is False, match the condition reason in Troubleshooting .
Step 2: Request zone placement Constrain a two-Pod (size: 2) serving replica to a single availability zone:
diffCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeployment metadata: name: qwen-distributed namespace: team-a spec: model: name: Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct engine: name: vLLM image: gpustack/runner:cuda13.0-vllm0.29.0 roles: - name: server replicas: 1 size: 2 acceleratorType: gpustack--nvidia-a10g-linux-amd64 resources: accelerator: "1" + topology: + requiredLevel: topology.kubernetes.io/zone Apply the deployment and verify that both member Pods of replica r0 land in the same zone:
bashCopy kubectl -n team-a get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=qwen-distributed \ -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{"\t"}{.spec.nodeName}{"\n"}{end}' | while read -r pod node; do zone=$(kubectl get node "$node" -o jsonpath='{.metadata.labels.topology\.kubernetes\.io/zone}') printf "%s\t%s\t%s\n" "$pod" "$node" "$zone" done If free GPUs are split across zones without two free GPUs in any single zone, Kueue holds the entire replica Pending instead of stranding half-scheduled Pods.
Rack placement Step 3: Publish an inventory snapshot Changing ordered hierarchy levels triggers HoldAndDrain queue migration; review Live hierarchy changes before running this step on shared clusters. Delete cloud-zones first so two sources do not claim the same Nodes:
bashCopy kubectl delete topologysource cloud-zones Save topology-inventory.yaml (replacing worker-a and worker-b with your Node names) to publish a three-level ConfigMap rack snapshot:
yamlCopy apiVersion: v1 kind: ConfigMap metadata: name: topology-inventory namespace: gpustack-system data: snapshot.yaml: | apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1alpha1 kind: TopologySourceConfiguration revision: inventory-42 nodes: worker-a: topology.gpustack.ai/region: region-a topology.gpustack.ai/zone: zone-a topology.gpustack.ai/rack: rack-01 worker-b: topology.gpustack.ai/region: region-a topology.gpustack.ai/zone: zone-a topology.gpustack.ai/rack: rack-02 --- apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: TopologySource metadata: name: data-center spec: nodeSelector: {} levels: - topology.gpustack.ai/region - topology.gpustack.ai/zone - topology.gpustack.ai/rack configMap: configMapRef: namespace: gpustack-system name: topology-inventory key: snapshot.yaml maxStaleness: 10m Apply topology-inventory.yaml and wait until data-center is Ready and queues report TopologyReady=True:
bashCopy kubectl apply -f topology-inventory.yaml kubectl get topologysource data-center \ -o jsonpath='{range .status.conditions[*]}{.type}={.status} {.reason}{"\n"}{end}' kubectl get node worker-a -o jsonpath='{.metadata.labels.topology\.gpustack\.ai/rack}{"\n"}' Example output (illustrative):
textCopy Valid=True Valid Ready=True Ready rack-01 If Valid=False or Ready=False, fix ConfigMap/topology-inventory or TopologySource/data-center rather than editing NFD NodeFeature objects directly; see Verification .
Step 4: Request rack placement Narrow qwen-distributed from zone-level placement to rack-level placement:
diffCopy apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1 kind: ModelDeployment metadata: name: qwen-distributed namespace: team-a spec: roles: - name: server topology: - requiredLevel: topology.kubernetes.io/zone + requiredLevel: topology.gpustack.ai/rack Verify that the rolled replica schedules all size Pods on Nodes sharing one topology.gpustack.ai/rack label (a single rack must hold enough GPUs for the full size).
Step 5: Update rack assignment When worker-b is re-cabled to rack-03, update ConfigMap/topology-inventory and increment revision:
diffCopy apiVersion: v1 kind: ConfigMap metadata: name: topology-inventory namespace: gpustack-system data: snapshot.yaml: | apiVersion: worker.gpustack.ai/v1alpha1 kind: TopologySourceConfiguration - revision: inventory-42 + revision: inventory-43 nodes: worker-a: topology.gpustack.ai/region: region-a topology.gpustack.ai/zone: zone-a topology.gpustack.ai/rack: rack-01 worker-b: topology.gpustack.ai/region: region-a topology.gpustack.ai/zone: zone-a - topology.gpustack.ai/rack: rack-02 + topology.gpustack.ai/rack: rack-03 Confirm that worker-b updates its rack label while keeping the same topology.gpustack.ai/profile hash:
bashCopy kubectl get node worker-b \ -o jsonpath='{.metadata.labels.topology\.gpustack\.ai/rack}{"\t"}{.metadata.labels.topology\.gpustack\.ai/profile}{"\n"}' Because spec.levels did not change, the profile hash stays identical and no HoldAndDrain queue migration occurs. Editing spec.levels changes the profile hash and drains queues; see Live hierarchy changes .
Limitations Each Node must match at most one Ready TopologySource; zero or multiple matches fall back to the hostname-only profile (Topology inventory sources ). Domain capacity fragmentation and multi-role gang holds are covered in Diagnose Pending workloads . Troubleshooting Symptom Signal Resolution TopologySource Ready=False Reason: InvalidHierarchy or SnapshotInvalid A child value maps to multiple parent values, or snapshot YAML is invalid. Fix the ConfigMap snapshot or node labels so levels form a strict tree. TopologySource Ready=False Reason: OwnershipConflict Two writable TopologySources match the same Node. Make their spec.nodeSelector sets disjoint. TopologySource Valid=False Reason: ConfigMapReadFailed Confirm configMapRef.name, namespace, and key exist and are readable by the worker. Node falls back to hostname profile Selected by zero or multiple Ready sources Inspect spec.nodeSelector across kubectl get topologysources -o yaml so exactly one Ready source matches the Node. Multi-role replica reserves one Workload while Pods wait Joint admission gang hold One role fits its domain while a peer role (Prefill or Decode) awaits domain capacity; check Workload conditions across all roles (Diagnose Pending workloads ). See also — Topology (capability overview) · Topology-Aware Scheduling Operations (ConfigMap, Topograph, and Webhook sources) · Configuration (topology.requiredLevel field rules)
